one_liner: Map the "prompt basin" geometry of SAM: for each object, the connected region of click locations that yield the correct mask, and test whether basin area predicts annotation cost.
hypothesis: Prompt-basin area (fraction of in-object clicks producing IoU>0.9 masks) is a stable per-object property that predicts human interactive annotation time better than object size or IoU of the best mask.
min_experiment: Densely sample clicks on ~500 COCO/LVIS instances, compute basin maps, correlate basin area with logged human click counts from an annotation study.
main_risk: Basin area may be confounded with object size and boundary complexity, requiring careful controls.

one_liner: Test whether SAM's point-prompt instability is driven by positional-encoding aliasing rather than semantic ambiguity, by comparing instability maps to the positional encoding's spatial frequency structure.
hypothesis: A significant fraction of mask flips under sub-8-pixel click perturbation aligns with the period of SAM's positional encoding grid, and re-encoding prompts with anti-aliased (low-pass) positional features reduces flips without hurting accuracy.
min_experiment: Sweep clicks on a sub-pixel grid over 200 objects, Fourier-analyze the flip map, then retrain only the prompt encoder with smoothed positional features and re-measure.
main_risk: Flip maps may be dominated by decoder attention effects, making the positional-encoding signal hard to isolate.

one_liner: Formalize and measure "prompt-order sensitivity" in multi-point prompting: whether the sequence in which identical clicks are given changes SAM's final mask, and why.
hypothesis: For a fixed set of k≥3 clicks, permuting click order changes final IoU by >5 points on a non-trivial fraction of objects, and the effect is mediated by the low-resolution mask prior passed between iterations.
min_experiment: For 1,000 objects, sample 10 permutations of 4 fixed clicks, measure IoU spread, then ablate the inter-step mask prior to test mediation.
main_risk: Effect may be small on natural images and only matter in adversarially chosen click sets.

one_liner: Investigate whether box prompts and point prompts activate distinct internal "modes" in SAM's decoder, explaining why box+point combinations sometimes underperform boxes alone.
hypothesis: Box and point prompts drive decoder cross-attention into two separable activation regimes (measurable by linear probes on decoder tokens), and combined prompts land in a low-density interpolation region where accuracy drops.
min_experiment: Collect decoder token activations under box-only, point-only, and mixed prompting on 5k objects; train probes to classify regime; correlate interpolation-region membership with per-object IoU drop.
main_risk: Activation regimes may not be linearly separable, weakening the probing methodology.

one_liner: Quantify "negative-click pathology": the hypothesis that SAM over-erodes masks after background clicks near thin structures, and trace it to the resolution of the mask prior.
hypothesis: The magnitude of over-erosion after a negative click scales with the local thinness of the structure relative to the 256×256 mask-prior resolution, and increasing prior resolution monotonically reduces it.
min_experiment: Build a thin-structure benchmark (DRIVE vessels, wire datasets), apply scripted negative clicks, measure erosion vs. local width, retrain decoder head at 2× prior resolution.
main_risk: Retraining at higher prior resolution may confound capacity with resolution.

one_liner: Test whether SAM's prompt sensitivity is predictable from the image encoder alone, enabling "sensitivity forecasting" before any prompt is given.
hypothesis: A lightweight head on frozen encoder features predicts per-pixel prompt instability (variance of masks under click jitter) with rank correlation >0.6, implying instability is encoded pre-prompt.
min_experiment: Generate instability maps via click jitter on 2k images, train a linear/MLP probe on encoder features to regress them, evaluate on held-out datasets.
main_risk: Instability may depend irreducibly on the prompt itself, capping achievable correlation.

one_liner: Characterize a "semantic granularity prior" in SAM: whether ambiguous clicks default to part, object, or group level in a way that is biased by texture statistics rather than semantics.
hypothesis: SAM's top-ranked mask granularity can be flipped from object to part by texture manipulations (contrast, high-frequency noise) that leave human granularity judgments unchanged.
min_experiment: Construct texture-perturbed versions of 500 part-whole images (e.g., PartImageNet), measure top-mask granularity flips vs. human judgments from a small user study.
main_risk: Texture manipulations may also shift human perception, requiring careful psychophysics controls.

one_liner: Study whether prompt jitter augmentation at fine-tuning time provably trades off peak accuracy for stability, and find the Pareto frontier.
hypothesis: There exists a jitter scale beyond which stability gains saturate while clean-prompt IoU keeps degrading, with the knee at roughly the object's median boundary distance.
min_experiment: Fine-tune SAM decoder with 6 jitter scales on the same data, plot stability (flip rate) vs. clean IoU, verify the knee against per-dataset boundary-distance statistics.
main_risk: The frontier may be dataset-specific, limiting a general law.

one_liner: Test the hypothesis that SAM's text-free prompt space is star-shaped: any correct mask reachable by some click is reachable from the object centroid via iterative refinement.
hypothesis: For >90% of objects, greedy iterative clicking starting at the centroid reaches within 2 IoU points of the best mask found by exhaustive click search, i.e., reachability is centroid-star-shaped.
min_experiment: On 1k objects, run exhaustive first-click search vs. centroid-start greedy refinement (3 rounds), compare best-achievable IoU distributions.
main_risk: "Greedy refinement" definition may drive the result more than model properties.

one_liner: Measure cross-model prompt transferability: whether the click that best segments an object in one SAM variant is also near-optimal in another, isolating whether prompt sensitivity is model-idiosyncratic or image-intrinsic.
hypothesis: Optimal-click transfer between SAM, HQ-SAM, and MobileSAM retains <60% of the achievable IoU gain over centroid clicks, indicating substantial model-idiosyncratic sensitivity.
min_experiment: Grid-search best clicks per object per model on 500 objects; evaluate each model with every other model's best clicks; report transfer matrices.
main_risk: Distilled variants share the teacher's idiosyncrasies, inflating apparent transfer.

one_liner: Investigate whether SAM prompt embeddings can be calibrated per-user: learning a tiny transformation of click embeddings that compensates for individual users' systematic click-placement biases.
hypothesis: A per-user 2-layer MLP on prompt embeddings, trained from <50 correction interactions, reduces that user's clicks-to-target by ≥20% relative to the shared encoder.
min_experiment: Collect click logs from 10 annotators on the same 200 objects, fit per-user prompt MLPs, evaluate held-out clicks-to-90%-IoU.
main_risk: User bias may be too inconsistent within-user for 50 interactions to suffice.

one_liner: Determine whether adversarially fragile prompts (clicks whose tiny perturbation flips the mask) coincide with human-perceived ambiguous regions or form a disjoint, model-specific set.
hypothesis: At least 40% of high-fragility click locations lie in regions humans rate as unambiguous, demonstrating model-specific fragility not explained by task ambiguity.
min_experiment: Compute fragility maps for 300 images; collect human ambiguity annotations on a grid; measure overlap statistics with permutation tests.
main_risk: Human ambiguity ratings are noisy and granularity-dependent.

one_liner: Test whether "prompt dropout" at inference (ensembling masks over random subsets of provided clicks) yields calibrated stability estimates that predict when interactive refinement will fail to converge.
hypothesis: Disagreement among prompt-subset ensembles at round t predicts non-convergence within the next 5 rounds with AUC>0.8, outperforming mask-confidence scores.
min_experiment: Simulate 5k interactive sessions with scripted correction policies, log subset-ensemble disagreement per round, fit and evaluate the convergence predictor.
main_risk: Simulated correction policies may not reflect human oscillation patterns.

one_liner: Characterize how image-space transformations (rotation, scale) commute with prompt-space transformations in SAM, defining an equivariance defect measure for promptable models.
hypothesis: SAM's prompt-conditional equivariance defect grows superlinearly with rotation angle and is dominated by the image encoder (not the prompt path), as isolated by swapping components across rotated/unrotated inputs.
min_experiment: Evaluate mask consistency under 16 rotation angles with correspondingly rotated prompts on 1k objects; ablate by feeding rotated features with unrotated prompts and vice versa.
main_risk: Interpolation artifacts during rotation may inflate the measured defect.

one_liner: Ask whether optimal prompting is learnable as a policy: train a small "prompter" network that places clicks for SAM, and test whether its learned policy generalizes across datasets better than heuristic policies.
hypothesis: A learned prompt-placement policy trained on one dataset outperforms center-of-error heuristics by ≥1 click on average on unseen datasets, indicating dataset-general prompting structure exists.
min_experiment: Train a policy with SAM frozen via REINFORCE/DAgger on COCO; evaluate clicks-to-90%-IoU on ADE20K, DAVIS frames, and medical slices vs. heuristics.
main_risk: Policy may overfit SAM's idiosyncrasies and fail under model updates.

one_liner: Characterize the forgetting curve of SAM2's memory bank: how re-identification accuracy decays with occlusion duration, and whether the decay is exponential (interference) or step-like (slot eviction).
hypothesis: Re-ID accuracy after occlusion follows a step function aligned with memory-slot eviction events rather than smooth decay, implying failures are architectural, not representational.
min_experiment: Construct controlled occlusion videos with parametric occlusion lengths (10–600 frames), measure re-ID success vs. length, and log memory-bank contents to align failures with evictions.
main_risk: Synthetic occlusions may not capture appearance change during real occlusions.

one_liner: Test whether SAM2's memory attention exhibits "identity capture": after a tracking error, the memory bank locks onto the distractor and actively suppresses recovery even when the true object reappears unambiguously.
hypothesis: Surgically deleting post-error memory entries at reappearance time restores correct tracking in >70% of failure cases, demonstrating that stale memories causally block recovery.
min_experiment: Collect 200 organic SAM2 failures on LVOS/long videos, replay each with targeted memory deletion at ground-truth reappearance frames, measure recovery rate.
main_risk: Requires ground-truth reappearance annotations; deletion timing may be a strong oracle.

one_liner: Study whether SAM2's frame-rate sensitivity constitutes a hidden hyperparameter: the same physical video at different fps yields systematically different masklets, violating temporal-sampling invariance.
hypothesis: Downsampling videos from 30 to 6 fps changes J&F by >8 points in a direction predictable from object speed, and simple memory-stride adaptation recovers most of the loss.
min_experiment: Re-time DAVIS/MOSE videos at 5 frame rates, evaluate SAM2 J&F vs. fps stratified by object velocity, test stride-adaptive memory writing.
main_risk: Re-timing artifacts (frame duplication/blur) may confound pure sampling effects.

one_liner: Quantify the interference cost of multi-object tracking in SAM2: whether tracking N objects with separate memory streams degrades each object's accuracy relative to solo tracking, despite nominally independent inference.
hypothesis: Per-object accuracy is statistically indistinguishable between solo and joint tracking, localizing all multi-object failures to prompt assignment rather than interference — or the null is falsified with measurable coupling.
min_experiment: On MOSE, run each annotated object solo and jointly with all others; paired per-object J&F comparison with significance testing.
main_risk: Result may be a boring null; value depends on framing either outcome as informative.

one_liner: Investigate whether SAM2's memory representations drift toward "recency-weighted appearance averages" that fail under cyclic appearance change (e.g., rotating objects), and whether phase-aware memory sampling fixes it.
hypothesis: Tracking error on periodic-appearance objects concentrates at phase points furthest from recently stored appearances, and uniform-phase memory sampling reduces those errors by ≥30%.
min_experiment: Build/collect turntable-style and gait videos with phase labels, correlate per-frame error with phase distance to memory contents, then swap eviction policy.
main_risk: Phase labeling of in-the-wild videos is hard; may need synthetic rendering.

one_liner: Test whether SAM2 can be prompted "in the past": propagating a late-video correction backwards through the memory mechanism, and characterizing the asymmetry between forward and backward propagation quality.
hypothesis: Backward propagation (reversed replay) recovers ≥90% of forward-propagation quality on reversible motion but <60% on articulated motion, quantifying a directional bias in learned memory.
min_experiment: On DAVIS, prompt at last frame and track on reversed video vs. prompt at first frame on forward video; stratify the gap by motion type.
main_risk: Reversed videos violate physics (e.g., gravity), confounding the asymmetry source.

one_liner: Determine whether SAM2's occlusion head produces calibrated occlusion probabilities, and whether miscalibration is the direct cause of premature track termination.
hypothesis: SAM2's occlusion scores are overconfident near partial occlusion (ECE>0.15 in the 30–70% occluded regime), and isotonic recalibration alone reduces wrong terminations by ≥25% without touching mask quality.
min_experiment: Extract occlusion scores on MOSE with ground-truth visibility, compute reliability diagrams, apply isotonic regression, re-run tracking with recalibrated thresholds.
main_risk: Ground-truth partial-occlusion percentages are scarce; may need synthetic composites.

one_liner: Study "memory poisoning" robustness: whether a few adversarially or naturally corrupted frames written into SAM2's memory disproportionately corrupt future predictions, and derive a write-gate criterion.
hypothesis: A single low-quality memory write during motion blur degrades subsequent-frame IoU superlinearly relative to skipping the write, and a quality-gated write policy (predicted-IoU threshold) recovers most losses.
min_experiment: Inject controlled blur/compression into single frames, compare downstream error with forced vs. gated writes across corruption severities.
main_risk: Gating may starve memory during genuinely hard sequences, hurting long-term recall.

one_liner: Ask whether SAM2's memory bank encodes identity or merely appearance, using twin-object videos (identical instances) to test if the model can maintain identity through crossovers without appearance cues.
hypothesis: SAM2's crossover identity accuracy on identical twins is near chance (≤60%), showing its memory is appearance-based with no motion-continuity integration.
min_experiment: Render synthetic twin-object crossing videos with controlled kinematics; measure post-crossing identity retention vs. crossing angle and speed.
main_risk: Synthetic-to-real gap; results may not predict real-world identity errors.

one_liner: Measure whether long-video error accumulation in SAM2 is dominated by rare catastrophic re-anchoring events rather than gradual drift, using changepoint analysis on per-frame IoU trajectories.
hypothesis: >70% of total IoU loss on 5-minute videos occurs within <5% of frames (catastrophic events), implying event prevention beats drift correction as a research target.
min_experiment: Run SAM2 on LVOS/long videos, compute per-frame IoU, apply changepoint detection, report error-mass concentration statistics and event triggers.
main_risk: Ground-truth density on long videos is sparse, complicating per-frame IoU estimation.

one_liner: Test a "memory rehearsal" inference scheme: periodically re-encoding the first-frame prompt features into memory to prevent representation drift, framed as testing whether anchor rehearsal beats recency in memory-based video models.
hypothesis: Pinning the initial conditioning frame permanently in memory improves long-video J&F by ≥5 points on videos with appearance drift while never hurting short videos by more than 1 point.
min_experiment: Modify memory eviction to always retain frame-0 entries; A/B on LVOS vs. DAVIS; stratify by video length and drift magnitude.
main_risk: Stale anchors may harm objects with legitimate large appearance change.

one_liner: Investigate whether SAM2 masklet quality can be predicted online from memory-attention entropy, giving a streaming self-diagnosis signal without ground truth.
hypothesis: Entropy of memory cross-attention distributions predicts per-frame IoU drops 5–10 frames before they occur, with earlier warning than the predicted-IoU head.
min_experiment: Log attention entropy and predicted IoU across MOSE runs, fit lagged predictors of true IoU collapse, compare lead times.
main_risk: Entropy may correlate with scene clutter generally, yielding many false alarms.

one_liner: Quantify how SAM2 handles topology changes (object splitting/merging, e.g., pouring liquids, dividing cells) and whether failures stem from the single-masklet assumption rather than perception.
hypothesis: At split events, SAM2 follows the fragment with higher feature similarity to memory and irreversibly drops the other, in >80% of cases, regardless of fragment size — a deterministic architectural bias.
min_experiment: Curate cell-division and object-splitting clips, annotate both fragments, measure which fragment SAM2 follows vs. feature-similarity and size predictors.
main_risk: Defining "correct" behavior at splits is task-dependent, complicating evaluation.

one_liner: Test whether streaming compute budgets change SAM2's error profile qualitatively: under frame dropping (real-time constraint), do errors shift from boundary noise to identity loss, implying different mitigation than offline settings?
hypothesis: Under 50% random frame drops, boundary-quality metrics degrade <10% while identity/re-ID errors more than double, showing memory (not perception) is the real-time bottleneck.
min_experiment: Simulate frame-drop patterns (random, bursty) on DAVIS/MOSE, decompose J&F changes into boundary vs. identity components.
main_risk: Metric decomposition into "identity vs boundary" requires careful, defensible definitions.

one_liner: Ask whether SAM2's video pretraining damaged its still-image ability relative to SAM1 in specific regimes (fine boundaries, dense scenes), constituting measurable negative transfer from temporal objectives.
hypothesis: SAM2 underperforms SAM1 on high-frequency-boundary objects and dense small-object scenes by a statistically significant margin, and the gap correlates with memory-module-induced feature smoothing.
min_experiment: Evaluate both models on identical still-image suites stratified by boundary frequency, object density, and size; test correlation of gaps with feature spectral content.
main_risk: Architecture and training-data differences confound the "temporal objective" attribution.

one_liner: Characterize the "concept granularity gap" in SAM3-style promptable concept segmentation: whether short noun-phrase prompts systematically fail on concepts defined by relations ("the cup on the left") versus attributes ("the red cup").
hypothesis: Recall on relation-defined targets is at least 30 points lower than on attribute-defined targets with matched visual difficulty, indicating relational grounding is the binding failure, not vocabulary.
min_experiment: Build matched prompt pairs (attribute vs. relation for the same target) on 1k images; measure recall/precision gap with visual difficulty controlled by target size and contrast.
main_risk: Constructing genuinely matched-difficulty pairs is subtle and may leak confounds.

one_liner: Test whether concept-promptable segmenters exhibit "exhaustivity failure": when asked for all instances of a concept, misses are not random but concentrated on instances far from the concept's visual prototype.
hypothesis: Missed instances are systematically farther from the class mean in the model's own embedding space than found instances (effect size d>0.8), making misses predictable a priori.
min_experiment: Run concept prompts on LVIS-style exhaustively annotated images, embed all GT instances, compare embedding distances of hits vs. misses.
main_risk: Embedding distance may proxy for size/occlusion, requiring multivariate controls.

one_liner: Study prompt-phrasing sensitivity for concept segmentation: whether synonymous phrasings ("dog" vs. "canine" vs. "a dog") produce different instance sets, and quantify a phrasing-invariance score.
hypothesis: Synonym substitution alone changes the returned instance set (symmetric difference) by >15% on average, and the variation is larger for rare concepts, falsifying phrasing invariance.
min_experiment: Curate 100 concepts × 5 phrasings, run on a fixed image corpus, compute pairwise instance-set Jaccard and stratify by concept frequency.
main_risk: Some "synonyms" carry real semantic differences, requiring careful linguistic vetting.

one_liner: Investigate negative-concept prompting: whether models can segment "all animals except dogs," and if failures reveal that concept prompts are implemented as similarity thresholds without set operations.
hypothesis: Performance on exclusion queries is no better than applying the positive query and randomly removing instances, demonstrating absence of compositional negation in current concept heads.
min_experiment: Construct 200 exclusion queries with ground truth on densely annotated images; compare against positive-query-plus-oracle-subtraction and random-subtraction baselines.
main_risk: Prompt formatting choices could dominate results; needs multiple phrasing templates.

one_liner: Test whether image exemplar prompts and text prompts for the same concept retrieve systematically different instance distributions, quantifying a cross-modal prompt gap within one model.
hypothesis: Exemplar prompts bias retrieval toward the exemplar's pose/context (measurable as reduced intra-retrieved-set diversity vs. text prompts) even when both achieve similar precision.
min_experiment: For 50 concepts, prompt via text and via 5 random exemplars each; compare retrieved-set diversity (pose/scale/context statistics) and overlap.
main_risk: Diversity metrics on retrieved sets are themselves contestable.

one_liner: Measure "hard-negative hallucination" in concept segmentation: the rate at which visually similar but categorically wrong objects are returned, as a function of the semantic distance of the nearest confusable category present.
hypothesis: False-positive rate is predicted by the presence of a taxonomic sibling in the image (odds ratio >3), and no current confidence signal separates sibling confusions from correct detections.
min_experiment: Assemble images containing sibling pairs (from a taxonomy), run single-concept prompts, quantify FP odds ratios and confidence overlap distributions.
main_risk: Requires reliable taxonomies; visual similarity may not track taxonomy.

one_liner: Ask whether concept segmenters internally decide instance count before segmenting (top-down) or segment then group (bottom-up), by probing intermediate representations for count information at different depths.
hypothesis: Count information is linearly decodable from mid-level representations before instance masks are resolved, and ablating it degrades exhaustivity specifically in crowded scenes.
min_experiment: Train linear probes for instance count at each transformer block on crowded images; causally patch count-carrying activations and observe exhaustivity changes.
main_risk: Linear decodability does not establish causal use; patching experiments are delicate.

one_liner: Test the temporal stability of concept prompts in video: whether a concept prompt applied per-frame yields flickering instance sets, and whether the flicker is attributable to threshold effects near the decision boundary.
hypothesis: >50% of instance flicker events involve match scores within a narrow band around the acceptance threshold, so score-hysteresis eliminates most flicker without new training.
min_experiment: Run concept prompts per-frame on videos with stable GT, log score trajectories of flickering instances, test hysteresis and temporal smoothing at the score level.
main_risk: Some flicker may come from encoder feature instability, not thresholds.

one_liner: Characterize how concept segmentation degrades under domain shift differently for the recognition pathway vs. the mask pathway, using domain pairs where one pathway is stressed at a time.
hypothesis: Under style shift (photo→sketch), recognition recall collapses while conditional mask quality (given correct recognition) stays within 5 points, indicating the pathways fail independently.
min_experiment: Evaluate on photo/sketch/clipart versions of matched scenes; report recognition recall and recognition-conditioned mask IoU separately.
main_risk: Truly matched cross-style scenes are scarce; may require rendered data.

one_liner: Study prompt-set interference: whether asking a concept segmenter for multiple concepts simultaneously changes the results for each concept relative to querying them one at a time.
hypothesis: Joint querying reduces per-concept recall for semantically close concepts sharing visual features, with interference proportional to embedding similarity of the queried concepts.
min_experiment: Query 100 concept pairs jointly and separately on the same corpus; regress recall deltas on inter-concept embedding similarity.
main_risk: Implementation details of batching may differ across systems, limiting generality.

one_liner: Test whether concept segmenters can abstain: measuring behavior when prompted with concepts absent from the image, and whether "absence competence" is independent of presence accuracy.
hypothesis: False-positive rates on absent-concept prompts are uncorrelated (r<0.2) with present-concept accuracy across concepts, revealing absence handling as a separate, unoptimized capability.
min_experiment: For 200 concepts, query images with verified absence; compute per-concept FP rates; correlate with standard AP on present cases.
main_risk: Verifying true absence requires exhaustive annotation, which is expensive.

one_liner: Investigate whether fine-grained concept boundaries ("mug" vs. "cup") in segmentation models match human category boundaries, using morphed/ambiguous objects as the probe set.
hypothesis: Model category boundaries on a morph continuum are systematically shifted toward the more frequent training concept, misaligning with the human 50% point by a measurable offset.
min_experiment: Generate 3D-rendered morph continua between confusable categories, query both concepts, compare model crossover point to crowdsourced human judgments.
main_risk: Rendered morphs may sit off-distribution for the model, distorting boundaries.

one_liner: Quantify the "vocabulary tail cliff": whether concept-segmentation quality decays smoothly or cliff-drops with decreasing concept frequency in pretraining-scale text corpora, using corpus frequency as the sole predictor.
hypothesis: There is a frequency threshold below which recall collapses discontinuously (cliff), rather than smooth log-linear decay, and the cliff location is stable across image domains.
min_experiment: Sample 500 concepts across 6 frequency decades, evaluate recall on a held-out annotated corpus, fit piecewise vs. smooth decay models and compare.
main_risk: Frequency estimates from public corpora may mismatch the actual pretraining data.

one_liner: Test whether concept segmenters leak instance masks across prompt semantics: prompting "shadow" or "reflection" of an object to probe whether the model represents non-material visual entities as segmentable concepts.
hypothesis: Models segment reflections as object instances at high rates when prompted with the object noun (not the word "reflection"), inflating false positives in reflective scenes by a measurable factor.
min_experiment: Curate mirror/water/glass scenes with annotated reflections; measure object-prompt hits on reflections vs. shadow controls; test "reflection of X" prompts.
main_risk: Annotation of reflection extents is genuinely ambiguous.

one_liner: Study whether interactive concept refinement (adding positive/negative exemplars) converges to the intended concept or oscillates, formalizing concept-refinement dynamics as a fixed-point problem.
hypothesis: Refinement is non-monotonic in ≥30% of sessions (adding a correct exemplar reduces F1), driven by exemplar-embedding averaging that shifts the decision boundary in unintended directions.
min_experiment: Simulate refinement sessions with oracle exemplar selection on 100 concepts; track F1 trajectories; identify oscillation conditions as a function of concept variance.
main_risk: Results depend on the specific exemplar-aggregation mechanism, limiting cross-model generality.

one_liner: Decompose MedSAM's improvement over SAM into intensity-statistics adaptation vs. anatomical-shape learning, by evaluating on intensity-remapped natural images and shape-preserved synthetic medical images.
hypothesis: Most of MedSAM's gain transfers to intensity-remapped natural objects (statistics), with anatomy-specific gains confined to organs with strong shape regularity.
min_experiment: Construct (a) natural images remapped to CT-like histograms and (b) synthetic phantoms with organ shapes but natural textures; compare SAM-vs-MedSAM deltas on each.
main_risk: Synthetic constructs may not cleanly isolate the two factors.

one_liner: Test whether MedSAM's box-prompt dependence hides an inability to reject wrong boxes: measuring segmentation behavior when boxes are misplaced on healthy tissue or wrong organs.
hypothesis: MedSAM segments a plausible-looking structure inside a wrong box in >80% of cases with high confidence, i.e., it lacks box-rejection capability entirely, and this rate is unaffected by fine-tuning data volume.
min_experiment: Systematically displace ground-truth boxes onto adjacent anatomy in CT/MR sets, record mask confidence and plausibility ratings from radiologists on a sample.
main_risk: "Plausible-looking" needs expert evaluation, which is costly.

one_liner: Investigate slice-wise inconsistency in 2D MedSAM applied to 3D volumes as a diagnostic signal: whether inter-slice mask incoherence predicts volumetric segmentation error better than per-slice confidence.
hypothesis: An inter-slice coherence statistic (e.g., Dice between adjacent slice masks adjusted for anatomy) predicts volumetric Dice with r>0.7, enabling label-free quality control.
min_experiment: Segment 200 CT volumes slice-wise, compute coherence statistics, correlate with GT volumetric Dice, compare against confidence-based QC.
main_risk: Coherence may fail for genuinely irregular pathologies (infiltrative tumors).

one_liner: Test whether medical fine-tuning of SAM redistributes errors from over-segmentation to under-segmentation in a clinically asymmetric way, and whether the direction is controllable at fine-tuning time.
hypothesis: Standard MedSAM fine-tuning systematically shifts boundary bias inward (under-segmentation of lesions), and a boundary-asymmetric loss weighting can set the bias direction without losing overall Dice.
min_experiment: Measure signed boundary error distributions of SAM vs. MedSAM on lesion datasets; retrain with asymmetric losses at 3 settings; verify controllability.
main_risk: Signed boundary error is sensitive to annotation-style bias in ground truth.

one_liner: Quantify "scanner fingerprint sensitivity": whether MedSAM performance varies more across scanner manufacturers than across patients, using multi-site datasets with crossed factors.
hypothesis: Scanner identity explains more variance in MedSAM Dice than patient-level anatomy variation for at least some organs, and the scanner effect is concentrated in encoder early layers.
min_experiment: Fit mixed-effects models of Dice on multi-site CT/MR (scanner, site, patient factors); probe early-layer feature shifts across scanners.
main_risk: Public multi-site data may confound scanner with population.

one_liner: Study whether MedSAM inherits and amplifies annotation-style artifacts from its fine-tuning corpus: e.g., systematically reproducing the margin conventions of the dominant annotating institution.
hypothesis: MedSAM's boundary placement on held-out data matches the majority training institution's style more than the test institution's own style, measurable via style-classifier probes on boundary geometry.
min_experiment: Train a boundary-style classifier distinguishing institutions on GT; apply to MedSAM outputs on cross-institution test sets; quantify style attribution.
main_risk: Requires datasets with known institutional provenance.

one_liner: Test few-shot modality onboarding: how many labeled cases from a truly novel modality (e.g., photoacoustic imaging) are needed for PEFT-adapted MedSAM to match a from-scratch U-Net, mapping the crossover curve.
hypothesis: The PEFT-vs-scratch crossover occurs below 50 labeled volumes for structurally familiar anatomy but above 500 for novel contrast mechanisms, showing the prior is anatomical rather than physical.
min_experiment: On 2 rare modalities, sweep training-set size for LoRA-MedSAM vs. nnU-Net-style baseline; locate crossover points per anatomy.
main_risk: Access to rare-modality data with quality labels.

one_liner: Investigate whether pathology (tumors, anomalies) breaks MedSAM's shape priors constructively or destructively: does the model fall back to image evidence or hallucinate healthy anatomy?
hypothesis: On organs with resections/anomalies, MedSAM's masks are biased toward the healthy-population shape atlas (measurable as reduced Dice specifically in the anomalous region), evidencing prior-driven hallucination.
min_experiment: Evaluate on post-surgical/anomalous organ datasets; decompose error into anomalous-region vs. typical-region components; compare against a no-shape-prior baseline.
main_risk: Anomalous-region localization requires extra annotation effort.

one_liner: Ask whether prompt semantics differ across medical and natural domains: a box in natural images means "the object," but in medicine may mean "region of interest including context" — and whether models internalize this pragmatic difference.
hypothesis: MedSAM interprets loose boxes as "segment the central organ" while SAM interprets them as "segment the largest salient object," and this pragmatic divergence is measurable by varying box looseness on matched cases.
min_experiment: Sweep box looseness (1.0×–3.0× GT) on natural and medical images for SAM/MedSAM; characterize the target-selection function of each model.
main_risk: Findings may reflect dataset box-style statistics rather than deep pragmatics.

one_liner: Quantify the interaction between windowing (CT display transforms) and MedSAM performance: whether the model has an implicit preferred windowing and how much performance is lost by feeding raw or wrongly windowed inputs.
hypothesis: MedSAM has a narrow effective windowing basin (performance drops >10 Dice outside it), and a learned per-case windowing predictor recovers the loss, indicating windowing should be model-internal.
min_experiment: Evaluate MedSAM over a windowing grid on abdominal CT; fit sensitivity surfaces per organ; train a tiny windowing regressor and re-evaluate.
main_risk: Optimal windowing may differ per organ within one scan, complicating a single-input pipeline.

one_liner: Test cross-anatomy prompt interference in a single fine-tuned model: whether adding fine-tuning data for new organs degrades boundary conventions on previously mastered organs even when overall Dice holds.
hypothesis: After adding organ-B data, organ-A Dice is stable but organ-A boundary-distance distributions shift measurably toward organ-B's annotation conventions — convention-level forgetting invisible to Dice.
min_experiment: Sequentially fine-tune on organ datasets with distinct margin conventions; track boundary-signed-error distributions per organ across stages.
main_risk: Convention differences across datasets may be too small to detect reliably.

one_liner: Study whether uncertainty maps from medical promptable models align with inter-radiologist disagreement regions, testing the claim that model uncertainty can substitute for multi-reader variability estimates.
hypothesis: Pixelwise correlation between MedSAM ensemble uncertainty and inter-reader disagreement is moderate on smooth organs but near zero on pathology boundaries — exactly where it is needed.
min_experiment: Use multi-reader datasets (e.g., prostate/lung), compute model uncertainty via prompt+dropout ensembles, correlate with reader variance maps stratified by tissue type.
main_risk: Few public multi-reader datasets; disagreement conflates style and true ambiguity.

one_liner: Investigate resolution-anisotropy failure: whether MedSAM errors on anisotropic volumes (thick slices) are dominated by the encoder's isotropy assumption and fixable by anisotropy-conditioned positional rescaling at inference.
hypothesis: Performance on sagittal/coronal reformats degrades proportionally to anisotropy ratio, and rescaling positional embeddings by the acquisition spacing recovers ≥50% of the loss without retraining.
min_experiment: Evaluate on reformatted views across anisotropy ratios; apply spacing-aware positional rescaling; measure recovery per organ.
main_risk: Positional rescaling may interact badly with pretrained attention patterns.

one_liner: Test whether MedSAM's failures on small lesions are detection failures or segmentation failures, by decoupling with oracle prompts: perfect boxes on lesions the model would otherwise miss.
hypothesis: With oracle boxes, small-lesion Dice recovers to within 10 points of large-lesion Dice, localizing the deficit almost entirely to the prompting/detection stage rather than mask decoding.
min_experiment: On lesion datasets stratified by diameter, compare automatic-prompt vs. oracle-box Dice; report the recoverable fraction per size bin.
main_risk: Oracle boxes may leak size information that inflates apparent decoder competence.

one_liner: Examine whether federating PEFT adapters across hospitals (adapter averaging vs. routing) preserves site-specific calibration while sharing anatomical knowledge, formalized as a modularity test of medical adaptation.
hypothesis: Averaged adapters transfer anatomy gains across sites but degrade per-site calibration, whereas a two-component decomposition (shared + site-specific low-rank parts) preserves both, demonstrating separability of knowledge types in adapter space.
min_experiment: Train LoRA adapters at 4+ simulated "sites" (public datasets), compare averaging vs. shared+specific decomposition on cross-site Dice and per-site ECE.
main_risk: Public datasets may under-represent true inter-hospital variation.

one_liner: Test whether SAM-family boundary errors are spectrally band-limited: errors concentrate in boundary curvature frequencies above a cutoff set by the mask decoder's upsampling path, defining a "boundary Nyquist limit" for promptable models.
hypothesis: Contour error energy is negligible below a model-specific curvature frequency and near-total above it, with the cutoff predictable from decoder feature-map resolution.
min_experiment: Compute contour Fourier descriptors of GT vs. predicted masks across models with different decoder resolutions; locate error cutoffs; test predictability from architecture.
main_risk: Natural object contours may lack sufficient high-frequency content to identify cutoffs precisely.

one_liner: Investigate whether high-quality boundary heads (HQ-SAM style) improve real boundary accuracy or mostly improve boundary "confidence sharpness" that games boundary metrics against soft ground truth.
hypothesis: A significant fraction of HQ-style metric gains disappears when evaluated against multi-annotator soft boundaries instead of single-annotator hard boundaries.
min_experiment: Collect 5-annotator boundaries on 300 objects; recompute boundary F-scores for SAM vs. HQ-SAM against soft references; compare gain shrinkage.
main_risk: Multi-annotator collection cost; annotator instructions may bias softness.

one_liner: Characterize the "boundary attachment hierarchy" of segmentation foundation models: when true boundaries are weak, which image cues (color edges, texture edges, depth discontinuities) the predicted boundary snaps to, in what priority order.
hypothesis: SAM-family models have a stable cue hierarchy (luminance edge > texture boundary > semantic boundary) that mispredicts human boundary placement in camouflage and low-contrast regimes in a systematic, correctable direction.
min_experiment: Render cue-conflict stimuli (color edge displaced from texture edge from GT boundary); measure attachment rates per cue across displacement magnitudes.
main_risk: Synthetic cue-conflict stimuli may be off-distribution.

one_liner: Test whether boundary quality and region quality are represented by separable subspaces in SAM's decoder, such that PEFT restricted to the boundary subspace improves contours without touching region behavior.
hypothesis: There exists a low-dimensional decoder weight subspace whose perturbation changes boundary F-score with near-zero effect on region IoU, demonstrable via subspace-constrained fine-tuning.
min_experiment: Fine-tune with projection onto candidate subspaces (from gradient PCA of boundary-only vs. region-only losses); measure the boundary/region change ratio.
main_risk: Subspaces may be input-dependent, defeating a global decomposition.

one_liner: Quantify boundary error as a function of annotation-tool provenance in training data: whether polygon-annotated training masks cause vertex-like straight-line artifacts in model boundary predictions.
hypothesis: Models trained on polygon-heavy data produce measurably straighter boundary segments (lower curvature entropy) than the true object statistics, and the artifact strength tracks the training-tool mixture.
min_experiment: Compare curvature statistics of predictions from models trained on polygon vs. matting-quality masks on identical test sets; correlate with training-source composition.
main_risk: Confounded by dataset content differences beyond tool type.

one_liner: Study occlusion-boundary vs. object-boundary confusion: whether segmentation models place boundaries at self-occlusion contours inside objects, and if this error is predictable from local depth-gradient magnitude.
hypothesis: Internal-boundary insertion probability scales with the strength of internal depth discontinuity, showing models use depth-edge proxies rather than object-level continuity.
min_experiment: Use datasets with depth (or estimated depth); detect internal-cut errors; regress error probability on internal depth-gradient statistics.
main_risk: Estimated depth introduces its own model biases into the analysis.

one_liner: Test a "boundary consistency under prompt ensembles" measure: whether averaging masks from multiple prompts sharpens or blurs boundaries, resolving when ensembling helps boundary quality.
hypothesis: Prompt ensembling improves boundary F-score only when individual-mask boundary errors are unbiased (zero-mean); under biased errors (consistent over/under-shoot) it entrenches the bias, and the regime is predictable per object.
min_experiment: For 1k objects, decompose boundary error into bias/variance across 10 prompts; verify ensemble gain aligns with the variance-dominant regime.
main_risk: Decomposition requires accurate GT boundaries at pixel level.

one_liner: Investigate whether transparent and translucent object boundaries expose a fundamental limitation of binary mask supervision: models trained with hard masks cannot represent partial coverage, and where they place the hard boundary is arbitrary.
hypothesis: On translucent regions, boundary placement variance across prompts is an order of magnitude higher than on opaque regions, and predicted logits in these regions carry recoverable alpha-matte information despite binary training.
min_experiment: Evaluate SAM logits against alpha mattes on translucency datasets; measure rank correlation between logits and true alpha in soft regions.
main_risk: Logit-alpha correlation may reflect trivial distance-to-boundary effects.

one_liner: Formalize "boundary drift under iterative refinement": whether repeated interactive corrections asymptotically converge to GT boundaries or to a model-specific attractor contour offset from GT.
hypothesis: For each object there exists an attractor contour differing from GT by a systematic offset (dependent on local contrast), and no click sequence can reduce error below this floor.
min_experiment: Run exhaustive refinement (50+ oracle clicks) on 300 objects; measure asymptotic residual error and its correlation with local image statistics.
main_risk: Oracle-click policies may not explore the reachable set fully.

one_liner: Test whether boundary quality transfers across scale: models fine-tuned to sharpen boundaries at one object scale may not transfer sharpening to other scales, revealing scale-specific boundary circuits.
hypothesis: Boundary-F gains from fine-tuning on large objects transfer <30% to small objects (and vice versa), indicating scale-indexed rather than scale-invariant boundary processing.
min_experiment: Fine-tune on size-restricted subsets (small-only, large-only); evaluate boundary metrics across the full size spectrum; compute transfer matrices.
main_risk: Size subsets differ in content, confounding scale with category.

one_liner: Examine whether the standard mask upsampling path (transposed conv/interpolation) imposes an anisotropic boundary error: axis-aligned boundaries reconstructed better than diagonal ones.
hypothesis: Boundary error as a function of local contour orientation shows 4-fold periodicity (worst at 45°), with amplitude determined by the upsampling method, and orientation-aware upsampling removes it.
min_experiment: Bin boundary errors by local GT contour orientation across datasets and models; compare amplitude across upsampler variants retrained identically.
main_risk: Natural-image orientation statistics may mask the effect; may need rotated evaluation.

one_liner: Ask whether models can predict their own boundary error field: an auxiliary head trained to output per-boundary-pixel expected displacement, tested for calibration and downstream utility in weighted fusion.
hypothesis: Expected boundary displacement is learnable to within 30% relative error and enables error-weighted mask fusion that beats uniform fusion on boundary F by a significant margin.
min_experiment: Train displacement head on existing datasets' residuals; evaluate calibration curves; test fusion utility on multi-prompt outputs.
main_risk: Residual fields may be too stochastic to learn beyond trivial contrast correlates.

one_liner: Study "semantic boundary leakage": whether boundaries between two touching objects of the same class are systematically worse than object-background boundaries at matched contrast, isolating instance-separation as a distinct boundary competence.
hypothesis: At matched local contrast, instance-instance boundary F is ≥20 points below instance-background F, and the gap survives boundary-focused fine-tuning, indicating a representational (not resolution) limit.
min_experiment: Classify each GT boundary pixel by type; compute type-conditional boundary metrics matched on local contrast; test persistence after HQ fine-tuning.
main_risk: Contrast matching across boundary types reduces usable data substantially.

one_liner: Test whether logit-space boundary refinement (deconvolving the decoder's learned blur) can recover boundary detail without any retraining, treating the decoder as a known degradation operator.
hypothesis: The decoder's boundary point-spread function is approximately input-independent, and Wiener-style deconvolution of mask logits improves boundary F on high-res GT without harming region IoU.
min_experiment: Estimate the effective PSF from step-edge synthetic inputs; apply deconvolution to logits on real data; measure boundary/region metric changes.
main_risk: The effective blur is likely input-dependent and nonlinear, breaking the deconvolution model.

one_liner: Investigate human perceptual thresholds for boundary error in applied contexts: below what boundary F improvement do downstream human users (editors, clinicians) stop noticing differences, calibrating "sufficient" boundary quality per application.
hypothesis: Perceptual indifference thresholds vary by an order of magnitude across applications (photo editing vs. radiotherapy), and current SOTA already exceeds the threshold for several applications while falling far short for others.
min_experiment: Two-alternative forced-choice studies with domain users comparing mask pairs at controlled boundary-F deltas across 3 application framings.
main_risk: User studies are expensive and threshold estimates may be task-framing sensitive.

one_liner: Characterize what is lost first in SAM distillation: rank-order the degradation of capabilities (boundary detail, ambiguity handling, rare-category grounding, prompt robustness) as student capacity shrinks.
hypothesis: Capabilities degrade in a consistent order across distillation methods (ambiguity handling first, boundary detail last), implying capability-specific capacity thresholds rather than uniform degradation.
min_experiment: Distill students at 5 capacity points; evaluate a battery isolating each capability; test order consistency across two distillation losses.
main_risk: Capability batteries may not cleanly isolate single capabilities.

one_liner: Test whether encoder-only distillation (MobileSAM style) creates a student-decoder mismatch: the frozen decoder receives slightly off-manifold features, causing errors that joint fine-tuning would fix at negligible cost.
hypothesis: Student encoder features lie measurably off the teacher feature manifold on out-of-distribution images (higher reconstruction error under a teacher-feature autoencoder), and decoder errors concentrate exactly where manifold deviation is largest.
min_experiment: Fit a density/AE model to teacher features; correlate student deviation with per-image IoU drop; test 1-epoch decoder adaptation.
main_risk: Manifold estimates in high dimensions are fragile.

one_liner: Study whether distillation transfers the teacher's prompt sensitivity or filters it: do students inherit the teacher's click-fragility maps, or develop their own?
hypothesis: Student fragility maps correlate with the teacher's (r>0.5) far more than architecture-matched independently trained models (r<0.2), demonstrating pathology inheritance through the distillation signal.
min_experiment: Compute click-fragility maps for teacher, distilled students, and independently trained controls on shared images; compare correlation structure.
main_risk: Shared training data alone may explain fragility correlation.

one_liner: Investigate quantization's disparate impact on segmentation: whether INT8/INT4 quantization degrades boundary pixels disproportionately relative to interior pixels, and which layers cause it.
hypothesis: Quantization error concentrates on boundary logits (where activations are near decision thresholds), with the final decoder layers contributing most, so mixed-precision on <10% of layers recovers most boundary loss.
min_experiment: Quantize progressively; map per-pixel logit perturbation vs. distance-to-boundary; layer-wise sensitivity scan; test targeted mixed precision.
main_risk: Effects may be hardware/kernel-specific, reducing generality.

one_liner: Test the "resolution honesty" of efficient SAM variants: whether claimed support for high-res inputs actually improves effective output resolution, measured by the smallest resolvable structure rather than input pixel count.
hypothesis: Effective resolution (minimum resolvable gap/protrusion size, measured psychophysics-style with synthetic targets) saturates well below input resolution for most efficient variants, and the saturation point predicts real-data small-structure performance.
min_experiment: Synthetic charts with parametric gaps/protrusions; find detection thresholds per model; validate against thin-structure benchmarks.
main_risk: Synthetic thresholds may not transfer to cluttered natural scenes.

one_liner: Ask whether distillation data composition matters more than method: a factorial study crossing distillation objectives with data mixtures to attribute student quality variance.
hypothesis: Data-mixture factors explain more student-performance variance than objective factors for promptable segmentation, especially in tail categories.
min_experiment: 3 objectives × 4 data mixtures, same student architecture and budget; variance decomposition of downstream metrics.
main_risk: Compute cost of the factorial grid; interactions may dominate main effects.

one_liner: Study latency-accuracy scheduling within a single model: whether early-exit mask decoding (emitting masks from intermediate decoder states) provides usable anytime segmentation, and where quality jumps occur.
hypothesis: Intermediate decoder states yield monotonically improving masks with a large quality jump at a specific stage (hypothesized: after the second token-to-image attention), making one natural early-exit point nearly free.
min_experiment: Instrument decoder to emit masks per stage; measure quality-vs-stage curves across datasets; identify jump structure.
main_risk: Intermediate states may need a trained readout head, adding confound.

one_liner: Test whether small students benefit from "uncertainty-matched" distillation: matching the teacher's output distribution (including its ambiguity structure) rather than its argmax masks.
hypothesis: Students distilled to match the teacher's multimask output distribution (all mask hypotheses + scores) preserve ambiguity handling at small capacity better than argmax distillation, at equal aggregate IoU.
min_experiment: Distill with argmax vs. full-hypothesis matching; evaluate on ambiguity benchmarks (part/whole clicks) and standard suites.
main_risk: Hypothesis-matching losses may be unstable to optimize.

one_liner: Investigate whether efficient attention approximations (linear attention, pooling) in mobile variants specifically damage long-range mask coherence — the ability to include distant disconnected parts of one object.
hypothesis: Mask fragmentation rate on spatially extended objects (e.g., fences, wires, occluded objects in two pieces) increases superlinearly as attention range shrinks, while compact-object metrics stay flat — a hidden failure invisible in standard benchmarks.
min_experiment: Evaluate attention variants on an extent-stratified benchmark; measure fragmentation (connected-component errors) vs. object spatial extent.
main_risk: Extent-stratified data with disconnected GT objects is scarce; may need curation.

one_liner: Test cascaded deployment honesty: whether a small model + selective escalation to the large model (based on the small model's self-assessment) actually beats the large model alone on cost-quality curves, or whether self-assessment failures cluster exactly on escalation-worthy cases.
hypothesis: Small-model confidence is anticorrelated with escalation need on the most severe failures (confidently wrong), capping cascade performance well below oracle escalation, and an external lightweight escalation critic closes most of the gap.
min_experiment: Build MobileSAM→SAM cascade; compare confidence-based vs. oracle vs. learned-critic escalation on cost-quality Pareto curves.
main_risk: Results depend on threshold tuning; needs careful Pareto methodology.

one_liner: Examine whether token pruning/merging in ViT encoders discards exactly the tokens later needed by mask decoding: a temporal mismatch between pruning criteria (classification saliency) and segmentation needs (boundary tokens).
hypothesis: Tokens pruned by attention-based saliency disproportionately cover object boundaries (measured by overlap statistics), and a decoder-gradient-informed pruning criterion retains boundary quality at equal token budgets.
min_experiment: Log pruned-token locations vs. GT boundaries across pruning ratios; compare saliency-based vs. gradient-informed criteria at matched FLOPs.
main_risk: Gradient-informed criteria may be too expensive to compute online.

one_liner: Study whether distilled students can exceed their teacher locally: identifying image regimes where MobileSAM-class students beat SAM due to smoothing away teacher idiosyncrasies, formalizing "beneficial compression."
hypothesis: Students outperform teachers on a stable, characterizable subset (hypothesized: high-noise/low-light images where teacher overfits texture), and this subset is predictable from image statistics.
min_experiment: Paired evaluation on large corpora; isolate student-win clusters; train an image-statistics classifier to predict wins; verify on new data.
main_risk: Student wins may be sparse noise rather than stable regimes.

one_liner: Test the interaction of distillation with subsequent PEFT: whether distilled students are harder to fine-tune (less adaptable) than same-size scratch models, quantifying an "adaptability tax" of distillation.
hypothesis: At matched size and downstream data, distilled students adapt less (lower fine-tuned ceiling, slower convergence) than scratch-trained peers, because distillation collapses feature diversity needed for adaptation.
min_experiment: Distill and scratch-train matched architectures; LoRA-tune both on 5 downstream segmentation tasks; compare ceilings and sample efficiency; measure feature-space effective rank.
main_risk: Matched scratch baselines at reasonable quality require substantial compute.

one_liner: Investigate energy-per-mask as a first-class metric: profiling where energy is actually spent (encoder, decoder, memory traffic) across SAM variants, and whether architectural choices ranked by FLOPs re-rank under measured energy.
hypothesis: Model rankings by measured energy-per-mask differ materially from FLOPs rankings (rank correlation <0.7), with memory-bound decoder stages penalizing some "efficient" designs.
min_experiment: Profile 6 variants on 2 hardware targets with hardware energy counters across batch sizes and resolutions; publish energy-per-mask Pareto curves.
main_risk: Hardware specificity limits generality; needs at least two platforms.

one_liner: Test whether tiny prompt-conditioned models can skip the heavy image encoder entirely for repeated prompting: caching a scene representation once and answering many prompts with a micro-decoder, quantifying the amortization frontier.
hypothesis: For sessions with ≥5 prompts, a micro-decoder (<5M params) over cached features achieves ≥95% of full-decoder quality, and quality loss concentrates on prompts far (in feature space) from the session's earlier prompts.
min_experiment: Train micro-decoders at several sizes on cached SAM features; evaluate per-prompt quality vs. session statistics; map the amortization frontier.
main_risk: Micro-decoders may fail on ambiguity handling, which matters in interactive use.

one_liner: Test whether the optimal LoRA insertion depth for vision models is task-type-dependent in a predictable way: low-level tasks (boundary refinement) benefit from early-layer adapters, semantic tasks from late-layer adapters.
hypothesis: A task's "feature-level demand" (measured by which frozen-layer probes best predict its labels) predicts the LoRA placement that maximizes fine-tuned performance, with rank correlation >0.7 across 12 tasks.
min_experiment: For 12 segmentation/detection tasks, run frozen-layer probing, then sweep single-block LoRA placements; test whether probes predict the best placement.
main_risk: Placement effects may be too flat in large models to discriminate.

one_liner: Investigate whether LoRA ranks needed for vision adaptation are set by the intrinsic dimensionality of the domain shift rather than task complexity, using controlled shifts of measurable dimensionality.
hypothesis: The minimal rank achieving 95% of full fine-tuning performance scales linearly with the estimated intrinsic dimension of the feature-space shift between source and target domains.
min_experiment: Construct domain shifts of controlled dimensionality (parametric corruptions, style axes); sweep ranks; regress required rank on shift dimension estimates.
main_risk: Intrinsic-dimension estimators are noisy in high dimensions.

one_liner: Study "adapter interference algebra": when two independently trained LoRA adapters are composed (added), can interference be predicted from the principal angles between their weight-update subspaces?
hypothesis: Post-composition performance drop correlates strongly with subspace overlap (small principal angles) in specific layers, enabling a pre-merge compatibility test that predicts failures before evaluation.
min_experiment: Train 20 task adapters on one backbone; merge all pairs; regress pairwise performance drop on principal-angle statistics per layer.
main_risk: Interference may be governed by activation-space (not weight-space) geometry.

one_liner: Test whether prompt-encoder-only fine-tuning of SAM (freezing image encoder and mask decoder) suffices for a surprising range of domain adaptations, implying many "domain gaps" are prompt-interpretation gaps.
hypothesis: For ≥30% of tested domain adaptations (medical, aerial, microscopy), prompt-encoder-only tuning recovers ≥80% of full-PEFT gains at <1% of trainable parameters.
min_experiment: For 8 domains, fine-tune each component in isolation (prompt encoder, decoder, encoder-LoRA) and in combination; build an attribution table.
main_risk: Component interactions may make isolated attributions misleading.

one_liner: Investigate the loss-landscape connectivity of PEFT solutions: whether independently trained LoRA runs on the same task land in linearly connected minima (in adapter space), unlike full fine-tuning.
hypothesis: LoRA solutions for the same vision task are linearly mode-connected (no loss barrier) at far higher rates than full fine-tuning solutions, explaining why adapter averaging works.
min_experiment: Train 10 seeds of LoRA and full FT on 3 segmentation tasks; measure loss barriers on linear paths; compare connectivity rates.
main_risk: Connectivity may trivially follow from low dimensionality, reducing novelty of the finding.

one_liner: Test whether PEFT under-trains "new physics" while over-fitting "new style": decomposing adaptation gains on domains that differ from pretraining in sensor physics vs. mere appearance statistics.
hypothesis: At fixed rank, PEFT closes style gaps (color/texture statistics) nearly fully but physics gaps (SAR speckle, ultrasound artifacts) only fractionally, and the gap ratio is rank-dependent in a characteristic way.
min_experiment: Build matched adaptation tasks (style-shifted natural images vs. SAR/ultrasound) with equal headroom; sweep ranks; compare gap-closure curves.
main_risk: "Equal headroom" matching across domain types is difficult to construct.

one_liner: Study gradient-flow bottlenecks in frozen-backbone PEFT: whether adaptation quality is limited by which layers gradients must traverse frozen, and whether inserting zero-init "gradient taps" (adapters used only for backward flow) helps.
hypothesis: Gradient norm attenuation through frozen blocks predicts per-layer adapter utility, and auxiliary gradient paths improve early-adapter effectiveness without adding inference cost.
min_experiment: Measure per-layer gradient statistics during LoRA training; correlate with per-layer adapter gains; test train-time-only auxiliary paths.
main_risk: Gradient attenuation may not be the binding constraint versus feature suitability.

one_liner: Ask whether PEFT changes what the model attends to or how it decodes: decomposing LoRA-induced behavioral change into attention-pattern change vs. value/readout change, per task.
hypothesis: Domain adaptation predominantly alters value/readout pathways (attention maps stay stable), while task-type changes (segmentation→depth) require attention-pattern changes — a dichotomy testable by constrained PEFT variants.
min_experiment: Train LoRA constrained to QK (attention-only) vs. VO (value-only) on domain-shift and task-shift settings; compare gains and attention-map drift.
main_risk: QK/VO constraints entangle with optimization difficulty, confounding interpretation.

one_liner: Test the data-scaling behavior of PEFT vs. full fine-tuning at the low-data frontier: whether PEFT's advantage at small n comes from implicit regularization or from preserving pretrained feature geometry, distinguishable by feature-space analysis.
hypothesis: PEFT's low-data advantage tracks preservation of pretrained feature neighborhoods (measured by k-NN overlap before/after tuning), not weight-space regularization strength, and disappears when full FT is constrained to preserve neighborhoods.
min_experiment: Sweep data sizes for LoRA, full FT, and neighborhood-regularized full FT on segmentation tasks; correlate advantage with feature-geometry preservation.
main_risk: Neighborhood-preserving full FT may be hard to implement cleanly.

one_liner: Investigate whether task vectors (weight deltas) from PEFT on vision tasks compose arithmetically across model scales: can an adapter trained on a small backbone be "up-mapped" to a larger backbone without retraining?
hypothesis: A linear map between small- and large-backbone feature spaces (fit once on unlabeled data) transports LoRA updates with ≥60% of retrained-adapter performance, indicating scale-invariant structure in adaptation directions.
min_experiment: Fit feature-space alignment between ViT-B and ViT-L; transport adapters for 5 tasks; compare against retrained adapters and zero-shot.
main_risk: Layer correspondence across scales is ill-defined.

one_liner: Study PEFT stability under prompt distribution shift: adapters tuned with box prompts may silently degrade point-prompt behavior, quantifying cross-prompt-type collateral damage of PEFT on promptable models.
hypothesis: Box-only fine-tuning degrades point-prompt IoU by a measurable margin even on in-domain data, and mixed-prompt tuning at a small mixing ratio eliminates the damage without diluting target gains.
min_experiment: LoRA-tune with box-only, point-only, mixed prompts on 3 domains; evaluate all prompt types before/after; find minimal protective mixing ratio.
main_risk: Effect sizes may be small for shallow adaptation.

one_liner: Test whether normalization-layer-only tuning (bias/scale) exploits a different adaptation mechanism than LoRA — feature re-weighting vs. feature re-mixing — with different failure profiles under distribution shift.
hypothesis: Norm-tuning and LoRA gains are partially non-overlapping (combined > either alone by more than additivity predicts on shifted data), because re-weighting corrects first-order statistics while re-mixing corrects feature correlations.
min_experiment: Tune norm-only, LoRA-only, and both on matched budgets across shift types; analyze which feature statistics each corrects.
main_risk: Budget matching across method families is nontrivial.

one_liner: Investigate "adaptation shortcuts": whether PEFT preferentially learns dataset-specific shortcuts (annotation style, class priors) before genuine visual features, and whether the learning-order signature can flag shortcut-dominated adaptation early.
hypothesis: Under LoRA, shortcut-aligned performance (on probe sets isolating annotation style/priors) rises earlier in training than genuine-feature performance, and the gap at 10% of training predicts final OOD degradation.
min_experiment: Construct probe sets separating shortcut vs. genuine cues for 4 datasets; log both curves during tuning; validate the early predictor on held-out runs.
main_risk: Constructing clean shortcut probes is dataset-specific and laborious.

one_liner: Ask whether PEFT can adapt a model's inductive biases (not just its features): e.g., tuning a ViT-based SAM to acquire scale equivariance for aerial imagery through adapter design alone, testing the limits of bias injection via low-rank updates.
hypothesis: Scale-equivariance error on aerial imagery cannot be reduced below a floor by any rank-r LoRA (floor decreasing slowly with r), while a tiny equivariant module achieves it immediately — establishing a bias-reachability boundary for PEFT.
min_experiment: Measure scale-consistency error across LoRA ranks vs. an equivariant baseline on aerial data with controlled scale factors.
main_risk: Negative results across ranks require careful optimization to be convincing.

one_liner: Test whether the best PEFT configuration is predictable from a cheap "fingerprint" of the target dataset (feature-shift statistics, label granularity, prompt type), learned across many adaptation runs as a meta-regression.
hypothesis: A meta-model trained on ~100 logged adaptation runs predicts near-optimal PEFT configuration (method, rank, placement, LR) for unseen datasets, retaining ≥90% of exhaustive-search performance at 5% of the cost.
min_experiment: Run a config grid across 25 diverse segmentation adaptations; fit the meta-regressor; validate on 5 held-out datasets.
main_risk: 25 datasets may under-sample the adaptation-problem space.

one_liner: Quantify "zero-shot erosion" during SAM fine-tuning: the decay curve of general promptable ability as a function of fine-tuning steps on a narrow domain, and identify the erosion-onset predictor.
hypothesis: Zero-shot erosion begins after a characteristic optimization phase transition (detectable by weight-update alignment shifting from decoder to encoder-adapter dominated), providing an early stopping signal that preserves generality at minimal target-task cost.
min_experiment: Fine-tune SAM on 4 narrow domains; checkpoint densely; track zero-shot suites and update-alignment statistics; test the predictor.
main_risk: The phase transition may not exist or may be dataset-specific.

one_liner: Test whether forgetting under PEFT is primarily an output-head phenomenon in promptable models: general capability persists in features but becomes unreadable by the shifted decoder, recoverable by decoder-only reset.
hypothesis: After domain PEFT, restoring only the original decoder recovers ≥70% of lost zero-shot performance while retaining ≥80% of domain gains, showing forgetting is mostly readout-level at low ranks.
min_experiment: After PEFT on 5 domains, evaluate all four combinations of {original, tuned} × {encoder-adapters, decoder}; build the recovery matrix.
main_risk: Encoder-adapter and decoder changes may be co-adapted, making swaps incoherent.

one_liner: Study forgetting asymmetry across capability types: whether fine-tuning erodes ambiguity handling faster than average IoU, making "still looks fine" checkpoints subtly broken for interactive use.
hypothesis: Multimask ambiguity quality degrades 2–3× faster (per fine-tuning step) than single-mask IoU, because narrow-domain data is ambiguity-poor and the multimask head unlearns first.
min_experiment: Fine-tune on single-mask medical data; track ambiguity benchmarks vs. IoU benchmarks per checkpoint; compare decay constants.
main_risk: Ambiguity benchmarks are less mature, adding measurement noise.

one_liner: Test "forgetting-free rank" existence: whether for each adaptation there is a maximal LoRA rank below which zero-shot performance is provably (empirically) preserved, and how this budget relates to target-task headroom.
hypothesis: Forgetting exhibits a rank threshold (sharp onset) rather than gradual growth, and the threshold correlates with the overlap between target-task gradients and the pretraining-dominant weight subspace.
min_experiment: Sweep ranks (1–256) across 6 adaptations; locate forgetting onsets; test correlation with gradient-subspace overlap measured cheaply upfront.
main_risk: Thresholds may be optimizer/LR-dependent, complicating a clean law.

one_liner: Investigate whether interleaving a tiny fraction of "self-generated pretraining-proxy" data (SAM's own outputs on diverse unlabeled images) during PEFT prevents forgetting as well as true pretraining data, which is often unavailable.
hypothesis: Rehearsing on the model's own frozen-checkpoint outputs (5% mixing) recovers ≥90% of the anti-forgetting benefit of true pretraining-data rehearsal across domains.
min_experiment: Compare no-rehearsal, true-data rehearsal, and self-output rehearsal at matched mixing ratios on 4 adaptations; measure zero-shot retention and target gains.
main_risk: Self-outputs encode model errors, possibly entrenching them (confirmation bias).

one_liner: Characterize sequential-adaptation orderings: whether adapting to domains in "increasing shift distance" order yields less total forgetting than the reverse, establishing curriculum effects in continual PEFT.
hypothesis: Near-to-far ordering (natural→aerial→medical) preserves more aggregate performance than far-to-near, because early small updates establish reusable directions that later updates refine rather than overwrite.
min_experiment: Run all 6 orderings of 3 domains (plus 2 longer sequences) with fixed budgets; measure final all-domain performance matrices.
main_risk: Order effects may be dwarfed by budget and LR effects.

one_liner: Test whether forgetting during vision PEFT is spatially selective in weight space: concentrated in identifiable "plasticity hotspots" (specific heads/blocks) whose freezing eliminates most forgetting at minor target-task cost.
hypothesis: >70% of zero-shot degradation is attributable to updates in <10% of adapted parameters (identifiable by influence-style attribution), and masking those parameters during tuning retains generality with <10% target-gain loss.
min_experiment: Attribute zero-shot loss to parameter groups via ablation/influence; retrain with hotspot masks; verify the retention/gain trade-off.
main_risk: Attribution instability; hotspots may shift when masked (whack-a-mole).

one_liner: Study cross-modal forgetting in multimodal PEFT: fine-tuning the vision tower of a vision-language model for segmentation may silently damage text-vision alignment, measurable only through multimodal (not vision-only) probes.
hypothesis: Vision-tower PEFT that improves segmentation degrades retrieval/grounding alignment measurably even when linear-probe vision quality is unchanged, and alignment damage correlates with update magnitude in late vision blocks feeding the shared space.
min_experiment: LoRA-tune the vision tower of an open VLM for segmentation; track retrieval, grounding, and VQA probes across checkpoints; localize damaging layers.
main_risk: Alignment metrics vary across probe tasks, complicating a unified conclusion.

one_liner: Ask whether forgetting is dominated by loss-function mismatch rather than data distribution: fine-tuning SAM with a different loss (e.g., Dice instead of its pretraining mix) may itself erode calibration/generality even on distribution-matched data.
hypothesis: Objective shift alone (same-distribution data, different loss) accounts for a substantial share of calibration erosion and multimask degradation, isolable by fine-tuning on pretraining-like data with altered losses.
min_experiment: Fine-tune on SA-1B-like data under 4 losses; measure generality/calibration erosion with data held fixed; compare against domain-shift-induced erosion.
main_risk: "Pretraining-like" data approximation may be imperfect.

one_liner: Test task-vector negation as forgetting repair: whether subtracting a scaled adaptation vector post hoc restores generality on demand, enabling a single checkpoint to be "dialed" between specialist and generalist modes at inference.
hypothesis: Performance on target and zero-shot suites varies smoothly and monotonically along the adaptation-vector scaling axis, with a Pareto-optimal dial setting outperforming both endpoints on mixed workloads.
min_experiment: Sweep interpolation coefficients on 5 adapted checkpoints; plot target-vs-zero-shot trade-off curves; test mixed-workload optima.
main_risk: Non-monotonic interpolation behavior would break the dial concept.

one_liner: Investigate forgetting through the lens of prompt-space coverage: fine-tuning with a narrow prompt distribution (tight boxes only) may cause "prompt-space forgetting" — degraded behavior on prompt regions unused during tuning — independent of image-domain effects.
hypothesis: Models fine-tuned with narrow prompt distributions degrade on held-out prompt regions (loose boxes, multi-point) even on the tuning images themselves, demonstrating prompt-space forgetting as a distinct phenomenon.
min_experiment: Fine-tune with restricted prompt families; evaluate the full prompt battery on tuning-domain images; map degradation across prompt space.
main_risk: Prompt-space effects may be small relative to image-domain effects.

one_liner: Study whether elastic-consolidation penalties transfer to adapter space: is penalizing adapter-parameter movement (relative to their own trajectory) effective, or does forgetting in PEFT require function-space (output-level) constraints?
hypothesis: Weight-space penalties on adapters are near-ineffective (adapter weights are non-identifiable), while function-space distillation on held-out images prevents forgetting at equal compute — a qualitative difference from full fine-tuning behavior.
min_experiment: Compare EWC-style adapter penalties vs. output distillation on sequential segmentation adaptations at matched budgets.
main_risk: Result may depend on adapter parameterization details.

one_liner: Test whether "forgetting" reported in fine-tuned VFMs is partially benchmark contamination artifact: zero-shot suites overlapping pretraining data make erosion look worse (or better) than true generalization change.
hypothesis: Forgetting magnitude measured on likely-contaminated benchmarks differs systematically from that on verified-novel data (post-training-date imagery), and the sign of the bias is predictable from memorization strength.
min_experiment: Assemble post-cutoff test imagery; compare fine-tuning-induced deltas on contaminated vs. novel suites for the same capabilities.
main_risk: Verifying non-contamination is hard without training-data access.
