one_liner: Investigate "dormant capability revival": whether capabilities apparently lost to fine-tuning can be revived by prompt engineering alone (specific prompt patterns re-eliciting pretrained behavior), indicating suppression rather than erasure.
hypothesis: For a substantial fraction of forgotten cases, there exist prompt configurations (multi-point patterns, box framings) that recover pre-fine-tuning outputs, proving the capability is suppressed, not erased — analogous to jailbreaking but for capability recovery.
min_experiment: Collect post-fine-tuning failures that pre-fine-tuning succeeded on; search prompt space per case; measure revival rate and pattern regularities.
main_risk: Prompt search may overfit per-case noise rather than reveal systematic revival.

one_liner: Test population-level forgetting laws: aggregating hundreds of community fine-tunes of SAM (public checkpoints) to fit an empirical law relating adaptation dataset properties to zero-shot erosion, treating the ecosystem as a natural experiment.
hypothesis: Across community checkpoints, zero-shot erosion follows a predictable function of adaptation-domain distance and update norm, robust enough to forecast erosion of new fine-tunes within ±15%.
min_experiment: Harvest 100+ public SAM fine-tunes; run a fixed zero-shot battery; fit and cross-validate the erosion law against checkpoint metadata.
main_risk: Public checkpoints have inconsistent provenance/documentation, adding noise.

one_liner: Test whether SAM's predicted-IoU head is calibrated conditionally: globally decent calibration may hide severe miscalibration conditioned on object category, size, or prompt type — the regimes where decisions are made.
hypothesis: Conditional expected calibration error stratified by object size is >3× the marginal ECE, with systematic overconfidence on small objects, making size-blind gating unsafe.
min_experiment: Compute reliability diagrams stratified by size/category/prompt-type on 5 datasets; quantify conditional-vs-marginal ECE ratios.
main_risk: Stratified bins may lack samples; needs large evaluation corpora.

one_liner: Investigate pixelwise mask-logit calibration as spatial fields: whether miscalibration has consistent spatial structure (overconfident interiors, underconfident boundaries) that a spatially-aware recalibration map fixes better than global temperature.
hypothesis: A single distance-to-boundary-conditioned recalibration function (fit once per model) reduces pixelwise ECE by ≥50% relative to global temperature across datasets, revealing spatially universal miscalibration structure.
min_experiment: Fit boundary-distance-binned recalibration on one dataset; test transfer of the same function across 6 datasets vs. per-dataset temperature.
main_risk: The structure may be dataset-dependent, breaking universality.

one_liner: Study whether prompt-ensemble variance is a fundamentally different uncertainty type than weight-ensemble variance in promptable models, capturing prompt-interpretation ambiguity vs. model uncertainty — and whether they are additive predictors of error.
hypothesis: Prompt-ensemble and dropout-ensemble variances are weakly correlated (r<0.4) and each independently predicts distinct error types (ambiguity errors vs. domain-shift errors), so their combination dominates either alone for failure prediction.
min_experiment: Compute both variances on 10k cases with error-type labels; fit predictive models per error type; test additivity.
main_risk: Error-type labeling is subjective and labor-intensive.

one_liner: Test conformal prediction for masks: constructing distribution-free confidence regions (inner/outer mask bounds) with guaranteed coverage, and measuring how loose the bounds must be for SAM-class models in vs. out of domain.
hypothesis: Conformalized morphological bounds (erode/dilate calibrated on residual quantiles) achieve target coverage with informative (non-trivial) width in-domain, but the required width explodes disproportionately under domain shift — quantifying guarantee costs honestly.
min_experiment: Calibrate morphological conformal bounds on one domain; evaluate coverage/width in-domain and across 4 shifted domains.
main_risk: Morphological score functions may be poorly matched to error structure, inflating widths.

one_liner: Ask whether the multimask scores of SAM constitute a calibrated distribution over interpretations: does the score vector's implied probability of "which mask a human would choose" match empirical human choice frequencies?
hypothesis: SAM's softmaxed mask scores misestimate human choice frequencies with systematic bias toward larger masks, and a monotone recalibration fixes downstream ambiguity-resolution accuracy without retraining.
min_experiment: Collect human mask-choice frequencies on 500 ambiguous prompts; compare to score-implied distributions; fit and validate recalibration.
main_risk: Human choices depend on task framing, adding variance.

one_liner: Investigate calibration transfer under PEFT: whether fine-tuning that improves accuracy systematically destroys calibration, and whether calibration can be preserved by a small "calibration rehearsal" loss at negligible accuracy cost.
hypothesis: Standard PEFT increases confidence faster than accuracy (growing overconfidence), and a proper-scoring-rule term on 1% held-out data eliminates the calibration damage without measurable accuracy loss.
min_experiment: Track ECE and accuracy across PEFT checkpoints on 5 adaptations, with and without the calibration term.
main_risk: Effect sizes may vary with loss choice, requiring several baselines.

one_liner: Test whether uncertainty communicated as "second-best hypothesis" (showing the alternative mask) beats scalar confidence for human decision quality in verification workflows — an uncertainty-representation question, not an estimation one.
hypothesis: Verifiers shown the top-2 masks catch more true errors per unit time than verifiers shown heatmaps or scalar scores, because alternatives direct attention to decision-relevant regions.
min_experiment: Within-subject user study (n≈20) verifying masks under 3 uncertainty displays; measure error-catch rate and time.
main_risk: User-study effects may be small relative to individual variance.

one_liner: Study "confidence collapse under iterative prompting": whether SAM's confidence monotonically increases with more clicks even when accuracy stagnates, creating dangerous certainty at interaction dead-ends.
hypothesis: Predicted IoU increases with click count roughly linearly even on objects where true IoU has plateaued, and the inflation rate is a stable model constant correctable post hoc.
min_experiment: Run scripted 10-click sessions on 2k objects; regress predicted and true IoU on click index; quantify divergence.
main_risk: Scripted clicks may not reproduce human interaction statistics.

one_liner: Investigate whether epistemic uncertainty in VFMs can be read from feature-space density (distance to pretraining feature manifold) without any ensembling, validated against actual error on novel domains.
hypothesis: A density model over encoder features (fit on generic unlabeled data) predicts domain-shift-induced errors with AUROC within 0.05 of deep ensembles at <5% of the cost, but fails specifically on adversarial and near-manifold shifts.
min_experiment: Fit normalizing-flow/k-NN density on SAM features; evaluate failure prediction across 8 shifted datasets against ensembles.
main_risk: Density estimation quality in 1024-d feature spaces.

one_liner: Test the "calibration inheritance" of downstream heads: whether heads trained on frozen VFM features inherit the encoder's confidence pathologies, implying calibration debt propagates through the ecosystem.
hypothesis: Heads trained on features from a miscalibrated encoder reproduce the encoder's error-confidence correlation structure even with calibrated training labels, and feature whitening reduces the inheritance.
min_experiment: Train matched heads on features from encoders with induced calibration differences; compare downstream reliability diagrams.
main_risk: Constructing encoders differing only in calibration is nontrivial.

one_liner: Study selective-prediction curves as the primary model-comparison tool: whether VFM rankings change when compared at matched coverage (fraction of cases attempted) rather than full coverage, revealing "risk-adjusted" model quality.
hypothesis: Model rankings on segmentation suites change for a substantial fraction of model pairs when evaluated at 80% coverage with each model's own confidence, making full-coverage leaderboards misleading for deployment choice.
min_experiment: Recompute pairwise rankings of 8 models at multiple coverage levels across suites; count rank inversions vs. full coverage.
main_risk: Depends on each model exposing a usable confidence — heterogeneity complicates fairness.

one_liner: Ask whether aleatoric-uncertainty ground truth can be constructed from annotation multiplicity, then test if any current segmentation uncertainty estimator actually predicts it rather than predicting model error.
hypothesis: Existing estimators correlate more with model error than with multi-annotator entropy (the true aleatoric target), failing the definitional test; a estimator trained explicitly on annotator entropy transfers better across models.
min_experiment: Use multi-annotator datasets; correlate estimator outputs with annotator entropy vs. model error; train an entropy-supervised estimator and test cross-model transfer.
main_risk: Annotator entropy confounds ambiguity with annotator skill variance.

one_liner: Test temporal calibration in video segmentation: whether confidence of SAM2 remains calibrated as tracking progresses, or degrades with time since last prompt, requiring time-conditioned recalibration.
hypothesis: Calibration error grows monotonically with frames-since-prompt, and conditioning recalibration on this single variable restores near-uniform calibration across a session.
min_experiment: Bin SAM2 confidence-accuracy pairs by frames-since-prompt across video suites; fit time-conditioned recalibration; validate on held-out videos.
main_risk: Confounding between time and content difficulty in real videos.

one_liner: Investigate calibration of "emptiness": how well promptable models express that a prompt hits nothing (background clicks, boxes over texture), and whether an explicit null-mask hypothesis improves pipeline precision.
hypothesis: Current models' best available null signal (low predicted IoU) is far from calibrated for emptiness detection, and adding a trained null-hypothesis output improves auto-annotation precision substantially at fixed recall.
min_experiment: Construct empty-prompt benchmarks; evaluate null-detection AUROC of existing signals; fine-tune with a null output token and compare.
main_risk: Defining "hits nothing" has edge cases (stuff classes, amorphous regions).

one_liner: Study cross-dataset transferability of recalibration maps: whether a recalibration function fitted on one dataset transfers to others within the same modality, testing if miscalibration is a model property or a data property.
hypothesis: Recalibration transfer retains ≥80% of ECE reduction within-modality but <30% across modalities, locating miscalibration jointly in model and modality statistics with quantified proportions.
min_experiment: Fit recalibration on each of 10 datasets; evaluate the full 10×10 transfer matrix; decompose variance into model/modality/data factors.
main_risk: Requires consistent GT quality across datasets for fair ECE.

one_liner: Establish the "token-occupancy law" for small-object segmentation: performance as a function of how many ViT tokens the object occupies, testing whether failures begin exactly below 1-token occupancy.
hypothesis: Segmentation quality collapses when objects occupy <1 token regardless of pixel count (varying input resolution to decouple the two), identifying tokenization, not information, as the binding constraint.
min_experiment: Evaluate the same physical objects at multiple input resolutions spanning the 1-token threshold; plot quality vs. token occupancy vs. pixel area.
main_risk: Resolution changes alter global context too, confounding the isolation.

one_liner: Test whether small-object information survives the encoder but dies in the decoder: probing whether frozen SAM features contain linearly decodable masks for objects the decoder fails on.
hypothesis: For a substantial fraction of decoder-failed small objects, a linear probe on encoder features recovers IoU>0.5 masks, proving recoverable information is discarded downstream.
min_experiment: Collect decoder failures on small objects; train per-dataset linear probes on frozen features; report recoverable fractions by size bin.
main_risk: Probe capacity choices blur the "information present" criterion.

one_liner: Investigate crop-and-zoom as principled inference for small objects: deriving the optimal zoom policy (when and how much to crop) from a model's measured size-response curve rather than heuristics.
hypothesis: A zoom policy that maps each object to the model's empirically optimal scale band (measured once on calibration data) beats fixed-zoom and no-zoom baselines by a significant margin at equal compute, and the optimal band is stable across datasets.
min_experiment: Measure IoU vs. rendered-scale curves; implement the derived policy; A/B against heuristics on small-object suites at matched FLOPs.
main_risk: Context loss from cropping may offset scale gains for context-dependent objects.

one_liner: Study thin-structure connectivity as a distinct competency: whether models that segment thin structures with high pixel accuracy still break topological connectivity, and whether connectivity failures cluster at specific curvature/junction motifs.
hypothesis: Connectivity breaks concentrate at high-curvature points and X-junctions (not randomly along structures), implicating specific local ambiguities rather than global capacity — testable via motif-conditioned break rates.
min_experiment: Extract break locations on vessel/wire datasets; classify local motifs; compare break-rate distributions against motif base rates.
main_risk: Motif taxonomy subjectivity; annotation of junction types.

one_liner: Test whether small-object detection failures in open-vocabulary detectors are recognition failures or localization failures, by decoupling with oracle boxes and oracle labels respectively.
hypothesis: For current open-vocab detectors, small-object AP loss decomposes predominantly into proposal-stage misses (localization), with classification-given-box nearly size-invariant — opposite to the pattern in closed-set detectors.
min_experiment: Run oracle-box and oracle-class ablations on size-stratified LVIS; report per-stage recovery by model family.
main_risk: Oracle ablations interact; ordering effects need careful design.

one_liner: Investigate the effect of training-data size distributions on small-object competence: does oversampling small instances at fixed data volume transfer to unseen categories, or does small-object skill remain category-bound?
hypothesis: Small-instance oversampling on category set A improves small-object performance on disjoint category set B by ≥50% of the within-A gain, evidencing a category-general smallness skill.
min_experiment: Fine-tune with size-resampled data on split A; evaluate size-stratified metrics on disjoint split B vs. controls.
main_risk: Category splits may leak visually similar classes.

one_liner: Ask whether context helps or hurts small objects in VFMs: measuring the causal effect of surrounding context on small-object segmentation via inpainting-based context ablations.
hypothesis: Context benefit is non-monotonic in object size: below a size threshold, ablating context (neutral inpainting) *improves* segmentation because attention mass stops leaking to context, reversing the standard assumption.
min_experiment: Inpaint context around objects at varying sizes; measure IoU deltas vs. size; track attention-mass reallocation.
main_risk: Inpainting artifacts may introduce their own confounds.

one_liner: Study sub-pixel boundary encoding for tiny objects: whether logit fields around 3–10 pixel objects carry sub-pixel localization information exceeding the mask grid, extractable for metrology applications.
hypothesis: Subpixel centroid/extent estimators computed from logits beat binarized-mask estimators by ≥2× localization accuracy on tiny objects, approaching the information-theoretic bound from image blur.
min_experiment: Synthetic tiny objects with exact ground truth positions; compare centroid/extent errors from logits vs. binary masks vs. classical fitting.
main_risk: Logit shapes may be decoder artifacts uncorrelated with true sub-pixel position.

one_liner: Test whether the small-object gap is partially an NMS/post-processing artifact in detectors: small objects suffer disproportionately from IoU-based duplicate removal because their IoU is hypersensitive to pixel-level box noise.
hypothesis: Scale-normalized duplicate-removal criteria (e.g., center-distance in units of object size) recover a measurable fraction of small-object AP without touching the model, quantifying how much "detection failure" is post-processing failure.
min_experiment: Replace NMS criteria with scale-normalized variants across detectors; report size-stratified AP deltas and error-type migration.
main_risk: May be less relevant to NMS-free architectures, dating the finding.

one_liner: Investigate attention starvation of small objects: whether the total attention mass a small object receives in a cluttered scene predicts its segmentation failure better than its size, formalizing "salience competition" as the failure driver.
hypothesis: Received-attention mass mediates the size-failure relationship (size loses predictive power once attention mass is conditioned on), and attention re-injection at the prompt location eliminates the clutter penalty.
min_experiment: Measure per-object received attention across clutter conditions; run mediation analysis; test inference-time attention biasing toward prompts.
main_risk: Attention mass is layer/head-ambiguous; needs a defensible aggregate.

one_liner: Study densely packed small instances (grains, cells, crowds) as a phase-transition problem: whether instance-separation ability collapses discontinuously at a critical packing density, and whether the critical density scales with model resolution.
hypothesis: Instance-recall vs. packing-density curves show a sharp transition whose critical point scales linearly with effective output resolution, enabling extrapolation of feasibility for a target density from model specs.
min_experiment: Synthetic packing-density sweeps plus real datasets binned by density; locate transitions across models with differing resolutions.
main_risk: Real-data density confounds with object appearance changes.

one_liner: Test whether small-object performance can be bought at inference time via test-time augmentation targeted by a size-aware disagreement detector, spending compute only where the size regime predicts fragility.
hypothesis: Size-and-disagreement-gated TTA achieves ≥90% of full-TTA small-object gains at ≤25% of its compute, establishing adaptive-compute allocation as strictly dominant for size-skewed workloads.
min_experiment: Implement gated vs. uniform TTA on size-skewed datasets; report Pareto curves of small-object AP vs. compute.
main_risk: Gains bounded by TTA's inherent ceiling on the base model.

one_liner: Investigate annotation reliability as the hidden ceiling for small objects: measuring inter-annotator IoU as a function of object size to determine where model "failures" are actually within label noise.
hypothesis: Inter-annotator IoU declines steeply below ~20px objects, and correcting model-human gaps for label noise removes a large share of the claimed small-object deficit on standard benchmarks.
min_experiment: Multi-annotate size-stratified samples from COCO/LVIS; compute noise-adjusted model gaps per size bin.
main_risk: Annotator recruitment/protocol strongly affects noise estimates.

one_liner: Ask whether video temporal integration can rescue small static objects: aggregating SAM2 features across frames of a shaking/moving camera to super-resolve small-object segmentation beyond single-frame ability.
hypothesis: SAM2's memory attention does not currently exploit sub-pixel multi-frame evidence (video ≈ best single frame for small statics), but explicit feature registration and averaging yields measurable super-resolution gains — locating an unexploited information source.
min_experiment: Controlled jittered-camera videos of resolution charts and small objects; compare SAM2, single-frame SAM, and registration-averaged variants.
main_risk: Registration errors may cancel the sub-pixel gains in practice.

one_liner: Test size-conditional prompt strategies: whether the optimal prompt type flips with object size (points beating boxes below a size threshold because tiny boxes are noisier than clicks), yielding a size-aware prompting rule.
hypothesis: Below a threshold size, point prompts outperform boxes (box coordinate noise exceeds object extent), and above it boxes win; the crossover is predictable from annotation-noise models.
min_experiment: Evaluate point vs. box prompting with realistic coordinate noise across size bins on 3 datasets; locate crossovers; validate the noise-model prediction.
main_risk: Crossover may depend on annotator-noise assumptions that vary by tool.

one_liner: Quantify metric-induced research bias: whether mIoU's insensitivity to boundary and small-object errors has measurably steered model development, by re-ranking historical models under error-type-balanced metrics.
hypothesis: Under a boundary- and size-balanced composite metric, the apparent monotone progress of segmentation models over recent generations flattens or partially inverts for specific capability axes.
min_experiment: Evaluate 12 historical models spanning 5 years under mIoU and 4 rebalanced composites; analyze trend changes per capability.
main_risk: Composite-metric design choices could themselves bias conclusions; needs sensitivity analysis.

one_liner: Test benchmark saturation vs. label-noise floor: for saturated segmentation benchmarks, determine whether top models have reached the label-noise ceiling, making residual gaps meaningless.
hypothesis: On several standard benchmarks, inter-annotator agreement bounds imply top-5 model differences are statistically indistinguishable, and bootstrap-over-annotations breaks current orderings.
min_experiment: Multi-annotate benchmark samples; propagate label uncertainty through metric computation; report significance of top-model gaps.
main_risk: Partial re-annotation may not capture full benchmark noise structure.

one_liner: Study "prompt protocol sensitivity" of promptable-model benchmarks: how much reported rankings depend on the simulated prompting protocol (click policy, box jitter), and define protocol-robust evaluation.
hypothesis: Model rankings flip for a substantial fraction of model pairs across common prompt protocols, and reporting a protocol-marginalized score (average over a protocol distribution) yields stable rankings.
min_experiment: Evaluate 8 models under 6 documented protocols; count ranking inversions; test stability of the marginalized score under protocol resampling.
main_risk: Defining the protocol distribution introduces its own arbitrariness.

one_liner: Investigate test-set contamination of VFMs via output regurgitation: detecting whether SAM-family models reproduce annotation-style idiosyncrasies of specific public test sets, indicating those sets leaked into training.
hypothesis: Models emit statistically detectable signatures (matching test-set-specific annotation conventions on ambiguous boundaries) on contaminated benchmarks but not on verified-clean ones, providing a contamination test without training-data access.
min_experiment: Define per-benchmark annotation-style fingerprints; test whether model outputs match fingerprints beyond what image evidence supports, using post-cutoff data as control.
main_risk: Style convergence may occur without contamination (confound).

one_liner: Build the case for "failure-mass" reporting: whether the tail of per-image errors (worst 5%) diverges across models that share identical mean metrics, and whether tail behavior predicts deployment incidents better than means.
hypothesis: Models matched within 0.5 mIoU differ by >2× in 95th-percentile per-image error, and tail metrics correlate better with human-reported failure severity in an applied setting.
min_experiment: Evaluate metric-matched model pairs; compare per-image error distributions; run a small practitioner study rating failure severity against both metric families.
main_risk: Tail estimates are high-variance; need large evaluation sets.

one_liner: Test whether "zero-shot" evaluations of promptable models are actually measuring prompt-engineering skill of the evaluator: variance across reasonable evaluator choices vs. variance across models.
hypothesis: Evaluator-choice variance amounts to a large fraction (>50%) of between-model variance on common zero-shot suites, quantified by crossed evaluator×model designs.
min_experiment: Have 6 independent evaluators (scripted configurations) evaluate 6 models; fit variance components; publish the ratio.
main_risk: Choosing "reasonable" evaluator configurations is itself contestable.

one_liner: Investigate benchmark ecology: whether the set of widely used segmentation benchmarks spans a small subspace of real-world image statistics, quantifying coverage holes against a large unlabeled corpus.
hypothesis: Standard benchmark suites cover <40% of the density of a broad web/robotics/medical usage corpus in feature space, with identifiable holes (night, motion blur, dense text, reflective surfaces) where model rankings differ from benchmark rankings.
min_experiment: Embed benchmarks and usage corpora in a common feature space; estimate coverage; spot-evaluate models in the largest holes with targeted annotation.
main_risk: Feature-space choice shapes coverage conclusions.

one_liner: Study granularity ambiguity as an evaluation confound: what fraction of measured "errors" on standard benchmarks are legitimate alternative granularities (part vs. whole) punished as mistakes?
hypothesis: Granularity-defensible predictions account for a nontrivial share (>15%) of measured error on instance benchmarks, and models differ systematically in granularity style, making current rankings partially granularity-taste rankings.
min_experiment: Human-review sampled "errors" from 5 models with a granularity-defensibility rubric; estimate confound share per model and benchmark.
main_risk: Defensibility judgments are subjective; needs multiple reviewers and agreement analysis.

one_liner: Test evaluation-through-use: whether downstream-task deltas (robot grasp success, image-editing user acceptance) correlate with segmentation-metric deltas across models, calibrating how much benchmark improvement buys real utility.
hypothesis: The benchmark-utility correlation is strong at low quality but saturates sharply beyond a task-specific threshold, and the threshold varies by an order of magnitude across applications.
min_experiment: Plug 6 models spanning quality levels into 3 downstream harnesses (grasping sim, editing study, counting pipeline); fit utility-vs-metric curves.
main_risk: Downstream harness idiosyncrasies may dominate the mapping.

one_liner: Investigate temporal evaluation drift: whether models evaluated on benchmarks collected years ago overestimate performance on current-day imagery (new products, styles, cameras), quantifying "benchmark aging" rates for segmentation.
hypothesis: Performance on temporally stratified imagery (matched content, different capture years) declines measurably with recency for models trained on older corpora, at a quantifiable rate per year that differs by category.
min_experiment: Collect year-stamped imagery of stable categories; evaluate fixed models across years; fit temporal decay curves.
main_risk: Isolating time from content/camera confounds requires careful matching.

one_liner: Test pairwise-comparison evaluation for segmentation: whether human A/B mask preferences produce different model rankings than IoU-based metrics, and build a preference-trained mask-quality model as an evaluation instrument.
hypothesis: Human pairwise preferences re-rank models relative to IoU in a reproducible way, and a learned preference model achieves higher agreement with held-out humans than any handcrafted metric.
min_experiment: Collect 10k pairwise mask preferences; compare metric-vs-human rank agreements; train and validate the preference model across datasets.
main_risk: Preferences are context-dependent (task framing changes what "better" means).

one_liner: Study statistical power of common evaluation practice: given typical test-set sizes and variances, what effect sizes can segmentation papers actually detect, and what fraction of published deltas fall below the detectable threshold?
hypothesis: A large fraction of recently published improvement claims fall below the minimum detectable effect at standard test sizes, implying the literature contains substantial noise mining.
min_experiment: Estimate per-benchmark metric variance via bootstrap; compute minimum detectable effects; survey published deltas from recent proceedings against them.
main_risk: Survey selection choices could bias the audit; must pre-register criteria.

one_liner: Investigate "annotation style transfer" as an evaluation equalizer: re-annotating a common test set under multiple explicit style guides to measure how much cross-dataset performance differences are style artifacts.
hypothesis: Under style-harmonized re-annotation, cross-dataset generalization gaps shrink by a sizable measurable fraction, re-attributing "domain gap" to convention gap for some dataset pairs.
min_experiment: Re-annotate 300 images under 3 style guides; evaluate fixed models against each; decompose gaps into style vs. residual domain components.
main_risk: Re-annotation cost; style guides may not capture implicit conventions.

one_liner: Test adaptive benchmarks that resist optimization: an evaluation protocol that continually reweights toward each submitted model's weakest regimes, and whether it changes development incentives in simulation.
hypothesis: Under simulated iterated development (models optimized against the benchmark), adaptive weakest-regime evaluation produces models with better worst-case and OOD behavior than static evaluation at equal development budget.
min_experiment: Simulate development loops (hyperparameter/data selection against static vs. adaptive metrics); compare resulting models on held-out stress suites.
main_risk: Simulation may poorly proxy real research dynamics.

one_liner: Quantify the reproducibility half-life of segmentation results: re-running headline evaluations from released code across environment/dependency drift to measure how fast reported numbers become irreproducible and why.
hypothesis: A significant fraction of headline numbers shift beyond claimed-improvement magnitudes when re-run with current dependencies, with image I/O and resize implementations as the dominant, fixable causes.
min_experiment: Re-run 15 released evaluation pipelines under controlled dependency variations; attribute deltas via ablation of I/O, resize, and numeric factors.
main_risk: Selection of re-runnable repos biases toward better-engineered work.

one_liner: Test the contrastive-vs-dense mismatch hypothesis: whether CLIP-style image-level pretraining produces feature geometries fundamentally misaligned with dense prediction (measured by intra-object feature coherence), explaining why segmentation heads on CLIP features underperform.
hypothesis: Intra-object feature coherence (variance within GT masks) predicts frozen-feature segmentation quality across 10 pretrained encoders better than linear-probe classification accuracy does, isolating the operative property.
min_experiment: Compute candidate geometric properties for 10 encoders; train identical heads; regress head performance on properties; validate the winner on held-out encoders.
main_risk: Properties are correlated across encoders, hampering causal isolation.

one_liner: Investigate whether SAM's encoder features and CLIP's features are complementary at the pixel level: fusing them not for performance engineering, but to map *which* pixels each representation uniquely resolves.
hypothesis: CLIP features uniquely resolve pixels requiring category identity (confusable textures across classes) while SAM features uniquely resolve geometric boundary pixels, with <20% overlap in uniquely resolved sets — quantifying the mismatch precisely.
min_experiment: Train per-pixel predictors from each feature set and their union; compute pixelwise information gains; cluster and characterize uniquely resolved pixels.
main_risk: Probe capacity may distort information attribution.

one_liner: Study resolution mismatch between pretraining and deployment: whether ViT features at unseen resolutions degrade due to positional extrapolation rather than content statistics, isolable by evaluating identical content at native vs. interpolated positions.
hypothesis: Most resolution-shift degradation in dense tasks traces to positional-embedding interpolation error (removable by resolution-specific positional refit on unlabeled data) rather than content-scale mismatch.
min_experiment: Evaluate dense probes at multiple resolutions with (a) interpolated positions, (b) refit positions, (c) content rescaled; decompose degradation.
main_risk: Positional refit may inadvertently adapt content statistics too.

one_liner: Test whether the "segmentation-friendly" property of DINO-style features is attributable to their emergent object-centric attention or to local smoothness, by constructing feature sets that dissociate the two properties.
hypothesis: Local smoothness without object-centric attention (achievable via smoothness-regularized distillation) accounts for most frozen-feature segmentation ability, demoting the celebrated attention structure to an epiphenomenon.
min_experiment: Distill feature sets preserving one property at a time; evaluate frozen segmentation probes; compare property-ablated performance.
main_risk: Clean dissociation via distillation may be technically difficult.

one_liner: Investigate token-grid anisotropy inheritance: whether downstream dense heads inherit the ViT patch grid as a measurable bias (mask edges snapping to patch boundaries), and how deep the artifact persists after upsampling layers.
hypothesis: Predicted boundary positions show statistically significant excess density at patch-boundary phases, decaying with decoder depth but never vanishing, and phase-randomized ensembling (shifted crops) removes it.
min_experiment: Histogram boundary positions modulo patch size across datasets/models; test excess at grid phases; validate the shifted-ensemble fix.
main_risk: Natural boundary statistics may alias with grid phases spuriously.

one_liner: Ask whether feature spaces of different VFMs are related by simple transformations: fitting linear/orthogonal maps between encoder feature spaces and measuring what fraction of dense-task-relevant structure survives translation.
hypothesis: Linear maps fit on unlabeled data transfer dense heads across same-family encoders with <10% relative loss, but fail across pretraining-objective families, quantifying which objectives create genuinely different geometries.
min_experiment: Fit maps between 6 encoder pairs; port segmentation heads; measure retention vs. retrained heads; group by objective family.
main_risk: Linear maps may be insufficient, requiring careful nonlinear controls.

one_liner: Study layer-role reorganization under fine-tuning: whether adapting a VFM for segmentation redistributes where (which depth) boundary and semantic information lives, breaking downstream tools that tap fixed layers.
hypothesis: Fine-tuning shifts information depth-profiles substantially (boundary information migrating earlier), and a lightweight "layer-role calibration" probe restores tool compatibility without retraining tools.
min_experiment: Probe information content per layer before/after various fine-tunings; quantify profile shifts; test probe-guided layer reselection.
main_risk: Probing methodology may itself be sensitive to feature scaling changes.

one_liner: Test whether multimodal joint spaces sacrifice spatial fidelity for alignment: measuring the spatial information (localization accuracy decodable from features) of vision encoders before and after text-alignment training at matched architectures.
hypothesis: Alignment training measurably reduces decodable localization precision relative to a vision-only twin (same data/architecture), with the loss concentrated in late layers and recoverable by early-layer skip connections.
min_experiment: Train matched encoders with and without alignment loss on identical data; compare spatial-decoding probes per layer.
main_risk: Matched-training compute cost; small-scale results may not extrapolate.

one_liner: Investigate "feature staleness" in cascaded vision systems: when a detector proposes regions and a promptable segmenter refines them, do the two models' representational disagreements (different notions of objectness) cause characteristic cascade failures?
hypothesis: Cascade errors concentrate on instances where the two models' objectness scores maximally disagree, and a 2-model agreement gate predicts cascade failure better than either model's confidence.
min_experiment: Build detector→SAM cascades; log both models' internal scores; test disagreement as a failure predictor across datasets.
main_risk: Score comparability across heterogeneous models needs careful normalization.

one_liner: Study whether frozen VFM features encode camera metadata (focal length, ISO, processing pipeline) strongly enough to act as shortcut features for downstream heads, causing camera-coupled generalization failure.
hypothesis: Camera parameters are decodable from VFM features with high accuracy, and downstream segmentation heads trained on camera-skewed data measurably exploit them (performance drops under camera-swap counterfactuals).
min_experiment: Probe camera-parameter decodability; train heads on camera-confounded splits; evaluate under camera-balanced test sets.
main_risk: Public datasets rarely document camera metadata richly.

one_liner: Test the "objectness universality" assumption: whether SAM's class-agnostic objectness transfers to domains with non-photographic object statistics (documents, circuit boards, star fields), or silently switches to texture-contiguity heuristics.
hypothesis: On non-photographic domains, SAM's masks align with local-contrast contiguity rather than domain-expert object definitions (measured by expert-annotated ground truth), and the misalignment is predictable from feature-statistics distance to natural photos.
min_experiment: Collect expert object definitions in 4 non-photo domains; evaluate SAM alignment; correlate misalignment with domain feature distance.
main_risk: Expert definitions vary within domains, complicating ground truth.

one_liner: Investigate representational collapse in feature upsampling: whether the common bilinear-upsample-then-convolve pattern discards a measurable fraction of the encoder's boundary information, using information-theoretic estimates before/after each decoder stage.
hypothesis: The first upsampling stage destroys more boundary-relevant information than all subsequent stages combined, and replacing only that stage with a learned resampler recovers most of the recoverable loss.
min_experiment: Estimate decodable boundary information after each decoder stage (probe-based); ablate/replace the lossiest stage; verify recovery.
main_risk: Information estimates via probes are lower bounds, complicating stage comparisons.

one_liner: Ask whether registers/artifact tokens in ViTs (high-norm background tokens) corrupt promptable segmentation specifically when prompts land near artifact-token locations, linking a known representation anomaly to a task-level failure.
hypothesis: Click prompts falling on artifact-token patches yield systematically degraded masks (excess failure rate) and register-token retrofitting eliminates the excess, establishing a causal chain from representation anomaly to user-visible failure.
min_experiment: Locate high-norm tokens; compare prompt failure rates on vs. off those patches; repeat with register-retrofitted encoders.
main_risk: Artifact-token locations correlate with background regions, needing careful matching.

one_liner: Study cross-modal prompt mismatch in unified models: whether visual prompts (boxes) and language prompts activate inconsistent segment hypotheses for the same target, quantifying intra-model cross-modal disagreement as a reliability signal.
hypothesis: Cross-modal disagreement (box-prompted vs. text-prompted masks for the same instance) exceeds 10% of cases, concentrates on boundary ambiguity and granularity, and flags errors with higher precision than single-modality confidence.
min_experiment: Prompt matched instances via box and text in one unified model; measure disagreement statistics; evaluate disagreement as an error detector.
main_risk: Text prompts introduce granularity variance beyond target identity.

one_liner: Test whether pretraining data geometry explains cross-encoder transfer asymmetries: encoders pretrained on object-centric photos transfer worse to scene-centric dense tasks than vice versa, controlling architecture and compute.
hypothesis: With architecture/objective/compute matched, pretraining-data composition (object-centric vs. scene-centric ratio) predicts direction and magnitude of dense-transfer asymmetry, establishing data geometry as a first-order factor.
min_experiment: Pretrain matched mid-scale encoders on composition-controlled mixtures; evaluate dense transfer both directions; fit composition-transfer curves.
main_risk: Mid-scale results may not extrapolate to production scales.

one_liner: Test whether DETR-style query slots develop persistent spatial "territories" that cause systematic misses when object counts in a region exceed local slot allocation, framing missed detections as a resource-allocation failure.
hypothesis: Each query's matched-object spatial distribution is stable across images (territories), and per-region miss rates are predicted by the ratio of local object count to local slot density, not by global count.
min_experiment: Map query-territory densities on trained detectors; regress regional miss rates on count/slot-density ratios across crowded datasets.
main_risk: Territories may be too diffuse in modern deformable variants.

one_liner: Investigate duplicate-suppression errors as identity decisions: when two overlapping detections are merged, how often does the survivor take the wrong class/box ("identity theft"), and is the error direction predictable from confidence miscalibration?
hypothesis: In overlap-merge events between different-class hypotheses, the surviving class is wrong in a substantial, calibration-predictable fraction of cases, so calibration repair improves detection accuracy without touching localization.
min_experiment: Log merge events on dense datasets; adjudicate survivor correctness against GT; test calibration-repaired merging.
main_risk: Requires GT-matched adjudication protocol for ambiguous overlaps.

one_liner: Study open-vocabulary detectors' "background prior" inheritance: whether regions labeled background in base training become systematically undetectable for novel classes occupying those regions (e.g., ceiling-mounted objects), a spatial prior contaminating open-vocabulary claims.
hypothesis: Novel-class recall is significantly lower in high-background-prior regions (quantified from base-training statistics) than in low-prior regions, controlling for object appearance — a location-based ceiling on open-vocabulary generalization.
min_experiment: Estimate spatial background priors from base annotations; evaluate novel-class recall stratified by prior; test prior-reweighted fine-tuning.
main_risk: Object appearance may covary with location, needing synthetic placements for control.

one_liner: Test the "confidence semantics drift" across detector operating points: whether a fixed confidence value means different precision at different object sizes/classes/times of day, making single-threshold deployment principally unsound — and quantify the cost.
hypothesis: Condition-conditional precision at a fixed confidence varies by >30 points across common strata, and per-stratum thresholding recovers a large fraction of oracle-threshold performance.
min_experiment: Compute conditional precision-confidence curves across strata on 4 datasets; measure fixed-vs-stratified thresholding gaps.
main_risk: Strata definitions influence conclusions; must pre-register.

one_liner: Investigate whether detection errors under occlusion follow an amodal-modal confusion: models localize the visible fragment but classify as if seeing the whole, or vice versa, producing characteristic box-class inconsistencies.
hypothesis: Under partial occlusion, box extent regresses toward visible-fragment bounds while class confidence remains near full-object levels, and this inconsistency signature predicts occlusion-caused errors with high precision.
min_experiment: Evaluate on occlusion-controlled composites; measure box-extent vs. class-confidence responses to occlusion fraction; validate the signature detector on real data.
main_risk: Synthetic occlusion may not reproduce natural occlusion statistics.

one_liner: Ask whether query-based detectors can count: probing whether the query-matching mechanism imposes an architectural ceiling on per-class instance counts (queries exhausted), distinct from perceptual limits.
hypothesis: Detection recall vs. instance count shows a sharp knee at a fraction of the query budget (interference before exhaustion), and the knee scales sublinearly with query count — an architectural law measurable across models.
min_experiment: Evaluate detectors with varied query budgets on count-controlled synthetic and real crowded scenes; locate knees; fit scaling.
main_risk: Training-data count distributions confound architectural limits.

one_liner: Study cross-class calibration coupling in detectors: whether improving one class's data (recalibrating its confidence) shifts other classes' precision through shared logit normalization, creating maintenance whack-a-mole in production.
hypothesis: Targeted single-class fine-tuning measurably shifts confidence distributions of untouched classes (beyond retraining noise), with coupling strength predicted by class co-occurrence and feature similarity.
min_experiment: Fine-tune on single-class data increments; measure per-class confidence/precision shifts vs. seed-noise baselines; model coupling factors.
main_risk: Distinguishing coupling from training stochasticity needs many seeds.

one_liner: Test whether "detect-then-segment" and "segment-then-group" pipelines have complementary failure sets, and whether their disagreement is a near-oracle error detector for both.
hypothesis: Failure sets overlap on <40% of errors, and pipeline disagreement detects errors of either pipeline with precision far above self-confidence, making dual-pipeline verification economically rational for high-stakes annotation.
min_experiment: Run representative pipelines of each family on shared benchmarks; compute failure overlap and disagreement-based detection curves.
main_risk: Implementation quality differences may masquerade as paradigm differences.

one_liner: Investigate prompt-box "gravity" in promptable detection: whether loose user boxes bias detected extents toward the box (anchoring), quantifying how prompt geometry contaminates output geometry.
hypothesis: Output box extent interpolates between true extent and prompt extent with a stable anchoring coefficient that grows with visual ambiguity, and deconvolving the anchoring improves extent accuracy on loose prompts.
min_experiment: Sweep prompt-box looseness/offsets on annotated objects; fit anchoring coefficients vs. ambiguity; test post-hoc deanchoring.
main_risk: Anchoring may be nonlinear and context-dependent, resisting a simple coefficient.

one_liner: Study temporal flicker of detectors on static scenes: quantifying detection instability under imperceptible frame noise as a "detection jitter constant," and testing whether jitter predicts real-video tracking failure downstream.
hypothesis: Sub-JND input perturbations produce class-flips or box jitter on a substantial fraction of borderline detections, and the per-model jitter constant predicts downstream tracker identity-switch rates better than AP does.
min_experiment: Replay static scenes with sensor-noise-level perturbations across detectors; compute jitter statistics; correlate with tracking metrics on video suites.
main_risk: Jitter depends on threshold placement; needs threshold-marginalized definitions.

one_liner: Ask whether long-tail detection failure is primarily a naming problem in open-vocab systems: rare classes are detected but assigned frequent-class names, testable by decoupling localization recall from naming accuracy on tail classes.
hypothesis: For open-vocab detectors, a majority of tail-class AP loss is naming failure (correct class-agnostic box exists), with naming errors biased toward frequent siblings — the reverse of closed-set detectors' miss-dominated profile.
min_experiment: Evaluate class-agnostic recall vs. named AP on LVIS tail; classify errors; compare paradigms.
main_risk: Class-agnostic matching criteria affect the decomposition.

one_liner: Test detector behavior under "class absence certainty": images guaranteed to contain zero instances (verified empty scenes), measuring the false-positive floor and its scaling with scene complexity — the detection analogue of specificity testing.
hypothesis: FP rates on verified-empty scenes scale superlinearly with texture complexity and are dominated by a small set of recurring "phantom motifs" per model, which are identifiable and suppressible.
min_experiment: Curate verified-empty scene sets across complexity levels; catalog FP motifs per detector; test motif-targeted suppression fine-tuning.
main_risk: Verifying absence at scale is expensive.

one_liner: Investigate whether detectors' localization and classification streams disagree systematically as functions of viewpoint: boxes degrading at oblique views while classification stays stable, generating viewpoint-conditioned inconsistency maps.
hypothesis: Localization error grows with viewpoint obliqueness at several times the rate of classification error, and the divergence is architecture-family-dependent (query-based vs. dense heads).
min_experiment: Use 3D-controlled renderings and multi-view real datasets; fit per-stream error-vs-viewpoint curves per architecture family.
main_risk: Rendering realism limits transfer of conclusions.

one_liner: Study "annotation-policy overfitting" in detection: whether models internalize dataset-specific box conventions (amodal vs. modal, include-handle-or-not), and quantify how much cross-dataset AP loss is convention mismatch rather than capability gap.
hypothesis: A learned per-dataset "convention translator" (small box-transform model) recovers a substantial fraction of cross-dataset AP loss without touching the detector, upper-bounding the convention share.
min_experiment: Train box-transform translators between dataset pairs on overlap classes; measure AP recovery; report convention-share estimates.
main_risk: Translators may absorb some genuine localization correction, inflating estimates.

one_liner: Test whether end-to-end detectors trained without NMS develop implicit internal suppression circuits, identifiable and editable, whose failure explains residual duplicate errors.
hypothesis: Duplicate suppression localizes to identifiable self-attention interactions among queries (ablating them restores duplicates), and residual duplicate errors occur exactly when those interactions saturate — enabling targeted capacity increase at that circuit.
min_experiment: Ablate query self-attention patterns systematically; measure duplicate-rate causality; correlate residual duplicates with circuit saturation statistics.
main_risk: Circuits may be distributed, resisting localization.

one_liner: Measure capability-resolved scaling laws for promptable segmentation: whether boundary quality, ambiguity handling, and small-object competence scale with model/data size at different exponents, implying divergent capability futures.
hypothesis: Small-object competence scales with a materially smaller exponent than average IoU, predicting that scale alone will not close the small-object gap within feasible budgets.
min_experiment: Evaluate a model-size ladder (existing checkpoints) on capability-isolating suites; fit per-capability scaling curves; compare exponents with uncertainty.
main_risk: Public ladders confound size with data/recipe changes.

one_liner: Test whether interactive efficiency (clicks-to-target) improves with scale faster than zero-click accuracy, indicating scale preferentially buys "correctability" rather than correctness.
hypothesis: Clicks-to-90%-IoU decreases with model scale at a rate exceeding the zero-click IoU improvement rate, because larger models better integrate corrective evidence.
min_experiment: Run standardized interactive protocols across a checkpoint ladder; fit scaling of clicks-to-target vs. zero-click metrics.
main_risk: Interactive protocol choices may interact with scale, needing multiple protocols.

one_liner: Investigate emergent prompt-composition ability: whether the capacity to correctly integrate 3+ heterogeneous prompts (points+box+text) appears discontinuously at some scale, or grows smoothly — testing "emergence" claims in a controllable vision setting.
hypothesis: Multi-prompt integration measured with continuous metrics (IoU under prompt conflict) improves smoothly with scale, and apparent discontinuities arise only under thresholded metrics — supporting the metric-artifact account of emergence for this capability.
min_experiment: Evaluate prompt-composition suites across scale ladders with both continuous and thresholded metrics; compare curve shapes.
main_risk: Available scale ladders may be too sparse to resolve curve shape.

one_liner: Study data-scaling saturation structure for segmentation pretraining: whether adding more same-distribution masks saturates capabilities in a fixed order, defining a "capability saturation schedule" that guides data-collection stopping.
hypothesis: Capabilities saturate in a stable order (region accuracy first, granularity control last) across data scales, and the order is predicted by per-capability label information density.
min_experiment: Train mid-scale models on nested data subsets; locate per-capability saturation points; test order stability across two data sources.
main_risk: Mid-scale saturation orders may reshuffle at production scale.

one_liner: Test inverse scaling candidates in vision: identify segmentation/detection behaviors that degrade with scale (e.g., over-reliance on semantic priors overriding pixel evidence in unusual scenes), and characterize their mechanism.
hypothesis: Larger VFMs increasingly override pixel evidence with semantic priors on prior-violating scenes (objects in impossible contexts, atypical colors), measurably worsening at fixed evaluation as scale grows.
min_experiment: Build prior-violation suites (counterfactual composites); evaluate across scale ladders; verify monotone degradation and probe the prior-vs-evidence mechanism.
main_risk: Composite artifacts may drive effects rather than priors.

one_liner: Ask whether scaling changes error correlation across models: as models grow, do their residual errors converge (shared blind spots) or decorrelate, determining the future value of ensembling and of independent model development.
hypothesis: Residual-error correlation between independently trained models increases with scale on in-distribution data but not OOD, implying shared-blind-spot risk concentrates in-domain.
min_experiment: Evaluate pairs of independent models at multiple scales; compute error correlations in/out of distribution; fit scale trends.
main_risk: Truly independent training runs at scale are scarce.

one_liner: Study the scaling of "prompt literalism": whether larger promptable models follow prompts more literally (segmenting exactly the clicked part) versus inferring intent (the whole object), quantifying an interpretive-stance drift with scale.
hypothesis: Interpretive stance drifts measurably with scale in a consistent direction (hypothesized: toward intent inference), changing optimal prompting strategies across model generations.
min_experiment: Present part-ambiguous prompts across a model ladder; classify outputs as literal/intent; fit stance-vs-scale curves.
main_risk: Stance classification requires careful operationalization.

one_liner: Test compute-optimal allocation between encoder and decoder for promptable segmentation: whether the scaling-optimal parameter split shifts toward decoders as tasks demand finer masks, contradicting the encoder-heavy convention.
hypothesis: For boundary-critical workloads, compute-optimal allocation places several times more relative capacity in the decode path than current designs, with the optimum shifting predictably with output-resolution demands.
min_experiment: Train an allocation grid (encoder/decoder splits) at fixed total compute across two scales; fit allocation-performance surfaces per workload type.
main_risk: Grid training cost; conclusions may depend on architecture family.

one_liner: Investigate whether scaling pretraining diversity (domains) vs. depth (more of the same) trades off differently for zero-shot robustness vs. adaptability, defining a diversity-depth frontier for VFM data strategy.
hypothesis: Diversity-heavy pretraining maximizes zero-shot robustness while depth-heavy maximizes post-PEFT ceilings, with the frontier's shape stable across model sizes — enabling strategy selection by intended use.
min_experiment: Pretrain matched mid-scale models on diversity/depth-controlled mixtures; evaluate zero-shot and post-PEFT endpoints; map the frontier.
main_risk: Mid-scale frontier may shift at production scale.

one_liner: Test whether scale substitutes for prompts: measuring the exchange rate between model scale and prompt information (how many fewer clicks a 10× model needs), and whether the exchange rate is constant or regime-dependent.
hypothesis: The scale-prompt exchange rate is strongly regime-dependent: scale substitutes for prompts on common objects but not on ambiguous/rare targets, where interaction remains irreplaceable at any feasible scale.
min_experiment: Measure clicks-to-target across a model ladder stratified by object commonness/ambiguity; fit exchange-rate surfaces.
main_risk: Ladder confounds (data/recipe) contaminate exchange estimates.

one_liner: Study memorization-generalization structure in segmentation pretraining: whether per-sample memorization (verbatim mask reproduction) concentrates on atypical annotation styles, and whether removing memorized samples changes downstream behavior.
hypothesis: Memorized training masks concentrate in style-atypical annotations, and their removal degrades style-robustness (memorization serves as implicit style coverage), revealing a functional role for memorization.
min_experiment: Detect memorized samples via influence/extraction tests at mid scale; retrain without them; compare style-robustness suites.
main_risk: Memorization detection for masks lacks established tooling.

one_liner: Ask whether emergent "segmentation without prompts" (unprompted object discovery quality) predicts promptable quality across scale, testing if a cheap unprompted probe forecasts expensive promptable evaluation.
hypothesis: Unprompted discovery quality (clustering-based) correlates with prompted performance across checkpoints within a training run (r>0.9), enabling proxy-based early stopping and data decisions.
min_experiment: Log both proxy and full protocol across training checkpoints of two runs; measure trajectory-wise correlation and decision agreement.
main_risk: Proxy validity may break exactly at decision-relevant margins.

one_liner: Test scale effects on annotation-noise robustness: whether larger models trained on noisy masks learn to *exceed* their label quality (denoising) or to reproduce noise more faithfully, resolving a bidirectional-prediction standoff.
hypothesis: Beyond a scale threshold, models' outputs are systematically closer to clean GT than their own noisy training labels on held-out replicas (denoising regime), with the threshold dependent on noise structure (random vs. systematic).
min_experiment: Train scale ladder on controlled-noise masks with clean held-out GT; measure output-vs-label proximity to truth across scales and noise types.
main_risk: Controlled noise may not represent real annotation error structure.

one_liner: Investigate whether scaling reduces or amplifies dataset bias expression: measuring bias metrics (e.g., context-dependence of detection) across a model ladder trained on the same biased corpus.
hypothesis: Contextual bias (e.g., failing to detect objects out of typical context) grows with scale at fixed data (stronger prior learning), while feature-level biases shrink — a two-regime pattern reconciling conflicting intuitions.
min_experiment: Evaluate context-swap and feature-bias suites across a fixed-data model ladder; fit per-bias-type scale trends.
main_risk: Fixed-data ladders are rare; may require training them.

one_liner: Test the "capability tax" of multi-task foundation training: whether adding tasks (detection, depth, captioning) to a segmentation foundation model at fixed compute imposes measurable per-capability costs, and map the task-interference matrix at scale.
hypothesis: Task pairs partition into stable synergy/interference classes (predictable from gradient-conflict statistics measured early in training), letting builders forecast the cost of each added capability before full training.
min_experiment: Train task-subset combinations at mid scale; measure interference matrix; validate early gradient-conflict forecasting on held-out combinations.
main_risk: Interference structure may be recipe-sensitive (loss weights, sampling).

one_liner: Model the human-model interaction as a two-agent system: whether humans adapt their clicking strategies to a model's quirks within a session, and how this co-adaptation contaminates interactive benchmarks that assume static user behavior.
hypothesis: Users measurably shift click strategies within 20 interactions (toward model-favorable placements), improving joint performance beyond what static-policy simulation predicts, by a quantifiable co-adaptation gain.
min_experiment: Longitudinal user study (n≈20) with click logging across 100 objects; detect strategy drift; compare joint-performance trajectories to static simulations.
main_risk: Individual variability may swamp co-adaptation signals at small n.

one_liner: Test whether "model asks, human answers" beats "human clicks freely": an active-querying interface where the model requests specific disambiguations, evaluated against free clicking at matched interaction budgets.
hypothesis: Model-directed binary queries ("is this region part of the object?") at points of maximal expected information gain reduce total interaction time by ≥30% versus free clicking at equal final quality.
min_experiment: Implement expected-information-gain query selection over SAM hypotheses; user study comparing paradigms at matched budgets.
main_risk: Query comprehension overhead may consume the theoretical gains.

one_liner: Characterize interaction failure spirals: sessions where each correction worsens the mask, identifying the dynamical signature (correction-response gain >1) and the conditions triggering instability.
hypothesis: Spiral sessions exhibit a measurable loop gain (mask-change magnitude per correction) exceeding 1 from the first correction, predictable from initial mask-hypothesis entropy, enabling early spiral warnings.
min_experiment: Mine spiral sessions from large simulated and human logs; fit loop-gain models; validate entropy-based early prediction.
main_risk: Spiral definition sensitivity; human logs are scarce.

one_liner: Test scribbles vs. clicks information-theoretically: measuring bits-of-constraint per second of user effort across prompt modalities, and whether the best modality flips with object complexity.
hypothesis: Scribbles dominate clicks in constraint-bits per second for high-genus/thin objects but lose for compact objects, with the crossover predictable from object skeleton complexity.
min_experiment: Instrument effort (time, path length) and outcome across modalities on complexity-stratified objects with real users; fit crossover curves.
main_risk: Effort measurement noise across users and devices.

one_liner: Study "correction locality violation": user corrections intended as local edits causing distant mask changes, quantifying the violation rate and its trust cost, and testing locality-constrained decoding.
hypothesis: Distant changes (>2× object scale from correction) occur in a nontrivial fraction of corrections, correlate with user-reported frustration, and locality-constrained decoding eliminates them at <2% quality cost.
min_experiment: Measure distant-change rates across correction types; user study linking violations to trust ratings; implement masked-region re-decoding and re-measure.
main_risk: Some distant changes are genuinely desirable (topology fixes), complicating the contract.

one_liner: Investigate optimal correction ordering for multi-error masks: whether fixing the largest error first (greedy) is suboptimal because corrections interact, and derive an interaction-aware ordering policy.
hypothesis: Interaction-aware ordering (fixing errors whose correction maximally reduces other errors) saves ≥20% of corrections versus greedy on multi-error masks, and the interaction structure is predictable from hypothesis overlap.
min_experiment: Simulate all correction orderings on multi-error cases; measure ordering spread; fit interaction predictors; validate the derived policy.
main_risk: Combinatorial simulation cost limits object sample sizes.

one_liner: Test undo-informed learning: whether user undo events (implicit negative feedback on model updates) form a supervision signal that, aggregated across sessions, identifies systematic model failures better than explicit error reports.
hypothesis: Failure clusters mined from undo events have higher precision for reproducible model bugs than clusters from explicit feedback, because undos are behaviorally honest and abundant.
min_experiment: Instrument an annotation tool; collect undo streams; cluster undo-preceding states; verify cluster reproducibility as model failures.
main_risk: Undos conflate user error with model error, needing disentanglement.

one_liner: Study expertise transfer through interaction data: whether models fine-tuned on expert-user interaction traces acquire the experts' disambiguation preferences, transferring tacit knowledge that explicit labels miss.
hypothesis: Training on interaction traces (state-action sequences) transfers acceptance thresholds and granularity preferences measurably better than training on final masks alone, evaluated by agreement with held-out expert decisions.
min_experiment: Collect expert traces; train trace-conditioned vs. mask-only models; compare on expert-agreement metrics.
main_risk: Trace data collection at scale; expert time is expensive.

one_liner: Test latency's causal effect on interactive segmentation quality: not just satisfaction, but whether response delays change user strategies (fewer, coarser corrections) and degrade final masks — with a measured latency-quality curve.
hypothesis: Final mask quality degrades measurably beyond a latency threshold (hypothesized 300–500ms) via a strategy-shift mechanism (users batch corrections), not merely reduced correction counts.
min_experiment: Within-subject study injecting controlled latencies; log strategies and final quality; fit the curve and test mediation via strategy variables.
main_risk: Lab settings may not reproduce production impatience.

one_liner: Investigate cross-object priming within sessions: whether segmenting several objects of a category primes the model-user system (via cached prompts or user expectations) to segment subsequent same-category objects faster, and whether tools should exploit it by batching similar objects.
hypothesis: Same-category batching reduces per-object interaction time by ≥15% relative to shuffled order, with the gain split measurably between user priming and exploitable model-side context reuse.
min_experiment: User study with batched vs. shuffled object orders; decompose gains via model-side context ablations.
main_risk: Fatigue and learning effects confound ordering effects.

one_liner: Test the "annotation authority" problem: when model suggestions disagree with novice annotators, who is right how often — and does showing model confidence change novice deference optimally or pathologically?
hypothesis: Novices over-defer to confident wrong suggestions (accepting a large fraction of high-confidence errors) and under-defer to unconfident correct ones, with net label quality *below* unassisted labeling in identifiable regimes.
min_experiment: Controlled study crossing suggestion correctness × displayed confidence × annotator expertise; measure acceptance and final quality.
main_risk: Ethical design needed around deliberately wrong suggestions.

one_liner: Study memory across sessions: whether a personalized interaction memory (this user's past corrections on similar content) reduces repeated corrections, and what memory representation (exemplar vs. adapter) transfers corrections best.
hypothesis: Retrieval-based exemplar memory (correction replay on visually similar regions) reduces repeated corrections more than adapter fine-tuning at equal storage, because corrections are instance-specific rather than distributional.
min_experiment: Longitudinal simulated + human sessions on themed corpora; compare exemplar-retrieval vs. adapter personalization on repeat-correction rates.
main_risk: Retrieval quality on visual similarity may bottleneck the exemplar approach.

one_liner: Test group interaction: multiple annotators refining the same mask concurrently or sequentially — does sequential refinement converge to better masks than the best individual, or do annotators undo each other along style disagreements?
hypothesis: Sequential multi-annotator refinement converges on content errors but oscillates indefinitely on style dimensions (boundary tightness), so style-locking (fixing conventions upfront) is necessary and sufficient for convergence.
min_experiment: Chain annotators on shared masks with/without style guides; measure convergence vs. oscillation spectra of successive edits.
main_risk: Recruiting enough annotators for chains; ordering effects.

one_liner: Investigate eyetracking as a zero-effort prompt channel: whether gaze fixations during natural viewing suffice as implicit clicks for promptable models, and where gaze-as-prompt fails relative to deliberate clicks.
hypothesis: Fixation clusters achieve within 15% of click-prompt quality for salient objects but fail systematically on low-salience targets where user intent diverges from bottom-up attention — mapping the gaze-prompt validity boundary.
min_experiment: Collect gaze during object-identification tasks; feed fixations as prompts; compare against clicks stratified by target salience.
main_risk: Eyetracker precision and calibration drift contaminate prompt quality.

one_liner: Test interruption robustness of interactive sessions: when users abandon sessions midway, are partial interaction traces usable as weak supervision, and how much value do incomplete sessions carry relative to completed ones?
hypothesis: Partial traces (with abandonment modeled as censoring, not rejection) recover ≥60% of completed-session supervision value per interaction, substantially changing the economics of annotation at scale.
min_experiment: Truncate sessions artificially at varying points; train with censoring-aware losses; map supervision value vs. completion fraction.
main_risk: Real abandonment is informative (harder cases), violating random-censoring assumptions.

one_liner: Construct a taxonomy of segmentation ambiguity (granularity, boundary, membership, count) and test whether SAM's three-mask output covers the empirical ambiguity distribution or systematically truncates it.
hypothesis: A significant fraction of ambiguous prompts (>25%) have ≥4 human-defensible interpretations, and SAM's three slots collapse distinct interpretation types rather than sampling them representatively.
min_experiment: Multi-annotate interpretations for 1k ambiguous prompts; classify ambiguity types; compare against SAM's hypothesis coverage.
main_risk: Interpretation enumeration by annotators may be incomplete.

one_liner: Test whether the diversity of SAM's multimask outputs is calibrated to input ambiguity: does hypothesis spread grow with true ambiguity, or is it a fixed architectural signature independent of the input?
hypothesis: SAM's inter-hypothesis diversity correlates only weakly (r<0.3) with human-measured ambiguity, behaving as a fixed part-whole-background template rather than input-adaptive uncertainty.
min_experiment: Correlate hypothesis-set diversity with annotator-interpretation entropy across prompts; test template-similarity of hypothesis structure across unrelated images.
main_risk: Diversity metrics on masks (IoU-based) may miss semantic diversity.

one_liner: Study whether ambiguity resolution should be lazy: systems that carry multiple mask hypotheses through downstream stages (tracking, counting) and resolve only at decision time, versus eager single-mask commitment — quantifying the value of deferred disambiguation.
hypothesis: Lazy resolution improves end-task metrics (tracking consistency, count intervals) by a measurable margin over eager commitment at bounded compute overhead, with gains concentrated on granularity-ambiguous instances.
min_experiment: Build hypothesis-propagating variants of tracking and counting pipelines; compare end metrics and compute against eager baselines.
main_risk: Hypothesis combinatorics may explode in long pipelines.

one_liner: Test whether part-whole ambiguity follows compositional structure: when a click is part-whole ambiguous, are the offered hypotheses consistent with a single part hierarchy, or incoherent mixtures (part of one decomposition, whole of another)?
hypothesis: A measurable fraction of SAM hypothesis triples are hierarchy-incoherent (hypotheses that cannot coexist in any single part decomposition), and incoherence predicts downstream selection errors.
min_experiment: Annotate part hierarchies for 500 objects; test hypothesis-set embeddability into single hierarchies; correlate incoherence with error rates.
main_risk: Ground-truth part hierarchies are themselves contestable.

one_liner: Investigate sequential hypothesis elicitation: prompting the model repeatedly with "give another interpretation" (via hypothesis-conditioned re-prompting) to enumerate its full interpretation space, measuring exhaustiveness and redundancy of the elicitable set.
hypothesis: Conditioned re-prompting (masking prior hypotheses' regions from prompts) elicits substantially more distinct valid interpretations than the default output, showing the interpretation space is larger than the interface exposes.
min_experiment: Implement iterative elicitation; measure yield curves (new valid interpretations per iteration) against annotator-enumerated references.
main_risk: Elicitation tricks may generate invalid interpretations requiring filtering.

one_liner: Study ambiguity as a transferable annotation: whether ambiguity maps (where interpretations disagree) transfer across models, enabling one model's ambiguity atlas to warn another model's users.
hypothesis: Inter-model ambiguity-map correlation is high (r>0.7) for granularity ambiguity but low for boundary ambiguity, splitting ambiguity into transferable and model-specific components with distinct handling.
min_experiment: Compute ambiguity maps for 5 models on shared corpora; correlate by ambiguity type; validate atlas-based warnings on a held-out model.
main_risk: Ambiguity-map estimation noise may cap measurable correlations.

one_liner: Test the "commitment cost" of single-mask APIs: quantifying how much downstream applications lose when the API returns argmax masks versus full hypothesis sets, across application types — an ecosystem-level interface-design question.
hypothesis: Hypothesis-set APIs improve downstream task metrics by application-dependent margins (large for counting/editing, small for classification), yielding a principled table of where single-mask interfaces are acceptable.
min_experiment: Run 5 downstream applications with argmax vs. hypothesis-set inputs; tabulate deltas; identify the interface-sensitive application classes.
main_risk: Application implementations may under-exploit hypothesis sets, underestimating the cost.

one_liner: Investigate whether disagreement between granularity levels can be resolved by task context injection: conditioning mask selection on a downstream task descriptor ("for grasping" vs. "for counting") and measuring intent-alignment gains.
hypothesis: Task-descriptor conditioning (learned selection head over hypotheses) aligns granularity choices with task-appropriate ground truth substantially better than context-free selection, generalizing across unseen task descriptions.
min_experiment: Build task-labeled granularity GT for 4 tasks; train/evaluate selection heads; test on held-out task descriptions.
main_risk: Task descriptors may be too coarse to determine granularity reliably.

one_liner: Study inter-annotator disagreement as a segmentation target: training models to output the *distribution* of human masks (not a consensus), and testing whether distribution-matched models make better downstream decisions under all aggregation rules.
hypothesis: Models trained to match annotator distributions (via multi-sample losses) can reproduce any consensus rule post hoc within noise, while consensus-trained models cannot recover the distribution — an asymmetry making distribution training strictly preferable at equal data.
min_experiment: Train both paradigms on multi-annotator data; evaluate recoverability of held-out aggregation rules and downstream decision quality.
main_risk: Multi-annotator data volume may be insufficient for distribution learning.

one_liner: Test whether ambiguity handling degrades under domain shift faster than accuracy: models losing their multi-hypothesis competence (collapsing to single modes) on new domains even where their argmax remains decent.
