hypothesis: Hypothesis-set quality (coverage of valid interpretations) degrades at several times the rate of argmax IoU under domain shift, silently breaking ambiguity-dependent workflows before accuracy alarms fire.
min_experiment: Evaluate hypothesis coverage and argmax IoU across a domain-shift ladder; compare degradation slopes.
main_risk: Valid-interpretation ground truth needed per domain — annotation-heavy.

one_liner: Investigate the geometry of hypothesis space: whether SAM's mask hypotheses for a prompt lie on a low-dimensional manifold (e.g., a granularity axis) whose parameterization enables continuous granularity control as a user-facing dial.
hypothesis: Interpolations in the decoder's hypothesis-token space produce valid intermediate-granularity masks (monotone nested regions) for most objects, evidencing a continuous internal granularity parameterization.
min_experiment: Interpolate hypothesis tokens; test mask validity/nestedness across interpolation; user-test a dial prototype on part-whole tasks.
main_risk: Interpolations may leave the valid-output manifold, producing artifacts.

one_liner: Test ambiguity-aware evaluation: scoring predictions as correct if they match *any* human-defensible interpretation, and measuring how model rankings change relative to fixed-GT scoring.
hypothesis: Under any-valid-interpretation scoring, model rankings change materially, with models penalized under fixed GT for systematic granularity styles recovering most, revealing style-vs-error confusion in current benchmarks.
min_experiment: Enumerate valid interpretations on 1k prompts; rescore 8 models; analyze rank shifts and per-model recovery patterns.
main_risk: Interpretation enumeration is expensive and possibly incomplete.

one_liner: Study count ambiguity in cluster objects (grapes, crowds, foliage): whether models represent "one cluster vs. many items" ambiguity at all, and how hypothesis sets behave on aggregation-ambiguous prompts.
hypothesis: On aggregation-ambiguous prompts, current hypothesis sets almost never span the collective-individual distinction (offering only spatial variants), missing an entire ambiguity dimension humans routinely intend.
min_experiment: Curate aggregation-ambiguous prompt sets; classify hypothesis-set spans; compare against human intent distributions.
main_risk: Constructing clean aggregation-ambiguous cases needs care.

one_liner: Investigate whether ambiguity signatures identify mislabeled training data: instances where a strong model's hypothesis set persistently disagrees with GT flagging annotation errors with high precision, turning ambiguity outputs into a data-cleaning instrument.
hypothesis: Cases where GT matches *no* model hypothesis while hypotheses agree with each other are enriched for true label errors (precision >80%), outperforming loss-based ranking at matched review budgets.
min_experiment: Apply the criterion to standard datasets; human-verify flagged samples; compare precision-recall of review queues against loss ranking.
main_risk: Model biases may systematically flag correct-but-unusual labels.

one_liner: Test whether ambiguity can be reduced pre-model by capture guidance: instructing capture (viewpoint, framing) to minimize downstream segmentation ambiguity, quantifying how much ambiguity is capture-removable versus intrinsic.
hypothesis: A substantial fraction of granularity/boundary ambiguity (>40%) is removable by capture changes (closer framing, angle changes), and a viewfinder-time ambiguity predictor can guide capture effectively.
min_experiment: Photograph objects under varied capture protocols; measure ambiguity metrics per protocol; train and field-test a capture-guidance predictor.
main_risk: Capture guidance is inapplicable to archival or third-party imagery.

one_liner: Build corruption-response fingerprints for promptable segmentation: per-model curves of performance vs. corruption type/severity, and test whether fingerprints predict which model survives a given deployment environment better than average robustness scores.
hypothesis: Environment-matched fingerprint selection picks the best model for a held-out environment substantially more often than mean-robustness ranking, proving the mean is decision-insufficient.
min_experiment: Profile 8 models across a corruption battery; characterize 5 real environments' corruption statistics; test fingerprint-matched vs. mean-based selection.
main_risk: Real environments mix corruptions in ways batteries may not span.

one_liner: Test whether prompt-based interaction masks robustness failures: interactive correction ability may fully compensate corruption-induced errors for some corruption types (recoverable) but not others (unrecoverable), splitting robustness into two operationally distinct kinds.
hypothesis: Blur/noise-induced errors are largely interaction-recoverable (clicks restore quality) while semantic corruptions (fog, low light) resist correction — because the former damage readout and the latter damage representation.
min_experiment: Measure clicks-to-target across corruption types/severities; classify corruptions by recoverability; verify the representation-vs-readout mechanism via probes.
main_risk: Recoverability may depend on simulated-clicker realism.

one_liner: Investigate adversarial prompts (not images): worst-case click/box placements within valid prompting regions that minimize performance, defining certified prompt-robustness radii for promptable models.
hypothesis: Worst-case in-object clicks degrade IoU by >30 points on a large fraction of objects (vs. <5 for average-case), and certified radii (prompt regions with guaranteed quality) are computable via Lipschitz-style analysis of the prompt encoder.
min_experiment: Optimize adversarial prompts per object; measure worst-vs-average gaps; derive and validate empirical certification bounds.
main_risk: Certification may yield vacuously small radii.

one_liner: Study compression robustness as a deployment reality: JPEG/H.264/AV1 artifacts' effect on segmentation, testing whether codec-aware fine-tuning transfers across codecs or requires per-codec treatment.
hypothesis: Codec artifacts cause boundary-localized errors with codec-specific signatures, and fine-tuning on one codec transfers partially within DCT-family codecs but not to learned codecs — defining codec-robustness equivalence classes.
min_experiment: Evaluate across codecs/bitrates; fine-tune per codec; build the transfer matrix; analyze artifact signatures.
main_risk: Codec implementations vary; needs careful pipeline control.

one_liner: Test the "shift direction asymmetry" hypothesis: models degrade differently under shifts toward higher vs. lower image quality than training (e.g., a model trained on web images tested on professional captures), revealing an unexamined asymmetry in domain-gap thinking.
hypothesis: Upshift (to cleaner/higher-quality inputs than training) causes measurable degradation with a distinct signature (over-segmentation of newly visible detail), demonstrating that "better input" can be out-of-distribution.
min_experiment: Construct quality-ladder datasets of identical scenes; evaluate models trained at middle rungs in both directions; characterize asymmetric error signatures.
main_risk: Building matched multi-quality captures is logistically heavy.

one_liner: Investigate spatially non-uniform robustness: whether corruption sensitivity varies across the image field (center vs. periphery) due to training composition bias, producing position-dependent reliability maps for VFMs.
hypothesis: Peripheral image regions show measurably higher corruption sensitivity than central regions (center-bias inheritance), and the positional profile transfers across corruption types within a model.
min_experiment: Corrupt localized patches at controlled positions; map sensitivity fields per model; test cross-corruption transfer of the field.
main_risk: Object-position statistics of test data confound positional attribution.

one_liner: Study robustness interactions: whether corruption combinations (blur+noise+low-light, as co-occur at night) degrade superadditively relative to single-corruption predictions, invalidating the single-corruption benchmark paradigm.
hypothesis: Naturalistic corruption combinations degrade performance significantly beyond additive predictions from marginals, with the interaction structure stable enough to model with pairwise terms.
min_experiment: Evaluate a factorial corruption grid; fit additive and pairwise models to degradation; quantify interaction excess on naturalistic combinations.
main_risk: Factorial grids grow combinatorially; needs fractional designs.

one_liner: Test whether robustness can be retrofitted through the prompt path alone: fine-tuning only the prompt encoder to compensate for known corruptions (encoding "this image is foggy" implicitly), leaving the heavy encoder untouched.
hypothesis: Corruption-conditioned prompt-encoder tuning recovers a meaningful fraction (>40%) of corruption-induced loss at <1% of encoder-tuning parameters, because much of the loss is decoder misreading of shifted features rather than lost information.
min_experiment: Tune prompt encoders per corruption family; compare recovery against LoRA-encoder baselines at matched and unmatched budgets.
main_risk: Information genuinely destroyed by corruption caps prompt-path recovery.

one_liner: Investigate "robustness forgetting" during standard fine-tuning: whether domain fine-tunes silently discard the pretrained model's corruption robustness even within the target domain, and whether robustness must be explicitly rehearsed.
hypothesis: Domain fine-tuning reduces corruption robustness within the target domain itself (clean-target overfitting), and mixing minimal corrupted target data (5%) fully preserves it — a free fix once measured.
min_experiment: Fine-tune on clean domains; evaluate corrupted-domain suites before/after; test corruption-mixing mitigation curves.
main_risk: Effect may vary strongly with fine-tuning depth, needing a breadth of configurations.

one_liner: Test weather/lighting counterfactuals via controlled re-rendering: using relighting models to generate the same scene under many conditions, isolating illumination robustness from all content confounds present in natural weather datasets.
hypothesis: Under content-controlled relighting, segmentation degradation attributes mostly to a low-dimensional set of illumination factors (shadow hardness, dynamic range compression), enabling targeted augmentation that closes most of the naturally measured gap.
min_experiment: Relight a scene corpus along controlled factors; regress degradation on factors; validate targeted augmentation on real night data.
main_risk: Relighting-model artifacts may contaminate the counterfactuals.

one_liner: Study robustness of the prompt-image binding: whether corruptions disrupt the model's association between prompt location and image content (clicks "landing" on wrong features under distortion) as a distinct failure channel from feature degradation.
hypothesis: Geometric distortions (rolling shutter, lens warp) cause binding errors identifiable by prompt-conditioned attention landing offset from the click, and binding errors respond to prompt-coordinate correction while feature errors do not — separating the channels.
min_experiment: Apply parametric geometric distortions; measure attention-landing offsets vs. mask errors; test coordinate-correction recovery.
main_risk: Attention landing is an imperfect proxy for binding.

one_liner: Test extreme-ratio safety: model behavior on inputs wildly outside spec (16:1 panoramas, 1000×20 strips, gigapixel crops), characterizing failure modes at input-geometry extremes that pipelines actually produce.
hypothesis: Beyond aspect-ratio thresholds, models fail non-obviously (plausible masks with systematic offsets) rather than obviously, making extreme-geometry inputs a silent-corruption class needing input validation with measured thresholds.
min_experiment: Evaluate across aspect/scale grids with GT; classify failure obviousness; derive validated input-spec boundaries per model.
main_risk: Findings are model-version-specific; needs an automated re-testing harness.

one_liner: Investigate whether self-supervised test-time objectives (entropy, consistency) used for adaptation can be gamed by the environment: distribution shifts under which TTA objectives improve while true accuracy collapses, mapping the safety envelope of test-time adaptation for segmentation.
hypothesis: Structured shifts (e.g., texture-uniform scenes) cause entropy-minimizing TTA to confidently collapse masks (proxy improves, accuracy collapses), and a proxy-accuracy divergence detector based on prediction topology flags these cases.
min_experiment: Run TTA methods across a shift taxonomy; identify divergence cases; build and validate the divergence detector.
main_risk: Detector may not generalize across TTA methods.

one_liner: Study multi-frame consistency as a robustness resource: for near-static cameras, whether enforcing temporal self-consistency at inference recovers single-frame corruption losses without any adaptation, quantifying the "free redundancy" available in video streams.
hypothesis: Consistency-filtered predictions (temporal median of aligned masks) recover ≥50% of corruption-induced loss for stochastic corruptions (noise, compression flicker) but ≤10% for static corruptions (fog), cleanly splitting corruption types by temporal recoverability.
min_experiment: Corrupt video streams; compare per-frame vs. consistency-filtered outputs by corruption type; map recoverability.
main_risk: Camera/scene motion breaks alignment assumptions.

one_liner: Test robustness certification transfer: whether randomized-smoothing-style certificates derived for classification transfer meaningfully to mask outputs (certifying pixel sets stable under bounded perturbations), and how large certified regions are for real VFMs.
hypothesis: Pixelwise smoothing certificates yield non-vacuous certified stable regions covering the majority of interior pixels but near-zero boundary bands, formalizing that only mask interiors are certifiable with current techniques.
min_experiment: Implement smoothed inference for SAM-class models; compute certified-pixel maps across datasets; report certified-fraction statistics vs. perturbation budgets.
main_risk: Smoothing degrades base performance, complicating fair reporting.

one_liner: Test whether referring-expression failures decompose along linguistic structure: quantifier failures ("all", "two of"), comparative failures ("the larger"), and negation failures having distinct error signatures and different scaling behavior.
hypothesis: Comparatives and negations fail at rates far exceeding matched-complexity attributive expressions, and their failures do not improve across model scale ladders while attributive failures do — locating a scale-resistant linguistic core.
min_experiment: Build construct-stratified referring benchmarks with matched visual difficulty; evaluate across scales; compare construct-specific trends.
main_risk: Matching visual difficulty across constructs is delicate.

one_liner: Investigate the "reporting bias inheritance" in grounded segmentation: whether visually groundable attributes that people rarely mention (default colors, typical sizes) are disproportionately ungroundable, tracing model gaps to language-data reporting statistics.
hypothesis: Grounding accuracy for attribute-object pairs correlates with the pair's text-corpus mention rate beyond visual frequency, demonstrating language-side reporting bias as an independent cause of grounding failure.
min_experiment: Estimate mention rates and visual frequencies for attribute-object pairs; evaluate grounding per pair; run the partial-correlation analysis.
main_risk: Corpus mention statistics approximate the actual training text imperfectly.

one_liner: Study spatial-language grounding resolution: how precisely models resolve spatial prepositions ("on", "under", "leaning against") into segmentation decisions, and whether errors reflect coarse bounding-region approximations of genuinely relational concepts.
hypothesis: Model behavior on preposition-guided segmentation matches a simple relative-bounding-box template (not configurational semantics), mispredicting exactly the configurations where template and true relation diverge (e.g., "under" with overhangs).
min_experiment: Construct configuration-controlled scenes dissociating templates from true relations; measure model agreement with each account.
main_risk: Scene construction (real or rendered) at controlled configurations is labor-intensive.

one_liner: Test cross-lingual grounding parity: whether open-vocabulary segmentation quality for concept translations tracks the training text's language distribution, and whether visual grounding transfers across languages through shared embeddings or must be relearned per language.
hypothesis: Grounding quality gaps across languages exceed what embedding-similarity to English predicts, indicating per-language grounding learning rather than free transfer through shared space.
min_experiment: Evaluate concept segmentation across 10 languages with matched concepts; regress gaps on language-data share and embedding alignment.
main_risk: Translation quality of evaluation concepts confounds capability measurement.

one_liner: Investigate description-length scaling: whether longer, more specific referring expressions monotonically improve grounding or exhibit an inverted-U (over-specification confusing models), and locate the optimal specificity point.
hypothesis: Grounding accuracy peaks at intermediate description lengths and declines with over-specification, because models mis-integrate redundant attributes into conjunctive constraints that spuriously fail.
min_experiment: Generate specificity ladders for fixed targets (1–10 attributes); measure accuracy curves; analyze failure modes at the over-specified end.
main_risk: Generated descriptions may introduce naturalness confounds along the ladder.

one_liner: Study grounding under referential ambiguity: when an expression matches multiple instances, do models exhibit consistent selection biases (leftmost, largest, most central), and do users' expectations match those biases?
hypothesis: Models show strong consistent selection biases (hypothesized: largest/most-central) that align with human expectations for only some ambiguity types, with mismatches concentrated in spatial-scanning conventions (humans expect reading-order).
min_experiment: Curate multi-match scenes; measure model selection distributions; collect human expectation distributions; compare alignment by ambiguity type.
main_risk: Human expectations vary culturally, complicating the reference standard.

one_liner: Test compositional binding errors in grounded segmentation: for "red cup next to blue plate," measuring attribute-object binding failure rates (segmenting the blue cup) as a function of scene distractor structure — the segmentation version of the binding problem.
hypothesis: Binding failures grow with distractor attribute-sharing in a pattern matching a similarity-based retrieval account (not random confusion), and the mask output localizes the failure to retrieval rather than segmentation.
min_experiment: Construct distractor-controlled scenes; measure binding-failure rates vs. distractor structure; fit retrieval-account predictions.
main_risk: Scene construction bias may favor one theoretical account.

one_liner: Investigate whether grounded models can segment by function ("something to cut with") versus by name, and whether function-grounding failures reflect missing affordance representations or missing lexical mappings.
hypothesis: Models fail function queries at high rates even for objects they segment correctly by name, and intermediate-layer probes show affordance information present but unaccessed by language — locating the failure in the mapping, not the representation.
min_experiment: Build name-vs-function query pairs; measure gaps; probe intermediate features for affordance decodability; test a small mapping layer trained on limited affordance data.
main_risk: Affordance ground truth is context-dependent and partly subjective.

one_liner: Study temporal referring in video ("the car that just turned left"): whether video segmentation models can ground event-anchored references, and if failures stem from missing event memory rather than language parsing.
hypothesis: Models parse event language correctly (verified via text-side probes) but cannot bind it to visual episodes beyond a few seconds back, localizing the failure in temporal binding rather than language understanding.
min_experiment: Build event-anchored referring benchmarks with controlled anchor-to-query delays; decompose failures via language-probe vs. temporal-window ablations.
main_risk: Constructing unambiguous event references at scale is expensive.

one_liner: Test whether text-prompt engineering transfers across grounded-segmentation models: prompt templates optimized on one model helping or hurting others, quantifying the portability of prompt-engineering investment in the vision-language space.
hypothesis: Optimized template gains transfer <40% across model families (near-zero across objective families), and transferability is predictable from text-encoder similarity — making prompt investment effectively model-specific.
min_experiment: Optimize templates per model on fixed tasks; cross-evaluate the template×model matrix; regress transfer on encoder similarity.
main_risk: Template optimization method choices may drive portability conclusions.

one_liner: Investigate vocabulary-free segmentation evaluation: measuring open-vocabulary models against exhaustive *unnamed* region annotations (is every coherent region segmentable by *some* query?) to separate vocabulary coverage from segmentation coverage.
hypothesis: A significant fraction of coherent regions (human-delineated, unnamed) are unreachable by any natural-language query for current models, quantifying a "nameability gap" distinct from mask-quality limits.
min_experiment: Exhaustively region-annotate images without names; crowdsource query attempts per region; measure the unreachable fraction and its correlates.
main_risk: "Any query" is human-crowdsourced, hence lower-bounded imperfectly.

one_liner: Study negation acquisition through contrastive fine-tuning: whether targeted "X but not Y" training generalizes negation compositionally to unseen concept pairs, or memorizes pair-specific exclusions — testing the learnability of a logical operator in grounding.
hypothesis: Negation fine-tuning on N concept pairs generalizes to held-out pairs with accuracy scaling in N (operator learning), rather than remaining at baseline (memorization), with a measurable sample-efficiency constant.
min_experiment: Fine-tune with negation data at varying pair counts; evaluate held-out pair negation; fit generalization-vs-N curves.
main_risk: Negation data construction may leak surface heuristics.

one_liner: Test attribute grounding density: whether models ground attributes only at object level (the whole cup is "red") or at true attribute extent (only the red stripe), measuring attribute-extent fidelity as a distinct capability from object segmentation.
hypothesis: Current grounded segmenters return object-level masks for sub-object attribute queries in the vast majority of cases, and attribute-extent fidelity requires (and responds to) part-level contrastive supervision — a measurable missing capability.
min_experiment: Annotate attribute extents distinct from object masks; evaluate models on extent-vs-object responses; test part-supervised fine-tuning.
main_risk: Attribute-extent ground truth involves genuinely fuzzy boundaries.

one_liner: Investigate query-image feedback loops in retrieval-then-segment systems: whether errors correlate across the retrieval and segmentation stages (shared embeddings), defeating the error-independence assumption behind pipeline reliability estimates.
hypothesis: Retrieval and segmentation errors on the same query-image pairs are strongly positively correlated when stages share encoders, inflating true system error rates well above independence-based estimates, and encoder diversification restores near-independence.
min_experiment: Build retrieve-then-segment systems with shared vs. diverse encoders; measure stage-error correlations and system-level reliability against predictions.
main_risk: Correlation depends on task mix; needs several workloads.

one_liner: Study "grounded hallucination" bidirectionality: whether models that hallucinate segmentation for absent concepts also fail to segment present-but-atypical instances, testing if both errors share a single prototype-matching mechanism with one threshold.
hypothesis: Per-concept hallucination rates and atypicality-miss rates are strongly correlated across concepts and both move together under prototype-threshold interventions, evidencing one underlying similarity threshold rather than two mechanisms.
min_experiment: Measure both error rates per concept across corpora; test threshold interventions; evaluate joint-movement predictions.
main_risk: Correlation may arise from concept difficulty confounds rather than shared mechanism.

one_liner: Characterize the annotation-pipeline fingerprint of SA-1B-scale datasets: measurable statistical signatures left by the model-in-the-loop collection process (mask complexity ceilings, boundary smoothness), and their inheritance by every model trained on the data.
hypothesis: SA-1B-style masks show detectable generator signatures (curvature spectra, size-complexity relationships) diverging from fully human datasets, and models trained on them reproduce these signatures on new images at measurable strength.
min_experiment: Compare mask-statistic distributions between assisted and manual datasets; train matched models on each; test signature reproduction on shared test images.
main_risk: Content differences between datasets confound pipeline signatures.

one_liner: Test model-collapse dynamics for segmentation self-training: iterating "train on own outputs" generations and measuring which mask properties degrade first, at what rate, and whether small human-data injections arrest collapse.
hypothesis: Collapse manifests first as boundary-detail loss and rare-morphology disappearance (before mean IoU moves), with degradation rate proportional to the pseudo-label fraction and arrested by ≥5% human data per generation.
min_experiment: Run 5 self-training generations with controlled human-data fractions; track boundary/diversity/rare-class metrics per generation.
main_risk: Compute cost of multi-generation training at meaningful scale.

one_liner: Study "easy-mask bias" in auto-curated datasets: confidence-filtered pseudo-labels over-representing easy objects, and whether models trained on such data develop measurable difficulty avoidance (worse-than-expected performance exactly on hard cases).
hypothesis: Confidence-filtered training produces models whose difficulty-performance curve is steeper than matched models trained on unfiltered noisy data, i.e., filtering trades noise robustness for hard-case competence in a quantifiable exchange.
min_experiment: Train on filtered vs. noise-matched unfiltered pseudo-labels; compare difficulty-stratified performance curves.
main_risk: Difficulty quantification itself requires a model, risking circularity.

one_liner: Investigate geographic/economic coverage bias in segmentation data through the object lens: household objects, vehicles, and street furniture from under-represented regions failing at rates predictable from data-source geography.
hypothesis: Region-specific object variants (cookware, vehicles, infrastructure) show boundary and recognition failures scaling with source-data geographic skew, and failures concentrate in category-atypical shapes rather than textures.
min_experiment: Assemble geographically stratified object imagery; evaluate models; regress failures on estimated data-source geography; classify failure types.
main_risk: Geographic data-source estimates for foundation datasets are rough.

one_liner: Test the marginal value of human annotation in the foundation era: on which data strata do human labels still beat model-generated labels for training (as measured by downstream gains per label dollar), and where has the crossover already happened?
hypothesis: Human labels retain positive marginal value only on identifiable strata (ambiguous boundaries, rare morphologies, small objects), with the value crossover predictable by model self-disagreement — enabling disagreement-directed human labeling.
min_experiment: Train with stratum-swapped label sources (human vs. model per stratum); measure downstream deltas per stratum; validate disagreement-based targeting.
main_risk: Stratum interactions may complicate clean attribution.

one_liner: Study duplication effects in web-scale segmentation corpora: near-duplicate scenes with slightly different auto-labels acting as label noise amplifiers, and whether dedup-with-label-reconciliation beats plain dedup.
hypothesis: Conflicting near-duplicate labels degrade boundary consistency measurably more than equivalent random noise (models oscillate between conventions), and reconciling labels across duplicate clusters before training recovers the loss.
min_experiment: Inject controlled duplicate-conflict structures; compare against matched random noise; test reconciliation preprocessing.
main_risk: Synthetic conflict structure may differ from natural duplication patterns.

one_liner: Investigate class co-occurrence scaffolding: whether models can only segment certain classes in their habitual context (ship needs water), quantifying context dependence per class and testing context-free data augmentation as the cure.
hypothesis: Per-class context dependence (performance drop under context swap) is predicted by training co-occurrence entropy (low-entropy classes are context-bound), and targeted decontextualized augmentation reduces dependence without hurting in-context performance.
min_experiment: Measure context-swap degradation per class; regress on co-occurrence entropy; run the augmentation intervention on the most context-bound classes.
main_risk: Context-swap composites introduce compositing artifacts.

one_liner: Test temporal data drift within training corpora: whether models weight recent-era imagery styles over older ones (or vice versa) beyond their corpus proportions, revealing implicit temporal weighting in training dynamics.
hypothesis: Per-era performance deviates from corpus-proportion predictions in a consistent direction (hypothesized: high-frequency modern styles dominate learning), quantifiable by era-stratified evaluation against era-stratified corpus statistics.
min_experiment: Stratify evaluation by capture era; compare performance profile against corpus era composition; test on models with known corpus vintages.
main_risk: Era correlates with content and resolution, needing careful controls.

one_liner: Study the "benchmark gravity" effect on data collection: whether new segmentation datasets increasingly resemble existing benchmarks statistically (convergent curation), shrinking the effective diversity of the evaluation ecosystem over time.
hypothesis: Distributional distance between new datasets and the benchmark centroid has decreased over publication years (controlling for domain), evidencing convergent curation that inflates cross-dataset generalization estimates.
min_experiment: Embed datasets by year of release in a common statistic space; test centroid-distance trends; correlate with reported generalization gaps.
main_risk: Genuine world homogenization (more phone photos) confounds curation effects.

one_liner: Test synthetic-data fingerprint leakage: whether models trained partly on rendered/generated imagery acquire detectable behavioral signatures on real data (e.g., expecting rendering-typical lighting), and whether signature strength predicts real-world degradation.
hypothesis: Synthetic-trained models show characteristic error patterns on real images (shadow-boundary handling, specular treatment) whose strength scales with synthetic fraction and predicts real-domain deficits, enabling a fingerprint-based synthetic-exposure audit of third-party models.
min_experiment: Train with controlled synthetic fractions; identify discriminative behavioral signatures; validate the audit on held-out models.
main_risk: Signatures may be renderer-specific, limiting audit generality.

one_liner: Investigate active-learning failure at foundation scale: whether classical uncertainty-based acquisition selects redundant or pathological samples when the labeler is a model-assisted pipeline, and design acquisition functions aware of the assistant's bias.
hypothesis: Uncertainty-based acquisition preferentially selects samples where the labeling assistant also fails, importing correlated label errors precisely on the acquired set and negating expected gains — measurable as an acquisition-labeler correlation penalty.
min_experiment: Simulate AL loops with assistant-labeled acquisitions vs. oracle labels; measure the correlation penalty; test decorrelated acquisition designs.
main_risk: Simulation fidelity to real assisted-labeling error structure.

one_liner: Study mask-quality stratification of training value: whether a small fraction of very-high-quality masks contributes disproportionately to boundary competence, supporting a "quality-pyramid" data strategy over uniform quality.
hypothesis: Boundary competence scales primarily with the volume of top-quality masks (matting-grade), largely independent of rough-mask volume beyond a threshold — implying pyramid budgets dominate uniform budgets at fixed cost.
min_experiment: Train on controlled quality mixtures at fixed budgets; fit per-capability value curves across mixtures; identify optimal pyramids.
main_risk: Quality-cost models vary across annotation vendors, affecting the budget mapping.

one_liner: Test cross-generation feedback risk in deployed annotation tools: whether datasets annotated with SAM-assisted tools produce models whose errors correlate with SAM's, creating an ecosystem-wide error monoculture measurable today.
hypothesis: Models trained on independent datasets that share SAM-assisted provenance exhibit significantly correlated errors on stress cases (relative to models from manually annotated data), demonstrating monoculture propagation through the tool layer.
min_experiment: Gather datasets with documented annotation tooling; train matched models; compare cross-dataset error correlations by tool provenance.
main_risk: Provenance documentation is sparse; confounds abound.

one_liner: Investigate optimal noise structure for mask training: whether structured label noise (systematic margins) damages learning more or less than unstructured noise at equal magnitude, informing which annotation errors are worth fixing.
hypothesis: Systematic noise (consistent over-tight margins) is learned as convention (recoverable by output calibration) while random noise of equal magnitude irreversibly blurs boundary learning — so QA should prioritize consistency over correctness.
min_experiment: Train on controlled noise types at matched magnitudes; measure recoverable vs. irrecoverable degradation; validate the calibration recovery for systematic noise.
main_risk: Real annotation noise mixes both types, complicating translation to practice.

one_liner: Study data ordering effects at scale: whether curriculum (easy-to-hard) vs. anti-curriculum vs. random data ordering during VFM pretraining changes final capability profiles (not just speed), testing order-dependence of what is ultimately learned.
hypothesis: Ordering leaves permanent capability signatures at fixed final loss (curriculum favoring boundary precision, anti-curriculum favoring hard-case recall), demonstrating path dependence in foundation training.
min_experiment: Pretrain matched mid-scale models under 3 orderings to equal final loss; compare capability batteries; replicate across seeds.
main_risk: "Equal final loss" stopping may itself bias comparisons.

one_liner: Test single-image adaptation limits: how much a promptable model can legitimately adapt from one test image (its own structures as self-supervision) without hallucinating, mapping the overfitting boundary of single-sample TTA for segmentation.
hypothesis: Gains from single-image TTA reverse sign after a predictable number of steps proportional to image self-similarity (texture repetitiveness), providing a computable early-stopping rule that keeps TTA safe.
min_experiment: Run TTA step ladders across images with measured self-similarity; locate gain-reversal points; validate the stopping rule out-of-sample.
main_risk: Reversal points may vary with the TTA objective choice.

one_liner: Study adaptation reversibility: after TTA on a corrupted stream, does the model return to baseline when conditions normalize, or accumulate permanent drift — and design "elastic" adaptation with guaranteed return properties.
hypothesis: Standard streaming TTA accumulates non-returning drift (hysteresis) after condition cycles, and anchoring adaptation as a bounded offset from frozen weights eliminates hysteresis at negligible adaptation cost.
min_experiment: Cycle corruption conditions on video streams; measure post-cycle deviation from baseline behavior; compare anchored vs. free adaptation.
main_risk: Some drift may be beneficial (environment learning), complicating the metric.

one_liner: Investigate what continual adaptation should key on: detecting *when* to adapt via distribution-shift detectors vs. adapting continuously, testing whether triggered adaptation dominates continuous adaptation in accuracy-stability trade-offs.
hypothesis: Shift-triggered adaptation (activate only when feature-drift detectors fire) matches continuous adaptation's shift responsiveness while eliminating most stable-period drift, dominating on combined metrics across realistic condition schedules.
min_experiment: Simulate realistic condition schedules on video corpora; compare policies on accuracy, drift, and compute; ablate detector choices.
main_risk: Detector latency may miss fast shifts, hiding triggered-policy weaknesses.

one_liner: Test cross-user adaptation contamination in shared deployments: one user's corrective adaptation degrading another user's workflows on a shared adapted model, quantifying the interference and testing per-user adapter isolation.
hypothesis: Pooled adaptation on conflicting user conventions (different granularity preferences) measurably degrades each user relative to per-user adapters, with interference proportional to convention divergence — quantifying the personalization-sharing trade-off.
min_experiment: Simulate user populations with divergent conventions; compare pooled vs. isolated adaptation on per-user metrics; fit interference-vs-divergence curves.
main_risk: Simulated conventions may understate real user diversity.

one_liner: Study feature-bank test-time adaptation: adapting via a growing episodic memory of test-domain features (retrieval-augmented inference) instead of weight updates, testing whether memory-based adaptation avoids forgetting and drift by construction.
hypothesis: Retrieval-augmented adaptation matches weight-update TTA's in-domain gains while exhibiting zero measurable drift and instant reversibility, at a storage cost growing sublinearly with stream length after deduplication.
min_experiment: Implement feature-bank inference over SAM features; compare against TTA baselines on gains, drift, reversibility, and storage across streams.
main_risk: Retrieval latency may violate real-time budgets.

one_liner: Investigate adaptation credit assignment in compound systems: when a detector-plus-segmenter pipeline degrades under shift, determining which component to adapt (and in what order) via component-wise shift attribution, rather than adapting everything.
hypothesis: Component-wise shift attribution (feature-drift localization per stage) predicts which single-component adaptation recovers the majority of pipeline loss, beating uniform adaptation at equal budget on most shift types.
min_experiment: Impose shifts affecting known stages; test attribution accuracy; compare attribution-directed vs. uniform adaptation recovery.
main_risk: Inter-stage interactions may defeat single-component attribution.

one_liner: Test "prompt memory" as continual learning: accumulating a library of (visual context → effective prompt) pairs instead of updating weights, treating continual improvement as prompt-policy learning over a frozen model.
hypothesis: Retrieval-based prompt policies (reuse prompts that worked in similar contexts) improve monotonically with experience without any forgetting risk, approaching a measurable fraction of weight-based continual learning's gains on recurring-context workloads.
min_experiment: Build the prompt-memory system on recurring-context streams (fixed camera datasets); track improvement curves against weight-based baselines.
main_risk: Gains cap at what prompt variation can express — possibly little for hard shifts.

one_liner: Study adaptation under label-delay: real feedback arrives hours or days late (human review), making standard online adaptation stale — quantify staleness costs and test delay-compensated adaptation schemes.
hypothesis: Adaptation value decays with feedback delay at a rate set by environment nonstationarity, and delay-aware weighting (discounting stale feedback against detected drift) recovers most of the no-delay value up to a computable delay horizon.
min_experiment: Replay streams with parametric feedback delays; measure value-decay curves; test delay-compensation schemes across nonstationarity levels.
main_risk: Nonstationarity estimation itself may be delayed, nesting the problem.

one_liner: Investigate negative transfer in fleet adaptation: aggregating adaptations across a device fleet (federated TTA) when devices face heterogeneous conditions, characterizing when sharing helps vs. poisons and deriving a sharing-decision statistic.
hypothesis: Pooled adaptation helps when inter-device condition similarity exceeds a threshold (measurable from feature statistics) and harms below it, and a similarity-gated sharing rule dominates both always-share and never-share policies.
min_experiment: Simulate fleets with controlled condition heterogeneity; map pooling benefit vs. similarity; validate the gating rule.
main_risk: Simulated heterogeneity may miss real-fleet correlation structures.

one_liner: Test whether adaptation should target the input instead of the model: learned per-deployment input transforms (color/tone/geometry correction toward the training distribution) as a weight-free adaptation alternative, and where input-space adaptation fundamentally cannot reach.
hypothesis: A learned invertible input transform recovers most performance for photometric shifts but none for semantic/content shifts, and the recoverable fraction is predictable from whether the shift commutes with the model's early layers.
min_experiment: Train input transforms across shift taxonomy; measure recovery fractions; test the commutation predictor.
main_risk: The commutation formalism may be too coarse for real shifts.

one_liner: Study self-supervised prompt-consistency adaptation: adapting on unlabeled targets by penalizing SAM's prompt-inconsistency (different prompts on one object should agree), and testing whether this vision-specific self-supervision beats generic entropy objectives.
hypothesis: Prompt-consistency objectives yield larger and safer adaptation gains than entropy minimization (less collapse risk, better boundary recovery) because they enforce a model-internal agreement invariant instead of confidence inflation.
min_experiment: Implement consistency-based TTA; compare against entropy/pseudo-label baselines across shift suites on gains and collapse rates.
main_risk: Consistency can be satisfied by degenerate solutions (empty masks) without careful constraints.

one_liner: Investigate long-horizon continual adaptation audit trails: methods to reconstruct *why* a continually adapted model behaves as it does (which past adaptations caused current behavior), enabling root-cause analysis after months of drift.
hypothesis: Logging low-rank adaptation increments with timestamps permits accurate behavioral attribution (replaying subsets identifies which increments caused a given behavior change) at storage costs feasible for year-long deployments.
min_experiment: Run months-long simulated adaptation with logging; test attribution accuracy on injected behavior changes; measure storage/replay costs.
main_risk: Increment interactions may defeat subset-replay attribution.

one_liner: Test adaptation-vs-reset scheduling: when accumulated adaptation underperforms a fresh restart from the base model plus quick re-adaptation, deriving the optimal reset schedule as a function of drift statistics.
hypothesis: Under realistic drift with occasional regime changes, periodic reset-plus-readapt outperforms pure continual adaptation, with the optimal reset period computable from measured regime-change frequency — a renewal-theory result for model maintenance.
min_experiment: Simulate drift with regime changes; compare reset schedules against continual baselines; validate the renewal-derived optimum.
main_risk: Real drift statistics may be too irregular for renewal assumptions.

one_liner: Study minimal-supervision drift correction: ranking cheap supervision types (single click per hour, one verified mask per day, binary "still working?" signals) by drift-correction value per unit human effort in streaming segmentation.
hypothesis: Sparse verified masks dominate abundant weak signals per effort-unit for representation drift, while abundant binary alarms dominate for threshold drift — a two-regime hierarchy enabling effort-optimal monitoring design.
min_experiment: Simulate drift scenarios with supervision budgets across types; measure correction value per effort; map the regime boundary.
main_risk: Effort costs vary by interface quality, complicating unit normalization.

one_liner: Test whether adaptation can be certified stable: constructing PEFT update families with provable output-deviation bounds on a reference distribution (adaptation that cannot change behavior on certified inputs beyond ε), enabling regulated in-field updates.
hypothesis: Norm-constrained low-rank updates with layer-wise Lipschitz budgets yield certified output-deviation bounds that are non-vacuous (tight enough to permit useful adaptation) on realistic reference sets — establishing feasible certified adaptation.
min_experiment: Derive bounds for constrained LoRA families; measure bound tightness vs. adaptation utility on medical shift tasks; characterize the certified-utility frontier.
main_risk: Bounds may be vacuous at useful adaptation strengths.

one_liner: Map the division of labor between SAM's decoder self-attention and cross-attention: which mask properties (extent, boundary, coherence) each attention type determines, via targeted attention-pattern interventions.
hypothesis: Mask extent decisions localize to token-to-image cross-attention while spatial coherence localizes to image self-attention, demonstrated by property-specific degradation under mechanism-specific perturbations.
min_experiment: Perturb each attention pathway independently (noise, ablation, patching); measure property-specific error responses across 1k objects.
main_risk: Pathways may be redundant, blurring attributions.

one_liner: Test whether the output-token bottleneck (a handful of mask tokens summarizing the whole query) causes information-theoretic mask complexity limits: masks whose description length exceeds token capacity failing predictably.
hypothesis: Mask reconstruction error grows sharply beyond a complexity threshold (measured in mask description length), and the threshold scales with mask-token count in controlled retraining — establishing a capacity law.
min_experiment: Evaluate error vs. mask complexity metrics; retrain decoder variants with 1–16 mask tokens; test threshold scaling.
main_risk: Mask complexity metrics are multiple and contestable.

one_liner: Investigate positional-embedding extrapolation pathologies: how promptable models behave when objects appear at positions/scales rare in pretraining (image corners, extreme sizes), attributing failures to embedding-space extrapolation vs. content unfamiliarity.
hypothesis: Corner/edge performance dips persist when familiar content is composited into rare positions (embedding-driven), and vanish under position-randomized fine-tuning of embeddings alone — isolating a cheap fix.
min_experiment: Composite objects across position grids; measure positional performance fields; retrain positional embeddings only; re-measure.
main_risk: Compositing artifacts may contaminate positional measurements.

one_liner: Study attention-sink formation in vision transformers used for segmentation: whether sink tokens (absorbing attention mass) create spatial dead zones where prompts underperform, and whether sink-aware inference redistributes attention productively.
hypothesis: Attention-sink locations create measurable prompt-response dead zones (lower mask quality for prompts landing there), and inference-time sink neutralization recovers the deficit without retraining.
min_experiment: Locate sinks per image; test prompt quality on/off sink locations with matched content; apply sink-masking at inference.
main_risk: Sink locations may covary with genuinely uninformative regions.

one_liner: Test layer-skip robustness as a modularity probe: which encoder layers can be skipped at inference with minimal segmentation damage, and whether skippable layers correspond to identifiable redundant computation that distillation should target first.
hypothesis: Skippability is bimodal (layers are either near-free or catastrophic to skip), stable across datasets, and predicts distillation-compression difficulty layer-by-layer.
min_experiment: Skip layers (with identity or interpolation bridges) singly and in combinations; measure segmentation damage; correlate with distillation outcomes.
main_risk: Skipping alters activation statistics for downstream layers, confounding attribution.

one_liner: Investigate whether mask decoders implement approximate energy minimization: testing if decoder iterations behave like optimization steps on an implicit energy (monotone refinement, convergence), which would license optimization-theoretic analysis of failures.
hypothesis: Decoder iterate sequences exhibit optimization signatures (monotone decrease of a learnable energy, step-size sensitivity, local-minimum trapping on ambiguous inputs), and trapping predicts multimodal ambiguity cases.
min_experiment: Fit implicit energies to iterate sequences; test monotonicity/convergence predictions; correlate trapping diagnostics with ambiguity benchmarks.
main_risk: Decoders may be too shallow (2 iterations) for meaningful dynamics.

one_liner: Study frequency-domain division of labor across encoder depth: whether early layers carry boundary-frequency information that late layers discard, explaining why single-layer feature taps force a boundary-semantics trade-off.
hypothesis: Decodable boundary information peaks at early-middle depth and decays monotonically after, while semantic information rises — with the crossing point predicting the optimal single-tap layer per task, and multi-tap fusion beating any single tap by a margin predicted by the spectral gap.
min_experiment: Probe boundary/semantic decodability per layer across models; validate tap-selection and fusion predictions on segmentation tasks.
main_risk: Probe architecture choices affect decodability estimates.

one_liner: Test stochasticity fingerprints of nondeterministic inference: whether GPU nondeterminism (atomics, reduction order) produces mask variation exceeding tolerance in boundary regions, quantifying the reproducibility floor of deployed segmentation.
hypothesis: Repeated identical-input inference varies boundary pixels measurably on borderline structures (near-threshold logits), setting a hardware-dependent reproducibility floor relevant for forensic and medical applications.
min_experiment: Run repeated inference across hardware/settings; quantify mask-variation statistics; map variation to logit-margin distributions.
main_risk: Modern deterministic-mode settings may make the effect negligible (still worth documenting).

one_liner: Investigate the role of the IoU-prediction head as a training regularizer: whether its auxiliary gradient shapes mask features beneficially (or harmfully), separable by training matched models with the head detached vs. attached.
hypothesis: The IoU head's gradients act as a mask-quality-aware curriculum (upweighting borderline cases), and detaching it degrades boundary quality measurably even when scores are never used — revealing a hidden training dependency.
min_experiment: Train matched models with attached/detached/stop-gradient IoU heads; compare mask quality and training dynamics.
main_risk: Retraining cost; effects may be small at scale.

one_liner: Study cross-image feature interference in batched inference: whether batch-level normalization or memory-optimization paths cause image A's content to measurably influence image B's masks, auditing inference isolation of production stacks.
hypothesis: Some production inference configurations exhibit measurable cross-image influence (output changes when batchmates change), concentrated in normalization-sensitive layers — a silent correctness bug class needing standardized audits.
min_experiment: Vary batchmates systematically for fixed target images across inference stacks; measure output deviations; localize responsible operations.
main_risk: Well-implemented stacks may show a null (still valuable as an audit protocol).

one_liner: Test width-vs-depth allocation in mask decoders: whether decoder capability scales better with more attention heads and width (parallel hypothesis capacity) or more iterations and depth (sequential refinement capacity), per failure type.
hypothesis: Width buys multi-hypothesis and multi-object capabilities while depth buys boundary refinement, with distinct saturation points — so the optimal decoder shape depends measurably on workload failure profiles.
min_experiment: Train a decoder shape grid on fixed encoders; evaluate per-capability batteries; map shape-capability response surfaces.
main_risk: Grid conclusions may depend on the frozen encoder choice.

one_liner: Investigate residual-stream pollution during multi-prompt inference: whether processing many prompts against cached features accumulates state (via any stateful component) that biases later prompts in the sequence, auditing prompt-order independence of inference engines.
hypothesis: Certain inference implementations show measurable prompt-order effects on identical prompt sets, traceable to implementation state rather than model design — establishing an audit protocol and a correctness bug class.
min_experiment: Permute large prompt sets on fixed images across implementations; test output invariance; bisect any violations to components.
main_risk: Likely null for reference implementations; value concentrated in optimized stacks.

one_liner: Study the emergence of instance individuation in encoder features: at which depth two touching same-class objects become linearly separable in feature space, and whether that depth predicts instance-separation ability across architectures.
hypothesis: Individuation depth (first layer where instance identity is linearly decodable for touching objects) varies across architectures and strongly predicts their touching-instance segmentation accuracy — a mechanistic performance predictor.
min_experiment: Probe instance separability per layer on touching-object corpora across 6 encoders; correlate depth statistics with downstream instance metrics.
main_risk: Linear separability may understate nonlinear individuation.

one_liner: Test activation-steering for segmentation control: whether adding learned steering vectors to decoder activations controls interpretable mask properties (grow/shrink, include-attachments, tighten-boundary) reliably across images — a training-free control interface.
hypothesis: Property-aligned steering directions exist (found from contrastive activation pairs), generalize across images with predictable strength-response curves, and compose approximately linearly for independent properties.
min_experiment: Extract steering vectors from contrastive pairs (tight/loose masks); test generalization, dose-response, and compositionality on held-out images.
main_risk: Directions may be entangled, producing side effects on unrelated properties.

one_liner: Investigate architectural memory of pretraining resolution: whether models pretrained at fixed resolution encode a persistent "native scale" detectable in feature statistics, biasing all downstream size perception even after multi-resolution fine-tuning.
hypothesis: Feature-statistic signatures of pretraining resolution survive multi-resolution fine-tuning and predict residual size-estimation biases (objects near native token scale privileged) — a persistent architectural memory with quantifiable behavioral footprint.
min_experiment: Fine-tune fixed-resolution models multi-resolution; test for surviving resolution signatures and size-conditioned performance asymmetries against natively multi-resolution controls.
main_risk: Distinguishing architectural memory from data effects requires careful controls.

one_liner: Test multi-view mask consistency as a 3D-understanding probe: whether SAM's masks of the same object from different viewpoints correspond to a single coherent 3D region, quantifying the "3D consistency defect" of 2D promptable models.
hypothesis: Cross-view mask lift-and-reproject consistency degrades sharply with viewpoint separation beyond 30°, with failure concentrated at self-occlusion boundaries, quantifying exactly where per-view masking breaks 3D pipelines.
min_experiment: Use multi-view datasets with meshes; prompt corresponding views; measure lift-reproject IoU vs. viewpoint separation; localize failures.
main_risk: Prompt correspondence across views must be automated carefully.

one_liner: Investigate whether monocular geometric cues in VFM features (implicit depth/normals) causally support segmentation decisions or are epiphenomenal, via cue-conflict scenes where geometry and appearance disagree.
hypothesis: On geometry-appearance conflict scenes (painted shadows, trompe-l'oeil), segmentation follows appearance over geometry in most cases, showing geometric information is present but unused — an integration gap rather than a representation gap.
min_experiment: Curate/construct conflict scenes; measure which cue masks follow; probe feature-level geometry presence in the same cases.
main_risk: Conflict scenes are rare and construction may introduce artifacts.

one_liner: Study native-3D vs. slice-wise 2D adaptation for volumetric medical segmentation at matched budgets: whether 2D foundation priors plus inter-slice fusion beat 3D-from-scratch across data scales, mapping the crossover.
hypothesis: 2D-foundation-plus-fusion dominates below a data threshold (per anatomy) and 3D-native above it, with the threshold predictable from through-plane information content of the anatomy.
min_experiment: Train both paradigms across data-size ladders on several anatomies; locate crossovers; regress on anatomy statistics.
main_risk: Fusion-method choice affects the 2D side's ceiling.

one_liner: Test 3D prompt semantics: what a "click" should mean in volumetric promptable segmentation (surface point vs. interior point vs. ray), and whether prompt-semantic mismatch explains failures of naive 2D-prompt ports to 3D.
hypothesis: Interior-point prompts and surface-point prompts produce systematically different segmentations in current 3D models (unintended sensitivity), and semantically explicit prompt encoding (declaring point type) improves 3D interactive efficiency measurably.
min_experiment: Evaluate 3D promptable models under controlled prompt placements (surface/interior/ray); measure sensitivity; test type-annotated prompt encoding.
main_risk: Few mature 3D promptable baselines exist to test.

one_liner: Investigate amodal completion competence: whether promptable models can be elicited (via prompts on occluded regions) to output amodal masks, and if amodal knowledge exists latently in models trained only on modal masks.
hypothesis: Prompting on occluder regions with object-context clicks elicits partial amodal completions significantly above chance, and a light amodal readout head trained on small data unlocks systematic amodal ability — evidencing latent amodal knowledge.
min_experiment: Construct occlusion-controlled scenes with amodal GT; test prompt-elicitation protocols; train small amodal heads on frozen features.
main_risk: Elicited completions may reflect shape priors rather than scene-specific inference.

one_liner: Study scale-metric blindness: promptable models cannot access metric scale (a toy car vs. real car at equal image size), testing whether metric-scale conditioning (camera intrinsics injection) changes segmentation decisions where physical size matters.
hypothesis: Intrinsics-conditioned fine-tuning measurably improves segmentation in scale-ambiguous cases (miniatures, close-ups) by resolving category priors correctly, demonstrating that metric information has task value beyond monocular cues.
min_experiment: Fine-tune with/without intrinsics tokens on datasets with camera metadata; evaluate on scale-ambiguity-stratified cases.
main_risk: Scale-ambiguous evaluation cases are rare and need curation.

one_liner: Test video-lifted pseudo-3D supervision: whether enforcing that SAM2 masklets sweep consistent 3D volumes (via structure-from-motion) during fine-tuning improves both video consistency and single-frame 3D-consistency defects.
hypothesis: SfM-consistency fine-tuning reduces cross-view mask defects and improves occlusion-boundary accuracy on still images, showing 3D-coherence supervision transfers to single-view geometric competence.
min_experiment: Fine-tune with SfM-consistency losses on unlabeled video; evaluate cross-view consistency, occlusion boundaries, and standard suites.
main_risk: SfM errors may inject geometric noise worse than the signal.

one_liner: Investigate viewpoint bias inheritance: quantifying how internet photography's canonical-viewpoint bias shapes segmentation competence across the viewing sphere, using controlled orbits of common objects.
hypothesis: Per-object segmentation quality over the viewing sphere correlates with estimated photographic viewpoint frequency, with characteristic collapse at rare viewpoints (top-down, underside) that targeted synthetic orbits repair.
min_experiment: Render/photograph object orbits; map quality over the sphere; correlate with viewpoint-frequency estimates; test synthetic-orbit fine-tuning.
main_risk: Viewpoint-frequency estimation for training corpora is approximate.

one_liner: Study part-segmentation consistency under articulation: whether part masks (e.g., limb boundaries) remain consistent as objects articulate, testing if models segment parts by geometry (joint structure) or by appearance snapshots.
hypothesis: Part-boundary placement varies systematically with pose (appearance-snapshot behavior) rather than staying anatomically anchored, and the inconsistency magnitude predicts downstream pose-estimation errors when masks are used as inputs.
min_experiment: Evaluate part masks across pose sequences with anatomical GT; measure boundary drift vs. pose; correlate with downstream tasks.
main_risk: Anatomical part GT under articulation is expensive to annotate.

one_liner: Test transparency-geometry entanglement: segmenting through transparent surfaces (objects behind glass) to determine whether models represent the layered scene structure or collapse layers into single-surface decisions.
hypothesis: Prompted on objects behind glass, models blend occluder and target into hybrid masks at high rates, and the blend ratio tracks relative contrast — evidencing layer collapse rather than layered representation, with prompt-based layer selection impossible in current architectures.
min_experiment: Curate behind-glass scenes with dual-layer GT; classify output modes (target/occluder/hybrid); test contrast dependence of blending.
main_risk: Dual-layer GT annotation is inherently ambiguous at reflections.

one_liner: Investigate volumetric prompt propagation: for 3D volumes, whether a single-slice prompt should propagate via the model's own features vs. geometric priors, and characterize where feature-propagation fails predictably (anatomy changes topology across slices).
hypothesis: Feature-based propagation fails predictably at topology-change slices (branch points, organ boundaries), and a topology-change detector (from feature-flow divergence) triggers re-prompting requests exactly where human input is needed.
min_experiment: Propagate prompts through annotated volumes; align failures with topology-change annotations; validate the detector's re-prompt triggering.
main_risk: Topology-change ground truth requires anatomical expertise.

one_liner: Study shadow-object binding: whether models segment objects with or without their shadows in a principled or contingent manner, and whether shadow treatment consistency can be controlled by a single learned direction.
hypothesis: Shadow inclusion is contingent on low-level contrast rather than represented as a semantic attachment relation, but a single activation direction can control inclusion consistently — revealing latent structure without semantic understanding.
min_experiment: Measure shadow-inclusion rates vs. contrast conditions; search for control directions via contrastive activation pairs; test consistency of controlled inclusion.
main_risk: Shadow GT (attached vs. cast) requires careful annotation protocol.

one_liner: Test cross-sensor volumetric transfer: whether adapters trained for CT transfer zero-shot to structurally similar but physically different volumetric modalities (industrial CT, micro-CT, OCT), locating the boundary between structure-transferable and physics-bound adaptation knowledge.
hypothesis: Anatomy/structure-related adapter components transfer across volumetric modalities (recoverable by adapter decomposition) while intensity-physics components do not, and the decomposition can be computed post hoc to enable partial transfer.
min_experiment: Train CT adapters; decompose (subspace analysis); test component-wise transfer to micro-CT/OCT tasks.
main_risk: The structure/physics decomposition may not align with any weight-space structure.

one_liner: Investigate whether egocentric video's geometric regularities (ground plane, hand proximity) are exploited or ignored by video segmentation models, testing egocentric-prior injection as a deployment-time improvement for wearables.
hypothesis: Current models leave measurable performance on the table in egocentric settings (errors violating ground-plane and hand-interaction priors), and lightweight prior injection (geometric consistency reranking) recovers a meaningful fraction without retraining.
min_experiment: Categorize errors on egocentric benchmarks by prior violation; implement prior-based reranking; measure recovery.
main_risk: Priors fail in edge cases (mirrors, climbing), needing safe gating.

one_liner: Study reflective-surface duplication: quantifying how often models segment reflections as independent objects across mirror/water/glass scenes, and whether reflection identity (link to source object) is decodable from features despite wrong mask outputs.
hypothesis: Reflection duplication is frequent and confidence-indistinguishable from real objects at the output level, yet reflection-vs-real is linearly decodable from intermediate features — an unread internal signal that a small head can surface for deduplication.
min_experiment: Curate reflection scenes with GT; measure duplication and confidence overlap; train reflection probes on frozen features; test deduplication.
main_risk: Probe results may not generalize across reflection types (specular vs. diffuse).

one_liner: Test whether segment-then-count beats count-then-segment architecturally: comparing error structures of counting via exhaustive instance segmentation vs. direct density estimation on the same backbone, per density regime.
hypothesis: Segmentation-based counting dominates below a density threshold and density estimation above it, with the crossover determined by the backbone's instance-separability depth (linking to individuation capacity), enabling a hybrid switcher with the best of both.
min_experiment: Train both heads on one frozen backbone; evaluate across density-stratified corpora; locate crossovers; validate the switcher.
main_risk: Head capacity differences may confound the paradigm comparison.

one_liner: Study whole-part consistency enforcement: whether requiring part masks to tile their parent object (no gaps/overlaps) at inference improves both part and whole accuracy, testing consistency as a free accuracy source.
hypothesis: Projecting predictions onto the consistency constraint (parts partition whole) improves part accuracy and boundary quality measurably on articulated categories, with gains proportional to the model's baseline inconsistency rate.
min_experiment: Measure baseline part-whole contradictions; apply constrained decoding/projection; evaluate accuracy changes across categories.
main_risk: GT part decompositions vary, making the constraint definition dataset-relative.

one_liner: Investigate relational segmentation ("segment what the person is holding"): whether failures decompose into relation detection vs. relatum segmentation, and whether relations are represented anywhere in frozen VFM features.
hypothesis: Relation information (holding, wearing, supporting) is weakly decodable from frozen features at object-pair level, and most task failures trace to relation detection (not segmentation), implying relation-focused supervision is the binding investment.
min_experiment: Build relation-conditioned benchmarks; decompose errors via oracle-relation and oracle-mask ablations; probe features for relation decodability.
main_risk: Oracle ablations require relation annotations at scale.

one_liner: Test hierarchical granularity coherence across the whole scene: whether a model's implicit scene parse (all masks at all granularities) forms a consistent hierarchy or contains cyclic/contradictory containment relations, defining a scene-level coherence score.
hypothesis: Current models produce containment contradictions (A contains B, B overlaps A's complement) in a substantial fraction of complex scenes, and the coherence score predicts downstream scene-graph task accuracy better than mean mask IoU.
min_experiment: Extract exhaustive multi-granularity masks; compute containment-consistency statistics; correlate coherence with scene-graph task performance.
main_risk: Exhaustive extraction protocols may shape coherence results.

one_liner: Study subitizing vs. counting signatures in VFMs: whether models show the human small-number advantage (exact for 1–4, approximate beyond), locating where numerical representations transition and whether the transition mirrors attention capacity.
hypothesis: Instance-count accuracy shows a sharp exact-to-approximate transition at a model-specific small number that scales with decoder query capacity, paralleling (but not matching) the human subitizing boundary.
min_experiment: Count-controlled scenes from 1–50 instances; measure exactness curves per model; correlate transitions with architectural capacity parameters.
main_risk: Count accuracy confounds with density/occlusion at higher numbers.

one_liner: Investigate object permanence in video segmentation at the representation level: whether occluded-object state is maintained in features during occlusion (decodable position/extent) or reconstructed at reappearance, distinguishing memory from re-detection accounts of SAM2 behavior.
hypothesis: Occluded-object position remains decodable from memory features during short occlusions (maintained state) but decays to chance before behavioral re-acquisition fails — showing behavior outlives representation via re-detection, a hybrid account with testable transition timing.
min_experiment: Probe occluded-object decodability across occlusion durations; align decay curves with behavioral re-acquisition success.
main_risk: Probes may read out scene priors rather than object state.

one_liner: Test material-vs-object segmentation entanglement: prompting on multi-material objects (knife with wooden handle) to characterize whether models default to material or object boundaries, and whether the default is controllable by prompt phrasing or position.
hypothesis: Click position within a material region biases output toward material boundaries while box prompts bias toward object boundaries — an implicit, undocumented prompt-type semantics that users unknowingly invoke.
min_experiment: Curate multi-material object sets with dual GT; measure output type vs. prompt type/position; document the semantics.
main_risk: Material GT boundaries need careful annotation standards.

one_liner: Study collective-entity segmentation: how models handle entities that exist only as collectives (queue of people, flock, pile), testing whether collective concepts have any representational support or degenerate to instance unions.
hypothesis: Prompted with collective nouns, models return either single instances or naive unions, never emergent collective boundaries (e.g., including interstitial space of a pile), demonstrating a missing representational category measurable against human collective-extent judgments.
min_experiment: Collect human collective-extent annotations; compare model outputs under collective prompts; classify output modes.
main_risk: Human collective extents have high variance requiring distribution-level comparison.

one_liner: Investigate cross-instance property transfer in prompting: whether "segment all things like this one" (exemplar generalization within an image) uses abstract property matching or template matching, dissociable by property-vs-appearance-matched distractor design.
hypothesis: Generalization follows appearance-template matching (fails on property-same/appearance-different instances) rather than property abstraction, with the failure structure predictable from feature-space distances — defining current limits of exemplar prompting.
min_experiment: Construct scenes with property/appearance-crossed instance sets; measure generalization patterns; fit both matching accounts.
main_risk: Constructing crossed sets in natural images is hard; may need staged photography.

one_liner: Test constituent tracking through transformations: whether models maintain part identity through object state changes (folded/unfolded, assembled/disassembled), probing identity representations beyond spatial continuity.
hypothesis: Part re-identification across state changes is near chance for current video models even with clean visibility, and contrastive fine-tuning on transformation pairs yields large gains — evidencing a data gap rather than architectural impossibility.
min_experiment: Curate transformation videos with part-identity GT; evaluate re-identification; run the contrastive fine-tuning intervention.
main_risk: Part-identity annotation through transformations is laborious.

one_liner: Study numerical prompt semantics: what "segment 3 apples" should return when 5 exist, and whether models have any consistent cardinality-constrained selection semantics (top-confidence, spatial clustering, or noncompliance).
hypothesis: Models ignore cardinality constraints entirely (returning all or one), and imposing selection semantics requires only a constrained decoding layer over existing hypothesis scores — cardinality competence is a readout, not a representation, problem.
min_experiment: Evaluate cardinality-constrained prompts on count-controlled scenes; classify compliance behavior; test constrained-decoding retrofits.
main_risk: Prompt phrasing may dominate results; needs phrasing marginalization.

one_liner: Investigate boundary sharing consistency: when two adjacent objects are segmented separately, whether their shared boundary coincides (pixel-level agreement) or leaves gaps/overlaps, quantifying pairwise consistency as a distinct model property.
hypothesis: Independently prompted adjacent masks disagree along shared boundaries by measurable margins (systematically biased toward double inclusion of boundary pixels), and joint decoding removes the inconsistency with side benefits to both masks' accuracy.
min_experiment: Prompt adjacent-object pairs independently; measure boundary agreement statistics; compare against joint-decoding variants.
main_risk: GT shared boundaries also have annotation noise, complicating attribution.

one_liner: Test scene-context arithmetic: whether removing an object (inpainting) changes segmentation of unrelated remaining objects, measuring the locality of scene representations and identifying nonlocal entanglement in VFM inference.
hypothesis: Removing one object measurably changes masks of distant unrelated objects in a nontrivial fraction of scenes, with entanglement structured by co-occurrence statistics (contextually related objects entangled most) — quantifying representational nonlocality.
min_experiment: Inpaint objects from scenes; measure mask changes on remaining objects vs. distance/relatedness; map entanglement structure.
main_risk: Inpainting quality contaminates the intervention.

one_liner: Study typed-part transfer: whether part vocabulary learned on one category (vehicle wheels) transfers to novel categories with analogous parts (office-chair wheels), testing compositional part abstraction in segmentation models.
hypothesis: Part segmentation transfers across categories at rates far above chance for functionally defined parts (wheels, handles, legs) but not stylistic parts, evidencing partial compositional abstraction with a functional/stylistic boundary.
min_experiment: Train part heads on source categories; evaluate on analogous parts of held-out categories; classify transfer by part type.
main_risk: Analogous-part correspondence definitions are contestable.

one_liner: Investigate the interaction of counting and ambiguity: propagating granularity ambiguity into count intervals (a "rock pile" count depends on granularity choice) and testing interval-valued counting against point estimates for decision quality.
hypothesis: Granularity-aware count intervals (derived from hypothesis sets) cover true task-relative counts with high reliability where point estimates mislead, improving downstream decisions (inventory, dosing) in measurable ways.
min_experiment: Build granularity-ambiguous counting benchmarks with task-relative GT; compare interval vs. point pipelines on decision-quality metrics.
main_risk: Interval consumers (downstream logic) must be built to evaluate fairly.
