one_liner: Build the failure taxonomy first: an empirically derived, model-agnostic taxonomy of segmentation failure modes (from large-scale clustering of error cases across models), tested for coverage, stability, and transferability as a reporting standard.
hypothesis: Unsupervised clustering of error signatures across many models converges to a stable taxonomy (~15–25 modes) that covers >90% of errors, transfers to unseen models, and predicts which mitigation family fixes each mode.
min_experiment: Collect 50k error cases across 10 models; cluster error signatures; validate coverage/stability on held-out models; test mitigation predictiveness on a subset.
main_risk: Clustering granularity choices shape the taxonomy subjectively.

one_liner: Test failure forecasting from inputs alone: predicting per-image failure probability before running the model (from cheap image statistics + a tiny forecaster), enabling pre-inference routing decisions at near-zero cost.
hypothesis: A forecaster on cheap statistics (resolution, clutter proxies, blur, domain classifier) predicts model failure with AUROC>0.75 — capturing most of post-hoc confidence's routing value at a fraction of the cost.
min_experiment: Train forecasters per model on labeled outcomes; compare routing value against post-hoc confidence at matched infrastructure cost.
main_risk: Forecast ceilings may be low if failures are content-specific.

one_liner: Study the "wrongness visibility" spectrum: classifying model errors by how detectable they are to non-expert users (obvious vs. plausible-but-wrong), and testing whether plausible-wrongness is predictable and reducible by training interventions.
hypothesis: A stable fraction of errors is rated "plausible" by users (undetectable without GT), this fraction varies substantially across models at equal accuracy, and plausibility-weighted training (penalizing confident coherent errors) reduces it measurably.
min_experiment: User-rate error detectability across models; verify inter-model variance at matched accuracy; run the plausibility-penalty training intervention.
main_risk: Detectability ratings depend on user expertise and task framing.

one_liner: Investigate confidence communication contracts: designing and testing model output "contracts" (e.g., "boundary within ±k px at 95%") that downstream engineers can build against, and measuring contract violation rates of current models.
hypothesis: Contract-style outputs (calibrated bounds per mask property) can be constructed post hoc with violation rates <5% in-domain, and contract-checking flags domain shift earlier than accuracy monitoring.
min_experiment: Define property contracts; calibrate on held-out data; measure violation rates in/out of domain; test violation-based shift detection.
main_risk: Contracts tight enough to be useful may be violated too often to be credible.

one_liner: Test disagreement-based regression testing for model updates: whether output diffs on an unlabeled canary corpus predict which capabilities changed between model versions, enabling label-free release qualification.
hypothesis: Structured diff analysis (where and how outputs changed on canaries) localizes capability changes with high agreement to labeled ground truth findings, enabling qualification decisions without new labels.
min_experiment: Compare model version pairs on canaries and labeled suites; measure agreement of diff-based vs. labeled findings; optimize canary composition.
main_risk: Diffs conflate improvements with regressions without labels; needs directional heuristics.

one_liner: Study human-model complementarity zones: mapping where model+human verification adds accuracy over either alone (as a function of case difficulty and model confidence), optimizing reviewer routing by measured complementarity rather than confidence alone.
hypothesis: Complementarity is non-monotone in difficulty: humans add most value in a mid-difficulty band, while model-hard cases are also human-hard — so confidence-based routing over-allocates review to unfixable cases, and complementarity-based routing improves corrected-output quality at equal review budget.
min_experiment: Collect human corrections across difficulty/confidence strata; map complementarity; compare routing policies at fixed budgets.
main_risk: Human performance varies by workforce, limiting map portability.

one_liner: Investigate failure contagion in downstream chains: how a single upstream mask error propagates through multi-stage pipelines (measure→decide→act), identifying amplification vs. attenuation stages and designing propagation-aware error budgets.
hypothesis: Error propagation is strongly stage-dependent (geometric measurement stages amplify boundary errors superlinearly; classification stages attenuate them), enabling propagation-aware budgets that reallocate accuracy requirements across the pipeline at equal end-task quality and lower total cost.
min_experiment: Instrument 3 real pipeline archetypes; inject controlled upstream errors; measure end-task degradation curves per error type; derive budgets.
main_risk: Pipeline archetypes may not generalize across industries.

one_liner: Test the monitoring-signal hierarchy for silent degradation: ranking practical label-free signals (confidence drift, output-statistic drift, disagreement with a shadow model, input-distribution drift) by detection latency and false-alarm cost across realistic degradation scenarios.
hypothesis: Shadow-model disagreement dominates on detection latency for model-side degradations while input-drift signals dominate for world-side changes — a two-axis hierarchy enabling principled monitoring design at known alarm budgets.
min_experiment: Simulate degradation scenario suites (model rot, drift, sensor faults); measure per-signal detection ROC and latency; publish the hierarchy.
main_risk: Scenario realism drives conclusions; needs practitioner-validated scenarios.

one_liner: Study explanation utility for segmentation failures: whether attaching causal explanations to failures ("missed due to backlight") changes user trust and behavior more appropriately than confidence scores, measured by calibrated reliance metrics.
hypothesis: Cause-attributed failure explanations improve appropriate reliance (accepting good masks, rejecting bad ones) over confidence-only displays, but only when explanations are verified-accurate — inaccurate explanations damage reliance below baseline, quantifying the accuracy bar explanations must meet.
min_experiment: User study crossing explanation presence×accuracy on verification tasks; measure reliance appropriateness and downstream decision quality.
main_risk: Constructing verified-accurate explanations requires solving attribution first for the study set.

one_liner: Investigate versioned-behavior pinning: techniques to guarantee that specific certified behaviors (golden-case outputs) survive model updates exactly, and measure the capability cost of pinning growing golden sets.
hypothesis: Constrained update methods (output-matching losses on golden sets) preserve pinned behaviors exactly with capability costs growing measurably but sublinearly in golden-set size up to a practical ceiling — defining the feasible scale of behavioral guarantees.
min_experiment: Fine-tune with golden-set constraints at growing set sizes; measure pin fidelity and general-capability costs; locate the practical ceiling.
main_risk: Exact pinning may be impossible under architecture changes, requiring tolerance definitions.

one_liner: Test the audit-probe suite concept: a small standardized set of diagnostic inputs (synthetic + curated) whose output pattern fingerprints a black-box segmentation model's capability profile, enabling third-party auditing without weights or large-scale evaluation.
hypothesis: A few hundred designed probes predict a model's full capability-battery profile with high fidelity (rank correlation >0.85 per capability), because capabilities constrain responses to designed probes strongly — making compact auditing information-theoretically feasible.
min_experiment: Design probe candidates; fit probe-to-battery predictors across many models; validate on held-out models including API-only ones.
main_risk: Probes may be gamed once public; needs private/rotating variants.

one_liner: Study cost-of-error asymmetry elicitation: methods to extract application-specific error cost functions from domain experts (which errors matter how much), and whether cost-aligned model selection differs materially from accuracy-based selection in practice.
hypothesis: Elicited cost functions across 5 application domains re-rank candidate models materially relative to mIoU ranking in most domains, with cost-aligned selection yielding measurable end-metric improvements in deployment simulations.
min_experiment: Run structured elicitation with domain experts; construct cost-weighted metrics; compare selections and simulate deployment outcomes.
main_risk: Elicited costs may be unstable across experts within a domain.

one_liner: Investigate abstention interface design: how a segmentation system should *say* "I can't do this region" (partial masks with holes vs. explicit unknown-region maps vs. refusal), measured by downstream human-system team performance rather than model metrics.
hypothesis: Explicit unknown-region maps (tri-state masks) outperform silent low-confidence holes and whole-image refusal on team task performance, because they preserve usable partial work while directing human attention — establishing tri-state output as the right interface primitive.
min_experiment: Implement three abstention interfaces; team-performance study on completion tasks with induced model uncertainty; compare throughput/quality.
main_risk: Results may depend on task time pressure and user training.

one_liner: Test long-tail incident mining from deployment logs: whether clustering production near-failures (user corrections, low-confidence spikes) surfaces novel failure modes absent from all public benchmarks, quantifying the benchmark-deployment failure gap.
hypothesis: A substantial fraction (>30%) of production failure clusters have no benchmark counterpart (novel modes: UI overlays, sensor artifacts, adversarial user content), quantifying how much reliability work benchmarks structurally cannot see.
min_experiment: Partner with a deployed annotation tool; mine and cluster incidents; match clusters against benchmark taxonomies; report the unmatched fraction.
main_risk: Requires production data access and careful privacy handling.

one_liner: Study reliability economics end-to-end: constructing the full cost curve of segmentation reliability (model cost + review cost + error cost) across operating points, and testing whether current deployments sit far from cost-optimal points in reconstructable case studies.
hypothesis: Reconstructed cost curves for real case studies show deployments operating far from optimal (typically over-reviewing easy strata and under-reviewing hard ones), with the optimality gap quantifiable and recoverable by joint optimization.
min_experiment: Reconstruct cost structures for 3 case studies; fit cost curves across operating points; compute and validate optimality gaps against recorded outcomes.
main_risk: Cost data access and generalizability across organizations.

one_liner: Test the "one benchmark to break them all" inverse-design method: automatically searching image space (via generative models with realism constraints) for inputs that maximize disagreement across all top segmentation models, characterizing the shared frontier of the field's capability.
hypothesis: Realism-constrained disagreement maximization discovers coherent input families (not noise) where all models fail together, and these families predict future architecture-independent failures better than any single-model analysis.
min_experiment: Optimize latent codes of a generative model for cross-model disagreement under realism constraints; cluster discovered families; validate their difficulty on held-out models.
main_risk: Generative-model bias constrains the searchable input space.

one_liner: Study capability arbitrage between prompting and fine-tuning: for a fixed target task, mapping when prompt engineering alone matches PEFT (and when it cannot), as a function of task distance from pretraining — a decision boundary for the cheapest adequate adaptation.
hypothesis: Prompt-only adaptation matches PEFT within noise for tasks below a measurable representational-distance threshold and falls off a cliff beyond it, giving a cheap pre-test (feature-distance measurement) that predicts the right adaptation tier.
min_experiment: For 20 tasks spanning distances, exhaust prompt-side optimization and compare to PEFT; regress the gap on distance measures; validate the pre-test.
main_risk: "Exhausting" prompt optimization is ill-defined; needs a standardized budget.

one_liner: Investigate the segmentation "Turing test": whether experts can distinguish model masks from human annotations at various quality tiers, using detectability as a model-free quality milestone and identifying the residual tells.
hypothesis: Current top models fail expert indistinguishability specifically on ambiguity-resolution style and boundary micro-conventions (not accuracy), and the identified tells define a concrete residual research agenda.
min_experiment: Expert forced-choice studies on mask provenance across quality tiers; analyze discriminating features via post-hoc interviews and feature analysis.
main_risk: Tells may reflect annotation-tool style rather than intelligence gaps.

one_liner: Test cross-task failure coupling within one VFM: whether an image that causes segmentation failure also elevates failure probability for detection/depth/captioning heads on the same backbone, measuring shared-representation risk concentration.
hypothesis: Per-image failure indicators across heads are substantially correlated (far above content-difficulty baselines), concentrated in backbone-attributable cases — quantifying the systemic-risk cost of representation sharing.
min_experiment: Evaluate multiple heads on shared backbones across corpora; measure failure correlations; decompose into backbone vs. head causes via representation-swap controls.
main_risk: Content difficulty inflates correlations; needs careful baselining.

one_liner: Study annotation instruments as measurement devices: applying metrology principles (calibration standards, traceability, uncertainty budgets) to segmentation ground truth, and testing whether metrology-grade GT changes model rankings.
hypothesis: Metrology-grade annotation (calibrated annotators, reference standards, stated uncertainty) yields GT whose uncertainty budgets overturn a measurable fraction of published model comparisons, establishing the necessity of measurement science for benchmarks.
min_experiment: Develop calibration protocols and reference objects; re-annotate benchmark samples metrologically; propagate uncertainty into model comparisons.
main_risk: Metrology-grade annotation cost limits scale.

one_liner: Test "model paleontology": inferring properties of a black-box model's training data (mask sources, domain mixture, annotation tools) purely from behavioral probes, validated on models with known provenance.
hypothesis: Behavioral probes (style reproduction, convention preferences, fingerprint statistics) recover training-mixture properties of known-provenance models with useful accuracy, enabling third-party provenance auditing of black boxes.
min_experiment: Train models on known mixtures; develop probe batteries; measure mixture-recovery accuracy; test on public models with documented data.
main_risk: Provenance signals may be washed out at scale or by data overlap.

one_liner: Investigate the interaction of image generation and segmentation models sharing training corpora: whether segmentation models are systematically better at segmenting generated images (distribution kinship), creating feedback risks as generated content floods the web.
hypothesis: Segmentation quality on generated images exceeds matched real images (kinship effect), causing confidence-filtered auto-curation to over-select generated content and compounding synthetic drift across generations.
min_experiment: Compare segmentation quality/confidence on matched real-vs-generated pairs; simulate curation loops; measure synthetic-fraction drift.
main_risk: Matching real and generated content fairly is nontrivial.

one_liner: Study attention-free segmentation foundations: whether state-space or convolutional architectures at matched scale reproduce SAM-class promptable behavior, isolating which observed failure modes are attention-specific vs. task-intrinsic.
hypothesis: Matched-scale attention-free models reproduce most aggregate performance but differ characteristically on long-range coherence and prompt-sensitivity failure modes, cleanly splitting the failure taxonomy into architectural and intrinsic parts.
min_experiment: Train matched promptable models (attention vs. SSM/conv) on identical data; run the full failure battery; classify failure modes by architecture dependence.
main_risk: Matched training at meaningful scale is expensive.

one_liner: Test knowledge-decay forecasting for deployed VFMs: modeling how a frozen model's real-world performance will decay over future years (from world-drift statistics), producing "shelf-life certificates" per application domain.
hypothesis: Domain-specific decay rates estimated from historical world-drift (product churn, style change velocity) forecast future performance decay within useful error bars, validated retrospectively on old models evaluated across the intervening years.
min_experiment: Retrospectively evaluate decade-old models on year-stratified data; fit decay models per domain; validate forecasts on held-out years.
main_risk: Historical decay may not extrapolate through structural breaks (new content types).

one_liner: Investigate minimal architectures for the prompt-to-mask function: distilling the entire promptable-segmentation behavior into interpretable-by-construction models (decision-tree/program hybrids over features) to measure how much of SAM's behavior is simple, and where irreducible complexity lives.
hypothesis: A large fraction of SAM's input-output behavior (hypothesized >70% of cases) is reproducible by compact interpretable programs over frozen features, with residual cases concentrating in ambiguity resolution — locating the genuinely complex core of the capability.
min_experiment: Fit interpretable surrogates to SAM behavior at scale; measure coverage-fidelity curves; characterize the non-surrogatable residual.
main_risk: Surrogate coverage may be inflated by easy-case abundance; needs difficulty-stratified reporting.

one_liner: Study open-weight vs. API-model behavioral divergence over time: longitudinally fingerprinting commercial segmentation APIs to detect silent model changes, measuring the rate and character of unannounced behavioral drift users are exposed to.
hypothesis: Longitudinal probing detects unannounced behavioral changes at measurable rates, with changes concentrated in confidence calibration and boundary conventions — quantifying the reproducibility risk of API dependence for scientific and industrial users.
min_experiment: Probe segmentation APIs on fixed suites at regular intervals for months; detect changepoints; characterize what changed.
main_risk: Requires sustained monitoring infrastructure and careful terms-of-service compliance.

one_liner: Test unified failure-cost dashboards as research infrastructure: whether presenting per-model failure taxonomies, tail metrics, and cost-weighted scores in a standardized public artifact changes which models practitioners select, measured by observed selection behavior versus leaderboard defaults.
hypothesis: Practitioners given multi-dimensional failure dashboards select models that outperform leaderboard-default choices on their own downstream tasks in a majority of cases, demonstrating that evaluation-information presentation (not just content) materially affects field outcomes.
min_experiment: Build dashboards for 10 models; run a selection study with practitioners having real downstream tasks; compare outcome quality of dashboard-informed vs. leaderboard-default selections.
main_risk: Study participants may not represent decision-makers in industry settings.
